101. **Member mutability (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* Superseded by design round 2 C1 (HANDOFF §9): members are read-only unless declared `ref this`; no `readonly` member marker; a witness must match `ref this` in both directions (BYN2814); `dyn ref readonly I` permits only members without `ref this` (BYN2813). Was: (D3) Abstract members marked `readonly` are non-mutating; unmarked ones may mutate. A mutating witness for a `readonly` member is BYN2814; `dyn ref readonly I` permits only `readonly` members and non-mutating defaults (BYN2813). The parser accepts `readonly` as an interface member modifier.
102. **L012 C compile (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* L012 compiles generated C standalone with `-Wall -Werror` (OwnershipCheckerTests.cs:364-384 pattern); Toolchain.cs:197 keeps `-w`. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
103. **Primitives (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* Primitives do not conform to user interfaces; BYN2807's help says so. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
104. **Code registration (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* Each code is registered in the task that first raises it, with its diag golden and explain page; `EveryCodeAppearsInAGoldenCase` stays green after every task. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
105. **Associated types (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* Associated types are `type Item;` only, no bounds. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
106. **TypedDump (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* No acceptance criterion relies on TypedDump (it dumps functions and locals only); run/diag goldens or unit tests instead. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
107. **`this` plumbing (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* `this` plumbing: `FunctionSymbol.Owner` stays `StructSymbol?`; a default template has `Interface` set and `Owner = null`; `BoundThis` takes a `TypeSymbol`; the `Binder` derives `ThisType`. Alternative rejected: widening `Owner` to `TypeSymbol` touches every `Owner.` member access in the emitter for no emitted case. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
108. **Instance-time conformance (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* Instance-time conformance: BYN2807 is forwarded at Compilation.cs:851 and checked inside the signature's `Instantiating` call so `_firstPass` dedupes it; generic conformers are checked once on the template and instance witnesses are built in `InstantiateType` by `Decl` twin lookup, defaults cloned with Self→instance. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
109. **`ToDynRef` ownership (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* `ToDynRef` ownership: `Conversions.Implicit` decides from `StructSymbol.Conformances`/`TypeParameterType.Constraints` (no `Compilation`); the lowerer keeps the operand a place (`Lvalue`); RegionAnalysis lends the operand root; a writable target requires a writable source place. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
110. **Vtable emission (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* Vtable emission: slots mirror `Signature`'s `fails` convention (`uint32_t` return, `ret* byn_out` last); thunks through `Helper`, vtables through a separate data list emitted after helper prototypes; `dyn ref readonly I` shares `byn_dyn_<I>`. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
111. **`let` enumerator (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* A `let` enumerator reuses `CheckWritable` through `MutationChecks` with the abstract `moveNext` as callee; no new code. Amended by round-2 C1: `moveNext` is mutating because it declares `ref this`; the error is BYN2104 with round 2's fix-it to `var`.
112. **Member alias (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* `type Item = T;` in a struct body is the existing `TypeAliasDecl` member; `DeclareMembers` treats a member alias whose name matches a base's associated type as the binding, which also makes `Circle.Item` resolvable in instances. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
113. **Interface name as a type (spec 006).** *Decided 2026-10-21 (spec 006 plan):* An interface name used as a plain type (outside a base list, `where` bound or `dyn ref`) is BYN2816; a default template is `IsGeneric` and never lowered; a type-parameter argument satisfies a constraint iff its own constraints include it; vtables and thunks are emitted on first `ToDynRef` use; `IIndexable` wins over `IEnumerator`; keyword bounds (`where T : struct`) stay parse errors. Kept (new in this plan; no earlier answer, not changed by round 2).
114. **`asSpan()` on a `let` List (found in the 006 review, 2026-10-23).** *Open:* `asSpan()` returns a writable `Span<T>` whatever the receiver, so `let k = List<i64>(); k.asSpan()[0] = 5;` compiles and a `let` List can be changed through a span. The spec (§ conversions table, rule on spans) does not say. Conservative option: on a non-writable place `asSpan()` returns `ReadOnlySpan<T>`. Not implemented; waiting for the user.
52. **Token kind names in the Bayan lexer (M22).** *Current choice:* the Bayan dump derives C# `TokenKind` names by upper-casing the first byte of the enum member name; `SelfhostLexerTests` asserts every C# kind name has that form.
45. **Unions (M18).** *Current choice:* `union Shape { Circle(f32 r), Rect(f32 w, f32 h), None }`; variants PascalCase; positional payload fields with names, read only through patterns (`.V(let x, _)`, `.V(var x)`, `Shape.V(...)`, unit `.None`); tag = declaration order; values stored inline; format `Circle(r: 1)` and unit `None`; equality by tag then payload; switches over a union must cover every variant or have a default (BYN2410 names the missing ones); unions in `catch (e) switch` unchanged (error unions deferred); property patterns on payloads deferred. Diagnostics BYN2700–2708. *Round 2 (§1):* cases are camelCase (BYN2009 with a rename fix), payload-free cases may declare `= <integer>` used as the C tag (a case without one takes the previous tag plus one), BYN2709–2711 check the values, and BYN2712 warns on a `_` arm over a union of this package.
46. **Generics (M19).** *Current choice:* `fn f<T>(…)`, `struct Pair<A, B>`, `union Option2<T>`; no constraints, so a `T` value may only be copied, passed, stored, returned, compared with `==`/`!=` and formatted (anything else is BYN2743, member access BYN2744). Inference by unification over arguments only (no target-type inference); explicit `f<i64>(…)` allowed; BYN2740–2742 for inference and arity. Monomorphized in every build mode (spec's debug witness tables deferred), C names mangled `byn_<mod>__f__<key>…`. Rules only a type argument can break (Map key, `==`/`!=`, formatting) are reported at the call or type-reference site; any other instantiation error is an internal error. No generic methods on non-generic structs (rejected as Unsupported); members of generic structs and free generic functions only.
47. **`Map` (M20).** *Superseded by spec 002:* the API is now spec §16's (`map[k]`, `map[k] = v`, `getOr`, `slot`, `remove`, `clear`, `contains`, `length`); the text below is the spec 001 state. *Current choice:* keys are integers, `char`, `bool`, `string`, plain enums (other key types are BYN2760); no indexer; `Map<K,V>()` allocates from `context.allocator` with `List` region rules; members `set`, `get` (`V?`), `containsKey`, `remove` (`bool`), `count`, `clear`; `set`/`remove`/`clear` are structural modifications (BYN3004 while iterating); iteration yields entries `(K key, V value)` in first-insertion order (updates keep position, re-insert after remove appends); formats as `{k: v, …}`; not comparable with `==`; hashing is FNV-1a 64 seeded 0 under `--test`, else time⊕pid; `HashMap` not provided. `set` is a keyword (`error set`) but parses as a member name.
48. **`Owned<T>` and recursive types (M21).** *Current choice:* `Owned(value)` allocates from `context.allocator`; `.value` reads; members auto-deref; a copyable pointer, never null, freed only with its arena; region rules as `List`. No `unique`/`move`. Read-only: no mutation through `.value` or auto-deref (BYN2106). Equality is deep, formatting prints the pointee. Direct by-value recursion in a struct or union is BYN2761, naming the cycle (replaces BYN2113 and BYN2707, now retired); recursion is allowed only through `Owned<…>`, `List<…>` or `Map<…>`. A struct field named `value` behind an `Owned` is reached as `o.value.value`.
49. **Unicode pinning (M22).** *Superseded by spec 002:* both lexers read the same generated tables (`Nfc.cs`/`UnicodeTables.g.cs` and `unicode-tables.byn`), so L001 no longer depends on system ICU. Earlier text: *Current choice:* L1 (lexer equivalence) holds per pinned Unicode version. `selfhost/lexer/unicode-tables.byn` is generated by `tools/Bayan.UnicodeGen` (Unicode 16.0.0, .NET 10.0.12) and regenerates only deliberately; the C# lexer's NFC answer follows system ICU (Q6) and may differ on another machine, which the `nfc` golden and corpus NFC cases then report.
50. **Corpus and timing (M23).** *Current choice:* the corpus generator (xorshift64, fixed seed) and the 10,000 inputs live in `SelfhostLexerTests`; `bayan-lex --many` also checks every span lies inside its input (L2). Timing: median of 5 on a 1 MB file, Bayan ≤ 10× C#, opt-out `BAYAN_SKIP_TIMING=1` (early return; xUnit 2.9.3 has no runtime skip). Measured: Bayan `fast` 6.75 ms vs C# 57 ms (C# side runs in the Debug test build).
51. **Round 3 step 0 (docs): `effect` and `rest` as words.** The plan writes `effect db = net, fs` as a declaration and `rest ReadOnlySpan<T> items` as a parameter modifier, while SPEC §2.4 reserved `effect`. *Current choice:* `effect` moves from the reserved list to a contextual declaration keyword; `rest` is a keyword (a call to a function named `rest` would now be an error, so the SPEC `switch` example calls `relax()`). Revisit if the designer wants `effect` reserved.
52. **Round 3 step 0: existing `toX` members.** Addendum 1 §3 bans instance `toX`/`asX` members (BYN5009 second form), but SPEC already has `n.toHex()` and `toUtf16()`, and `fromUtf8`. *Resolved 2026-10-23 (HANDOFF §27, plan J81–J82):* `toHex` → `string(n, as: .hex)`, `toUtf16()` → the `utf16` view, `fromUtf8` → `try string(bytes)` / `string.tryFrom(bytes)`; old spellings get BYN2230 in step 5.4.
53. **Round 3 step 0: conversion wording.** SPEC §6.2 said "use `from` / `into`" for conversions. *Current choice:* replaced by the `T(x)` conversion rule (Sūq A4), which is what the addendum's table uses.
54. **Round 3 step 0: historical documents keep round-2 fences.** `docs/suq-agent-brief.md` (Sūq-0 goldens written for the round-2 compiler), `docs/bayan-status-for-suq.md` (a status snapshot whose "Implemented" syntax is round 2) and `docs/bayan-terminal-style.md` (rendered compiler output) describe the compiler as it is today, so their code fences are unchanged. Only `bayan fmt` → `bayan format` was applied. *Current choice:* sweep them when the compiler implements the syntax.
55. **Round 3 step 0: commits.** The HANDOFF asks for a commit per document; the run harness commits the whole worktree at the end, so the edits are not split.
56. **Round 3 step 0: GRAMMAR §12 sources.** The plan gives no Arabic source for `until`/`through`, role-noun function fields or the `Untrusted<T>` status. *Current choice:* no source rows were added for them.
115. **Round 3 step 0b: `string.from(bytes)`.** O13 and J82 rename `fromUtf8` to `try string(bytes)` / `string.tryFrom(bytes)`, but the implemented v0.1 form is `string.from(bytes) fails Utf8Error` (Q71), which J82 does not name. *Current choice:* SPEC §3.2, §6.2 and §8 state `try string(bytes)`; the compiler keeps `string.from` until step 5.4, which should rename it under BYN2230 like `fromUtf8`.
116. **Round 3 step 0b: generics in debug builds.** SPEC §11 said debug builds share generic code through witness tables, with `@specialize` / `@shared` per function; HANDOFF §30 and J90 say generics are monomorphized and interface values are the explicit dynamic form. *Current choice:* SPEC §11 states monomorphization in every build mode, and `@specialize` / `@shared` are dropped. Revisit if a debug-build compile-time budget needs shared code.
117. **Round 3 step 0b: the FFI wide-string type.** HANDOFF §27 says nul-terminated UTF-16 follows the same form as `cstr` but gives no type name. *Current choice:* SPEC §18 describes the rule without naming a type; `string16` (§3.2) is unchanged.
118. **Round 3 step 0b: `Handle<T>`.** SPEC §9.6 lists `Pool<T>` + `Handle<T>` as present, while J88 keeps generational handles out of round 3. *Current choice:* §9.6 is kept and gains the typed-index-first rule from HANDOFF §31; handles are added only when the selfhost AST or Sūq shows the need.
119. **Round 3 step 0b: docs ahead of the compiler.** The `onPanic` and `asSpan()` mentions in `docs/diagnostics/BYN2019`, `BYN2612`, `BYN2613`, `BYN2614`, `BYN2786`, `BYN3004` and `BYN3006` now use `Panic.handler`, `span`, `mutableSpan()` and `copy()`, although the compiler's BYN2614 message still names `Panic.onPanic` and the builtins are renamed only in step 5.4; the rest of those pages keep round-2 syntax. The call forms in historical records are renamed too (`docs/bayan-status-for-suq.md`, `docs/suq-0-goldens-report.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `work/todo.md`, `work/status/previous.md`); their code fences stay round 2, as in Q54. *Current choice:* step 5.4 updates the BYN2614 message to match its page.
120. **Pointer type spelling in type-first declarations.** §18 writes `Sqlite3* db`; the friction log F-37/F-63 suggests prefix `*Sqlite3 db` / `out *Sqlite3 db`. *Decided 2026-10-24 (user):* postfix `T*` (`Sqlite3* db`); the prefix forms `*T` and `*mut T` from the old Sūq drafts become input forms. A pointer C must not write through (C `const char*`) is `readonly u8*`. SPEC §18 records it; the parser has no pointer types yet, so the input-form code is allocated when they are parsed (work/todo.md). Revision 0001 (2026-10-24) allocates BYN1066 `PrefixPointerInput` and adds `*const T` → `readonly T*`.
121. **The `using` keyword after `using let` is gone.** SPEC §2.4 (line 108) still lists `using` among the control keywords, and the C#-comparison row (line 2131) still names it. Plan C46 removes `using let` but does not say whether `using` stays reserved. *Current choice:* the keyword list and the row are unchanged.
122. **Round 3 step 5.1b: `let` or `var` in the BYN1043 local fix (J55).** J55 says the fix writes `var` when the local is reassigned, but the parser has no binder. *Current choice:* a syntactic scan of the rest of the enclosing block picks `var` when the name is assigned (`=`, compound assignment, through `.field` or `[i]`), incremented, passed as `ref`/`out`, or declared without a value; a change through a mutating method (`xs.append(…)`) is not seen, so the fix writes `let` and BYN2104's fix then turns it into `var`. Revisit if the fix moves to the binder.
123. **Round 3 step 5.1b: `const T x` and `let T x`.** Neither form is named in the plan. *Current choice:* both are BYN1043 like a bare `T x`, and the fix keeps the written keyword (`const i64 n = 1` → `const n: i64 = 1`), since SPEC writes `const` as a name-first binding.
124. **Round 3 step 5.1b: `except .case` narrowing before case-level error sets.** SPEC §3.14 narrows a `union error` with `except .rejected`, but a function's error sets are whole `union error` declarations, so `fails Retryable` cannot leave a case out of the `fail`, propagation, conformance and exhaustiveness checks without new binder state. *Current choice:* `union error R = A, B except .x, .y` parses (one or more `.case`, after the whole member list) and BYN3202 checks the composition, then BYN2022 rejects the `except` so no program gets a wider set than it declared. Revisit when error sets carry excluded cases.
125. **Round 3 step 5.1b: `type distinct` before step 5.3b.** J5 binds `type distinct X = T` as a nominal wrapper in 5.3b. *Current choice:* 5.1b parses it (`TypeAliasDecl.Distinct`) and the binder rejects it with BYN2022 rather than treating it as a plain alias.
126. **Round 3 step 5.1b: BYN1029 wording.** The plan keeps `error set` under BYN1029 but gives no new message. *Current choice:* any `error set`, and `|` between the members of a `union error` composition, is BYN1029 "an error set is declared `union error {0} = A, B`", with one fix that writes `union error` and `,`.
127. **Round 3 step 5.1b: which `unique` types BYN3209 covers.** SPEC §3.11 says a `unique` type cannot be `const`, but a module `const` of a list is a static array today (BYN2229). *Current choice:* BYN3209 fires when the unique part of the type is a `struct unique` (declared or held by a field), not for `List`, `Map`, `StrBuf` or `Owned`.
128. **Round 3 step 5.1b: receiver forms before typestate.** HANDOFF §2 lists `this is .s`, `ref this is .s`, `move this`, `move this is .s` and `this is .a or .b`; the row scopes 5.1b to `this is .s` (parse only). *Current choice:* `this is .s` and `ref this is .s` parse as the first parameter and set `FunctionDecl.ReceiverState`; the binder ignores the state (the receiver stays read-only or `ref`). A `this is .s` after other parameters is not a receiver and fails as a parameter type; `move this`, `or` states and BYN1061 wait for their steps.
129. **Round 3 step 5.1b: what follows `pattern`.** SPEC §6.5 shows only `pattern T { … }`. *Current choice:* `pattern` is the keyword only when a type name follows on the same line (`pattern` followed by a name is never an expression), then any pattern parses; `pattern .a or .b` without a type stays a name. After `=` in a `const` (module or local) it is a `PatternExpr`, which the binder rejects with BYN2022 until named patterns bind (with `except`); elsewhere BYN1046. A property pattern's designation no longer crosses a line break, so `const p = pattern T { … }` does not swallow the next line's first name.
130. **Round 3 step 5.1c: `requires` rules before step 5.3b.** Rules on fields, structs and `type distinct` now parse (`FieldDecl.Requires`, `StructDecl.Rules`, `TypeAliasDecl.Requires`), but construction-time checking is 5.3b. *Current choice:* `Compilation.CheckRequires` reports BYN2322 on each rule so none is silently unchecked; it is a binder diagnostic, not a parse one, so `bayan format` can still apply BYN1050. 5.3b deletes the check.
131. **Round 3 step 5.1c: classifying a rule by content (O3).** *Current choice:* a rule is struct-level when it has `at .f` or names a field of the same struct as a bare identifier (not after `.`); otherwise it stays on the field above. A rule under a field that uses both `it` and another field (`requires it != password`) moves to the struct with `it` unresolved; 5.3b should give it the field above as `at`, or reject it.
132. **Round 3 step 5.1c: where `because` and attribute arguments go.** *Current choice:* `because "…"` must be on the line of its attribute or call; `@name(args)` takes `(args)` only on its own line, so `@cases` alone followed by a `(`-line is not misread. The parse part of BYN8001 covers `@allow` without a reason and any empty or blank reason; `@json(expose)`, `…Unchecked()` and `unsafe` wait for 5.3a. `unsafe because` is not parsed: no `unsafe` block statement exists yet.
133. **Round 3 step 5.1c: what BYN1048 covers.** *Current choice:* `char` in a type position (including a `(char)x` cast) is BYN1048 and the tree holds `rune`; the char-literal lexer messages (BYN0007-0009) keep "char literal" because the selfhost lexer must match them byte for byte, and `PrimitiveKind.Char` keeps its C# name. `rune` is a type name, not a keyword.
134. **Round 3 step 5.1d: `except` is an expression node.** The plan says `BinaryOp.Except`, but the right side is a pattern, not an expression. *Current choice:* `ExceptExpr` (value, pattern), parsed at the `is` level (J17) and dumped as `(except v p)`.
135. **Round 3 step 5.1d: where BYN1051 applies.** *Current choice:* only `case` labels and `switch` arms report it; `_ except p` gets the fix `not p`, any other left side parses as `left and not p` with no fix. Other pattern positions are not checked.
136. **Round 3 step 5.1d: `allocator` stays.** J11 renames the allocator effect to `alloc`. *Current choice:* `provide allocator: arena { }` keeps the existing name until the effect rename is scheduled.
137. **Round 3 step 5.1d: particles.** *Current choice:* all eight (`from`, `to`, `until`, `through`, `at`, `by`, `for`, `as`) are accepted before a parameter's passing mode and as argument labels (`for:` and `as:`); any other word there is BYN5008 with no fix. `dyn` is never read as a particle.
138. **Round 3 step 5.1d: per-line `state`.** Not implemented; the `states` block of 5.1e replaces it. `become .s` parses into `BecomeStmt` and the binder ignores it. The block landed in 5.1e, with BYN1059 for per-line `state`.
139. **Round 3 step 5.1d: BYN6001 position.** *Current choice:* `noalloc`, `nosuspend` and `suspends` are reported only in signature position (after the parameters and again after `uses`), with a fix that deletes the word.
140. **Round 3 step 5.2b: `style.primitives: .csharp` while the parser still raises BYN1030.** SPEC §3.1 accepts the C# names with no diagnostic, but `Parser.cs` still reports eight of them in type positions as BYN1030, and no plan step retires it (`Parser.cs`, `Keywords.cs` and `TypeResolver.cs` are outside the 5.2b row, as is J70's type printer). *Current choice:* the parser is unchanged; `bayan format` under `.csharp` rewrites the sized names to C# names and does not apply BYN1030's fix, so a `.csharp` project formats cleanly and idempotently but does not build until a step retires BYN1030, reserves the C# names in the lexer and renders types in the project style. *Decided 2026-10-24 (user):* retire BYN1030, since §28 has the compiler accept both spellings with no diagnostic; tombstone like BYN1049 ("retired, the rewrite moved to `bayan format`; never reuse"). Done as a small step after 5.1d. Done.
141. **Round 3 step 5.2b: which tokens `bayan format` respells.** *Current choice:* a primitive name is rewritten wherever it is an identifier not after `.` or `?.` (types, `int(x)`, `int.tryFrom(x)`), since SPEC reserves the C# names everywhere; under `.csharp` a local named `i32` would be renamed too. A boolean operator is rewritten only when the file parses to the same tree and the same diagnostic codes afterwards, so `is not null`, `case 1 or 2` and the `!` of `T!E` stay; `!x` becomes `not x` and `a&&b` gets spaces (`a and b`); `not x` becomes `!x` unless a comment or line break follows `not`.
142. **Round 3 step 5.2b: where `bayan format` finds `style`, and what `--check` prints.** *Current choice:* each file uses the `package.byn` in its directory or the nearest one above it; no manifest means the defaults (`.symbols`, `.sized`); a manifest with errors is reported and its files are left alone (exit 1). `--check` writes nothing, prints `would format <file>` per file that would change, and exits 1 if any would; input forms without a fix are reported as in a normal run.
143. **Round 3 step 5.2a: BYN1062 needs `trustUnchecked()` to bind, which the plan puts in 5.3e.** An input form is an error, so raising BYN1062 on `trust(x, reason: …)` with nothing to bind its canonical form would leave no way to unwrap an `Untrusted<T>`, and the sources could not be converted. *Current choice:* `BinderCalls.cs` binds `x.trustUnchecked()` (no arguments) to the existing `trust` builtin: an `Untrusted<T>` receiver gives `T`, another receiver is the BYN2202 mismatch `trust` gives, and a missing `because` is BYN8001 (the parser already reports an empty one). Any call to a member named `trustUnchecked` with no arguments takes this path. 5.3e keeps the rest of §17 (clean facts, `Untrusted<bool>`, exemptions). BYN2787 is now reached only by `trust(…)` calls that are not `trust(x, reason: …)`, such as `trust(u)`; whether it retires once `trust` is gone is left to 5.3e.
144. **Round 3 step 5.2a: when BYN1062 has a fix.** *Current choice:* BYN1062 is raised only for the shape `trust(x, reason: …)` (a positional value, then `reason:`); its fix is offered only when the reason is a plain string literal, since `because` takes a literal (an interpolated or variable reason is reported with no fix, and `bayan format` lists it). The value goes in parentheses unless it is a name, member access, call, index, literal or parenthesized expression; the rewritten call goes in parentheses unless a closer, a comma or a line break follows it, so `trust(v, reason: "r") + 1` becomes `(v.trustUnchecked() because "r") + 1`.
145. **Round 3 step 5.2a: comments in a one-line union.** *Current choice:* the BYN1053 rewrite keeps a `/* */` comment that sat between cases at the end of the case line it followed (or after `{` for one before the first case); the next pass turns it into `//` (BYN1047).
150. **Round 3 `#line` (J93): which path the directive names.** HANDOFF §30 says `#line N "file.byn"` without saying absolute or relative. *Current choice:* the path panics already print (relative to the package root; a loose file by its name), so the emitted C and the cache key do not depend on where the project lives; the compile directory is recorded as `.` (`-ffile-prefix-map`), so a debugger started in the project root finds the file. An absolute path would work from anywhere but makes the C differ per checkout. Consecutive statements on one line share one directive; a `for` loop's increment maps to its head; code after each function body is reset to `#line N "main.c"`.
151. **Round 3 `#line` (J93): the shape of the internal compiler error.** *Current choice:* BYN4001 (the first backend code) with no location: the head line, then the C compiler's text verbatim (its `main.byn:L:C` locations come from `#line`); under `--diagnostics json` the C text is the `help` field. Exit code stays 4 (toolchain). Failures before the C compiler runs (none found, unknown target, unwritable cache) stay plain toolchain messages.
160. **Round 3 step 5.1e: `extern` is still BYN1016.** BYN1067 allows pointer types only in `extern` declarations, but the `extern` modifier is still rejected (BYN1016), so no pointer is legal anywhere and `bayan format` cannot apply BYN1066's fix (BYN1067 blocks the file). *Current choice (conservative):* `extern` stays rejected, since no step row makes it parse; the parser tracks `extern` so BYN1067 is skipped inside one once it is allowed. Which step accepts `extern` declarations?
161. **Round 3 step 5.1e: where BYN1059's fix puts the `states` block.** J58 says "after the fields". *Current choice:* every `state x` line carries one shared fix: the lines leave their places and the block takes the place of the last line, after any members between them; members after the last `state` line stay after the block. No fix when the struct already has a `states` block, or a `state` line shares its line with other code or a comment. A second `states` block is BYN2006 from the parser.
162. **Round 3 step 5.1e: where the C# names are rejected as names (BYN0012).** *Current choice:* the parser's shared name reader reports a C# primitive name unless it follows `.`, so it covers declarations (types, functions, parameters, fields, locals, loop variables, states, patterns) and also the few name references it reads (module paths, `uses` effects, field initializers), where no such name can exist anyway. A name in a `name: Type` input form (BYN1043) is checked after the fix rewrites it.
163. **Round 3 step 5.1e: which compact format specs BYN1068 knows.** *Current choice:* the six in SPEC §21.5 (`:hex`, `:binary`, `:octal`, `:iso`, `:debug`, `:.N`), parsed as the named spec they stand for; any other compact spec (`:N2`, `:x8`, `:8`) is BYN1001 with no fix. Named specs parse as `name: expr` (`as` allowed as a name) and are not checked until 5.4.
164. **Round 3 step 5.1e: BYN1066 and BYN1067 on one `*`.** Both start at the same offset, and the parser's same-start check kept only the first. *Current choice:* both are reported; BYN1067 bypasses the check (the type parsed in full, so no recovery is needed). A nested `**T` reports BYN1067 once, on the innermost pointer.
165. **Round 3 step 5.1e: no code for a parameter after `rest`.** SPEC §10 allows only named optional parameters after `rest`, and the plan names no code for breaking that. *Current choice:* a positional parameter (no default) or a second `rest` after `rest` is BYN1001 "expected a named optional parameter after `rest`", with no fix. A dedicated code would need a plan change.
166. **Round 3 step 5.1e: `expects` is contextual.** SPEC §2.4 does not list `expects` among the keywords, so it gets no `TokenKind` and stays a name elsewhere (`let expects = 1`). *Current choice:* it is a clause word after a parameter list, like `becomes`, and joins the line before (waṣl) when the next token is a name, `!`, `not` or `this`.
167. **Round 3 step 5.3c: `TypeResolver` does not resolve `RefinedType`.** Step 5.1e parses `T is .a or .b` on parameters, fields, local annotations (`let x: T is .a or .b`) and alias right sides (`type Done = Order is .paid or .shipped`) into the `RefinedType` node, but `src/Bayan.Semantics/TypeResolver.cs` has no case for it, so `ResolveCore` falls to `default` and returns `ErrorType` with no diagnostic. *Needed in 5.3c:* a `RefinedType` case that resolves the inner type and the states (J56, J57), and `TypeResolver.cs` added to 5.3c's file list, which does not name it today. No new `TokenKind` was added, so `selfhost/lexer/tokens.byn` needs no change. *Answered 2026-10-24 (5.3c, first half):* `ResolveCore` resolves `RefinedType`, and `ResolveNamed` resolves `T.s` when the last segment is camelCase and the head is a struct (J56); both give a `StateType`, and an unknown state is BYN7007.
180. **Round 3 step 5.3d: the allocator handler name.** J11 renames the effect to `alloc`. *Current choice:* `provide alloc: arena { }` is the canonical form and `provide allocator: arena { }` is still accepted (Q136), so no source breaks.
181. **Round 3 step 5.3d: which handlers lower.** SPEC §14 lists a handler per effect but v0.1 has only the arena. *Current choice:* only `alloc`/`allocator` lowers; `net`, `fs`, `clock`, `random`, `env`, `process`, `console` and `log` are BYN2022 "the `X` handler"; any other name, and `suspend` (it has no handler), is BYN6007.
182. **Round 3 step 5.3d: which built-ins carry which effect.** *Current choice:* `print`, `Io.stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` and stream writes are `console` (`readAll` also `alloc`); `readFile`, `readText`, `listDir` are `fs` + `alloc`, `writeFile` is `fs`; `run`/`runBatch` are `process` + `alloc`; `monotonicNanos` is `clock`; `List()`, `Owned`, `Arena()`, growing `StrBuf()`, `string.from`/`tryFrom`, `.copy`, `toHex`, `append`/`add`, map inserts and list/map literals are `alloc`, as is interpolation that is not written straight into `print`, `log`, `panic` or `StrBuf.append` (those format on the stack). `log`, `panic` and `todo` are pure.
183. **Round 3 step 5.3d: which effects need a capability.** *Current choice:* only `net`, `fs`, `process` and `env` (BYN6004, reported once per function that calls the built-in, at its `uses` clause or, when it infers, its name; not at each caller); a `package.byn` without `capabilities` bounds nothing, so loose files and old manifests build.
184. **Round 3 step 5.3d: alias scope.** *Current choice:* an `effect` alias resolves only in the module that declares it; a `public effect` is parsed but not yet importable. An alias that reaches itself is BYN6003 at the reference.
185. **Round 3 step 5.3d: `log` levels.** *Current choice:* the built-in `LogLevel` is `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `as:` defaults to `.info`, and every level prints (no filter until `provide log:` lowers). `LogLevel` is not a nameable type in v0.1; only `.member` arguments reach it.
186. **Round 3 step 5.3d: `log` output.** *Current choice:* `byn_log` flushes stdout, then writes `<level>: <text>` and a newline to stderr, with `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and other control bytes escaped (`\u{X}`) so one call is one line. Interpolated text is formatted into a 512-byte stack buffer and truncated beyond it, so `log` never allocates.
187. **Round 3 step 5.3d: getters and constructors infer.** SPEC §14 bounds interface methods, and only a function signature can carry `uses`. *Current choice:* getters (`string name => …`, interface `{ get }`) and constructors infer their effects even when public, and an interface property has no bound (no BYN6005). A call through an abstract getter contributes no effects.
188. **Round 3 step 5.3d: built-in interface members are pure bounds.** *Current choice:* `IIndexable.get` and the other built-in interface methods have no `uses`, so a witness that allocates is BYN6005 (`diag/for-unique-item*.diag`). Open: whether `get` should be `uses alloc`.
189. **Round 3 step 5.3d: what `bayan test -v` shows.** *Current choice:* under `-v` a passing test's captured stdout and stderr are printed indented under its line (each test is its own process, so the capture is per test); without `-v` they are dropped, as before.
200. **Round 3 step 5.3a: the BYN1054 fix.** The plan's help reads `try ({1})`; SPEC §18 writes the narrow form as `(try f()) + g()`. *Current choice:* help and fix wrap the failing call as `(try call)` in place, keeping the rest of the expression outside. `try` now parses down to `??` (`ParseBinary(Prec.Coalesce)`), so `try f() + 1` covers the sum. When a `try` covers several failing calls and is not itself a single failing call, only the first gets BYN1054; the others get BYN2602 as if uncovered.
201. **Round 3 step 5.3a: what BYN8001 checks.** *Current choice:* any call whose callee name (member or bare) ends in `Unchecked` without `because`, in the binder (this replaces the 5.2a check in `BindTrustUnchecked`); `@allow` and `@json(expose)` in the parser, where `@allow` already was. `unsafe` is not checked: there are no `unsafe` blocks to parse yet.
202. **Round 3 step 5.3a: BYN3201's help says `let _ = …`.** SPEC §2.5 and BYN1012's help write the discard as `_ = f()`, but that does not bind today (BYN2001, `_` is not defined). *Current choice:* BYN3201 says `let _ = …`, and sources that dropped a builtin's result (`removeLast`, `remove`, `moveNext`, `Io.run`, `string.from`) now use `let _ =`. Either `_ = …` binds as a discard or the SPEC and BYN1012 change.
203. **Round 3 step 5.3a: the guard of `defer … if c` (J20).** *Current choice:* the condition is evaluated once at registration and spilled to a temporary in the lowerer; the body runs at scope exit if it was true. The same applies to `errdefer`/`defer failing`.
204. **Round 3 step 5.3a: block arms in `switch` (J49).** *Current choice:* a `{ … }` arm is parsed as a block only in a `catch` switch (elsewhere `{` still starts a literal); in a value position the block has type never, and one that can complete normally is BYN2611 at its closing brace, reusing the `catch` block wording. A `return` arm already typed never.
220. **Round 3 step 5.3b: `ValidationError<T>.invalid` without a payload.** SPEC §11 gives `invalid` a `List<Violation<T>>`, but error cases carry no payload yet. *Resolved (revision 0006):* step 5.3h adds error-case payloads and then the violation list; until then a failed check is the payload-less `ValidationError.invalid`, and `ValidationError<T>` is one set for every `T`.
221. **Round 3 step 5.3b: `except .case` narrowing.** `union error R = E except .c` and `fails E except .c` need a set minus some cases, and `ErrorUnionType` held whole sets only. *Current choice:* `ErrorUnionType.Excluded` and `FunctionSymbol.ExcludedErrors` record the cases taken out; an unknown case is BYN2228, excluding every case is BYN2609, `return .c` or a callee's `.c` reaching a function that excludes it is BYN2603, and `catch (E.c)` of an excluded case is BYN2228. `catch switch` exhaustiveness skips excluded cases. An implementation must exclude the same cases as its interface. The `except` BYN2022 from 5.1b is gone (`run/errors-except-narrowing`, `diag/except-narrowing`).
222. **Round 3 step 5.3b: unwrapping a distinct value.** *Current choice:* a distinct type is a struct with one field `value`, so the raw value is `x.value`; `T(raw)` builds and checks one. A conversion back such as `i64(x)` is not built, since the plan does not name it.
223. **Round 3 step 5.3b: constructors of a checked struct.** *Current choice:* a call to a struct's constructor is checked like a literal (it needs `try` or `catch` when the rules are undecided), and the constructor body may assign the fields one at a time (no BYN3208 inside it), since the check runs on the value it returns.
224. **Round 3 step 5.3b: `move` before `with`.** Revision 0007 writes the fix for `let copy = tx with { … }` as `move tx with { … }`, but that parses as moving the whole `with` expression and is BYN2782; only `(move tx) with { … }` compiles. BYN2780's help on a `with` does not suggest `move` at all. *Resolved (revision 0008):* `with` binds looser than every prefix operator, so `move tx with { … }` is `(move tx) with { … }`; `move (tx with { … })` stays BYN2782, and BYN2780's help on a `with` copy is "write `move {0} with { … }` to give up `{0}`" (`run/with-move-unique`, `diag/move-with-parenthesized`, `diag/with-unique-copy`).
225. **Round 3 step 5.3b: `requires` on a generic struct.** Plan §11 (d) says v0.1 checks field and struct-level rules, with no generic exemption. *Current choice:* `requires` on a generic struct is BYN2022 (`Compilation.DeclareCheck`), since the check is declared once per template and an instance's rules would bind against type parameters; such a struct gets no `T.Field`. Open: whether 5.3b should check rules per instance.
226. **Round 3 step 5.3b: `@sealed` misuse helps.** The plan names no help for a misplaced `@sealed` (BYN1016). *Current choice:* "put `@sealed` on a struct" on another declaration, "write `@sealed` with no arguments and no `because`" with arguments or `because`; both start with a verb from `HelpLanguageTests`. *Resolved (revision 0008):* the plan's BYN1016 entry holds both helps as built; `docs/diagnostics/BYN1016.md` carries them.
227. **Round 3 step 5.3b: `try x with { … }` and revision 0008.** 0008 says every prefix operator binds tighter than `with`, but `try` covers the whole expression to its right (SPEC §18, settled), so `try x with { … }` stays `try (x with { … })`: the re-check of the `with` is what can fail. *Resolved (user, 2026-10-24; erratum on revision 0008):* `try` is a scope keyword, not one of 0008's prefix operators, because the `with` re-check on a struct with `requires` can fail and `try` must cover it; `move`, `-`, `!`, `~`, `^` and casts bind tighter than `with`.
240. **Round 3 step 5.5: how `bayan audit` finds bypasses.** The CLI is published with `PublishAot`, so a reflection walk over the syntax records is not trim-safe, and no syntax walker exists. *Current choice:* `Audit.cs` reads tokens: each `because` with the construct before it (`@name(…)`, the called member as `name()`, or `unsafe`) and its literal reason, and each `unsafe` or `extern` not followed by `because`, shown as its declaration head with "no reason given". A file that does not compile is still audited; the exit code is 0. C sources per dependency (SPEC §19.3) are not listed: v0.1 has no dependencies. A syntax walker in `Bayan.Syntax` (owner: whichever step next touches `Nodes.cs`) would let it name full callees.
241. **Round 3 step 5.5: what `bayan features --used` reports (J22).** *Current choice:* JSON `{ version: 1, nodes, builtins, diagnostics }`, each a sorted list, for a build with tests included. `nodes`: the syntax record names of every declaration (nested members, attributes and `because` clauses included) and of the syntax behind every bound node in a function or test body, so a node the binder never reaches is not counted. `builtins`: the C# names of `BuiltinMember` and `BuiltinFunction` (`StringLength`, `Print`). `diagnostics`: the codes the build reported (warnings only; a build with errors exits 1 and prints none). The coverage doc maps them to spec sections by hand.
242. **Round 3 step 5.5: docs outside the row.** SPEC §21.2 still says `bayan format` is "not in v0.1", and its table is split by a paragraph (the `bayan pkg` … `bayan new test X` rows sit after the `--color` text); `docs/bayan-terminal-style.md` §4 has no `bayan audit` section, though `StyleTests` now renders an `audit` shape. *Current choice:* unchanged here (SPEC is frozen, so a draft revision; terminal style belongs to its own doc step). `bayan fmt` uses the existing unknown-command path, whose usage text names `format <path>`; no extra hint line was added (J71). *Closed (revision 0009, accepted 2026-10-24):* SPEC §21.2 fixed, and `bayan fmt` now prints one more line, "the formatter is `bayan format`", after the unknown-command line. The `bayan audit` section in `docs/bayan-terminal-style.md` stays with that document's step.
260. **Round 3 step 5.3e: the particle check's hook is in `Compilation.cs`.** Steps 5.3b and 5.3c own `Compilation.cs`. *Current choice:* one line, `Particles.Check(this, file.Source, fn);`, at the end of `DeclareParameters`; the check itself is in `src/Bayan.Semantics/Particles.cs`. The owning step should confirm or move the call.
261. **Round 3 step 5.3e: where `Untrusted<bool>` converts (J41).** J41 says "usable directly as a condition", but `BindCondition` is in `Binder.cs`, which another step owns. *Current choice:* the conversion is in `Convert` (`BinderExpressions.cs`), so an `Untrusted<bool>` converts to `bool` wherever a `bool` is expected, not only in conditions.
262. **Round 3 step 5.3e: BYN2305 stays for `bool`.** SPEC retires BYN2305 and BYN2307 when particles land, and also says `bool` parameters are still passed by name. *Current choice:* BYN2307 is retired (tombstone page, descriptor `RetiredArgumentsSwapped`); BYN2305 keeps its code for `bool` parameters only, so `show(true)` is still reported. Either SPEC keeps BYN2305 for `bool` or the `bool` rule gets a new code.
263. **Round 3 step 5.3e: the `@positional` exemption cannot be tested.** J39 exempts constructors of `@positional` structs, but `CheckAttributes` in `Compilation.cs` rejects `@positional` as an unknown attribute. *Current choice:* no exemption code and no golden until the attribute exists. *Resolved (revision 0008):* step 5.3g builds `@positional` (the generated constructor and its BYN5004–5006 exemption) and tests the exemption.
264. **Round 3 step 5.3e: exemptions by construction.** J39 exempts `rest` tails, operators, laws and union and state payloads. *Current choice:* `rest`, operators and laws do not exist yet, and payloads are not `FunctionSymbol`s, so none reaches the check; each needs a golden when it lands.
265. **Round 3 step 5.3e: the `trust` builtin lookup stays in `Builtins.cs`.** `Builtins.cs` is owned by 5.3b. *Current choice:* unchanged; `trustUnchecked() because` binds through the existing lookup.
266. **Round 3 step 5.3e: particles in selfhost/lexer and tools/lex-diff where J24 does not decide.** J24 names six meanings; several parameters fit none. *Current choice:* `for` for the value looked up or the item worked on (`inRanges(ranges, for: cp)`, `isDigitOf(digits, for: b)`, `run(cmd, for: path)`, `differs(a, from: b, for: path)`); `as` for the other side of an equality (`sameBytes(a, as: b)`); `to` for a padding width (`hex(value, to: 4)`, `lineNumber(n, to: width)`); `from`/`through` for an inclusive byte range (`isContinuation(bytes, at: pos, from: lo, through: hi)`). Where a second argument fit no particle it was removed for a composition (J24): `appendHex(ref sb, v, digits)` became `sb.append(hex(v, to: digits))`, and `scanDigits` derives the `0x`/`0b` prefix from its `DigitKind` instead of taking it.
267. **Round 3 step 5.3e: BYN2301 and BYN2303 name a parameter by its particle.** *Current choice:* a parameter with a particle is matched and reported by the particle, the label the call writes, so `area(width: 3)` for `area(i64 width, by i64 height)` reads "missing argument `by` for `area`". Open: whether the message should name both (`by` (`height`)).
270. **Round 3 step 5.4a: needs `Compilation.cs`: the manifest's `grammar` in `CompilationOptions`.** Also needs `Compilation.cs` (`CheckAttributes`): `@allow(…) because` and the rename attributes `@json`/`@column` that exempt a name from the BYN51xx lints; none of them is accepted yet. *Current choice:* `Naming` reads `package.byn` from `Compilation.DisplayRoot` itself (cached per compilation), and the attribute exemption is not built.
271. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `Log.<level>(…)` reports BYN5007.** *Resolved (built in Chunk 3b):* `BindCall` reports BYN5007 for `Log.<level>(…)` when `Log` is not declared (no local, type, function, constant or import of that name) and the member is a `LogLevel` member; the label is at `Log.<level>` with no text (the plan gives only its place). The fix `log(text, as: .<level>)` is offered for a single unlabeled argument; other argument shapes get the help without a fix.
272. **Round 3 step 5.4a: BYN5014 has no fix-it.** The fix adds the word to `grammar` in `package.byn`, a file other than the one reported, and `Fix` carries no file. *Current choice:* the help names the three lists; no fix until `Fix` carries a file.
280. **Round 3 step 5.3f: shared syntax files.** `Nodes.cs` and `AstDump.cs` are shared with 5.1e and 5.3h. *Current choice:* 5.3f adds `FailStmt`, and `AssertStmt.Fails` and `VariantPattern.Binding` as init properties, so the existing constructors (and other steps' call sites) are unchanged; `AstDump` prints `Fail …`, `Assert … fails …` and `(variant .x name)`.
281. **Round 3 step 5.3f: BYN1057 in `bayan format`.** `Format.cs` is outside the row's file list and unowned now that 5.1e has landed. *Current choice:* 5.3f adds BYN1057 to `InputForms`, so `bayan format` rewrites `(T)x` to `T(x)`; the corpus, examples and the selfhost lexer were migrated with it. BYN1056 is a binder diagnostic, so `format` (parse only) does not apply its fix.
282. **Round 3 step 5.3f: BYN1056 on a qualified error.** *Current choice:* `return Set.x` is BYN1056 as well as `return .x`; the message names `.x` (the plan's `{0}` is the case), and the fix replaces only `return` with `fail`, keeping `Set.x`.
283. **Round 3 step 5.3f: the `assert … fails` diagram.** *Current choice:* on a mismatch the power-assert output shows the call with one bar and its outcome (`returned 3` or `failed with E.worse`), not the values of the call's arguments.
284. **Round 3 step 5.3f: what a whole-value binding narrows.** *Current choice:* in `.percentOff p`, `p` has the union's type (it prints and passes as the whole value) and only a read of `p.field` on that local sees the case's payload (`BoundUnionField`); a field another case has stays BYN2704 and an unknown one BYN2003. `.none n` on a unit case binds too. Moving a `unique` payload field out of `p` is not supported (reads only); the binding owns or borrows the subject as a `{ } v` designation does.
285. **Round 3 step 5.3f: `char(x)`.** Migrating `diag/char-input` from `(char)0x41` to `char(0x41)` dropped that line's BYN1048: `char` is reported as an input form only in type positions, and as a callee it binds as `rune`. *Current choice:* unchanged here (the BYN1048 site is not in the row); the golden lost one of its three diagnostics.
290. **Round 3 step 5.3c: `become` outside a struct with states.** The plan gives no code for `become .s` in a free function or in a method of a struct without states. *Current choice:* BYN7007 "`{0}` has no state `.{1}`", with `{0}` the owning struct, or the function when there is none.
291. **Round 3 step 5.3c: what BYN7001's `{3}` shows.** The plan does not say how "but it is `{3}`" spells the known type. *Current choice:* the type's display name: `Order` for the plain struct, `Order.draft` for one state, `Order is .paid or .shipped` for several; for `this` it is the state the receiver declares.
292. **Round 3 step 5.3c: state names are case-checked.** States go through the union-case declaration, so `Open` in a `states` block is BYN2009 "must be camelCase" with a rename fix, like a union case (J56 relies on camelCase states). *Current choice:* kept; `diag/positional-states` gains two BYN2009.
293. **Round 3 step 5.3c: a type listing every state.** *Current choice:* `T is .a or .b` that lists all of `T`'s states accepts a plain `T` (Identity), but stays its own type and is not folded into `T`, so a single-state struct's `T.s` literal keeps its state.
294. **Round 3 step 5.3c: the parser builds `T.s { … }`.** Step 5.1e parses `T.s` only as a type, so `Order.paid { … }` was BYN1005. *Current choice:* `ParseNameOrStructLiteral` in `Parser.cs` (outside the row) parses a PascalCase name, `.`, a camelCase name and a struct-literal body on the same line as a `StructLiteralExpr` with the type `T.s`; nothing in `selfhost/` changes.
295. **Round 3 step 5.3c: what a local is known to be.** SPEC §3.17 narrows through `is`, `switch` and a `becomes` call on a `var`, but does not say when the knowledge ends. *Current choice:* a `var` declared or inferred with a state type holds the plain struct, and its state is a fact; a `let` and a parameter keep their state type. A fact is learned in the branch an `is` test proves (and after an `if` whose other branch always exits), in a `switch` arm without a guard, from an assignment of a state-typed value, and after a statement `o.f(…)` or `try o.f(…)` (or `f(…)` on `this`) where `f` takes `ref this` and `becomes .s` (a failing call handled in place teaches nothing, since a failed transition leaves the state unchanged). A fact is dropped by any assignment, by passing the local `out`, by a `becomes` call that is not such a statement, at the entry of a loop for every `var` and `ref` parameter (and for `this` in a `ref this` method), and when its block ends; what a branch learns does not survive the branch. Passing the local or `this` `ref` and calling a `ref this` method without `becomes` keep the fact (revision 0010 item 5: rules A–C keep the callee from changing the state).
296. **Round 3 step 5.3c: BYN7004's fix in a `switch` expression.** The plan says "fix yes" and the help is "add a `case .{0}` arm", but an expression arm needs a value the compiler cannot invent. *Current choice:* a statement `switch` gets the fix (an empty `case .s:` section after the last one, at its indentation); an expression `switch` gets the help without a fix. An optional subject (`Order?`) keeps BYN2410.
297. **Round 3 step 5.3c: `become` without a `this` to change.** No plan code covers `become .s` in a `static` method or in a method that takes neither `ref this` nor `move this`. *Current choice:* in a `static` method, BYN2022 "`become` in a static method is not supported in v0.1" at `become`; in a method with a plain `this`, BYN2115 "`{0}` modifies `this` but is not declared `ref this`" with its `ref this` fix, as for any write to `this`. Since revision 0010, a plain `this` method that declares `becomes` gets BYN7010 at its signature instead, and its `become` reports nothing more.
298. **Round 3 step 5.3c: `becomes` with no receiver (revision 0010).** Revision 0010 makes `becomes` on a free function BYN7010, but BYN7010's message names the receiver it takes, its label sits at the receiver and its fix rewrites it, and a free function or a `static` method has none. *Current choice:* BYN7010 is reported for instance methods only (a written `this`/`move this` receiver, or the name of a method with no receiver written, whose fix inserts `ref this`); a `static` method keeps BYN2022 at its `become` and BYN7009 at a return without one; a free function keeps BYN7007 at its `become` (no struct owns the state) and BYN7009. A revision should say whether a free or `static` `becomes` gets BYN7010 at the clause, and with what `{2}`.
300. **Round 3 step 5.3g: the `expects` trap text (J68).** J68 says a failed `expects` traps with `precondition failed: {expr}`; SPEC §7.9 (frozen) says `contract violated: <text>`, which the compiler already prints. *Current choice:* the SPEC text stays; a revision should pick one.
301. **Round 3 step 5.3g: overlapping particle-set overloads are BYN2006.** BYN3213 is reserved for overloads that differ by type. *Current choice:* a second function or method whose particle set lets one call match both (`shift(x, by:)` beside `shift(y, by:, to: = 0)`) is reported as BYN2006 "declared twice" at the second declaration and dropped; the overlap test compares required particles against shared labels and the ranges of unlabeled arguments.
302. **Round 3 step 5.3g: BYN3214's help names `copy()`.** The plan's help is "copy it first: `{0}.copy()`", but v0.1 `copy` takes its allocator (`xs.copy(to: arena)`; `.copy()` is BYN2301). *Current choice:* the help is the plan's text; the page shows `copy(to: arena)`. The help should change if `copy()` without an allocator does not land with §27.
303. **Round 3 step 5.3g: where BYN5011 points.** The plan labels it at `expects`, but `FunctionDecl.Requires` keeps only the clause. *Current choice:* the binder finds the keyword in the source just before the clause (no parser change); for the `requires` input form it points at the clause.
304. **Round 3 step 5.3g: what `rest` accepts.** *Current choice:* a `rest` parameter whose type is not a span is matched like any other parameter (no diagnostic; the parser only builds span types from the input forms); `..x` spreads only as the whole tail (`f(..xs)`), and mixed with other values (`f(1, ..xs)`) it is an open range, BYN2215; a generic `rest ReadOnlySpan<T>` does not infer `T` from the tail. J64's "a positional argument after the rest tail joins the tail" is read literally: `total(4, by: 10, 5)` passes `[4, 5]`.
305. **Round 3 step 5.3g: BYN3214 lives in `RegionAnalysis.cs`.** That file is not in the row, but the region rules already decide what outlives a call. *Current choice:* a `rest` parameter borrows a region that ends with the call; returning it or storing it through `ref`, `out` or `this` reports BYN3214 instead of BYN3002/BYN3003.
306. **Round 3 step 5.3g: method overloads and conformance.** *Current choice:* a struct may overload a method by particle set and calls pick by labels, but interface conformance (`Conformance.cs`) and member lookups that are not calls still take the first method of the name.
310. **Round 3 step 5.3h: payload binding in `catch switch` arms and `except`.** *Resolved (criteria v2 opened `BinderCalls.cs` for new methods):* two hooks in `BindPattern` send `.case(…)`, `.case name` and `Set.case(…)` on an error-set input to `BindErrorCasePattern` (`BinderErrors.cs`), which binds the subpatterns against the case's `Fields` (BYN2706 with no payload, BYN2703 for a wrong count, BYN2411 for a case outside the set or excluded, BYN2228 for an unknown name) and gives a whole-value binding the set's type with `name.field` reads (`BoundErrorField`, Question 284); a hook in `Collect` counts a case pattern with irrefutable subpatterns toward exhaustiveness. `except` (`fails E except .c`, `union error R = E except .c`) and the `catch (Set.case)` filter take case names only, so payload bindings do not apply there; they work with payload cases unchanged (`run/errors-payload-binding`). A plain `switch` on an error value binds the same way.
311. **Round 3 step 5.3h: the `Result` layout is one struct for the program.** SPEC §3.12 gives an error a tag plus the largest payload. *Current choice:* every error set and union of sets is the C struct `byn_err` (`uint32_t code`, then a union `p` with a struct `e<code>` for each case that has fields), so the largest payload is taken over every case in the program, not per set, and widening a set to a union changes no bits. Failing functions return `byn_err`; built-in failing calls still return the runtime's bare code and are wrapped at the call; `Result<T, E>` keeps the error as `byn_err err`. Payload fields are not dropped or moved: a unique or owned payload value leaks (todo).
312. **Round 3 step 5.3h: where `.case(…)` binds, and labels.** `BindCall` is in `BinderCalls.cs`. *Current choice:* `BindErrorNew` (new `BinderErrors.cs`) runs before `BindCall` in the `BinderExpressions` dispatch for `.case(…)` against an error-set type and for `Set.case(…)`; `fail .case(…)` binds in `BindFail`. Arguments bind as union payloads do (`enforceNames: false`), so `.rejected("x", 1)` binds by position although SPEC §3.12 wants labels with several payload fields; the same holds for unions. A bare `.case` with a payload is BYN2705 wherever it is built: after `fail`, and through `Built` (`BinderErrors.cs`) in `BindConverted` (typed `let`, `return`, fields, elements), an untyped `let` or `const` and a call argument; patterns, `==` and `catch` filters bind the bare case as a test of the code.
313. **Round 3 step 5.3h: needs `TypeResolver.cs`: `ValidationError<T>` per `T`.** *Built in step 5.4b:* `TypeResolver.cs` resolves `ValidationError<T>` of a struct with `requires` to that struct's own set (`Compilation.ValidationErrorOf`), whose `invalid` case carries `List<Violation<T>> violations`; `Violation<T> { T.Field field, Rule rule }` and `Rule` are declared in `Builtins.cs`; the check (`Binder.BindChecks`) fills the list (Question 335). For any other `T` (a distinct type, a struct without `requires`, no argument) the shared payload-less set remains.
314. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `replace(at:by:)`.** *Resolved (built in Chunk 2, gate 2):* list `replace(at: Range<i64>, by: ReadOnlySpan<T>)` replaces the elements in the range (`a..b` or `a..=b`, a literal or a held value) with the items, which may differ in number; a list converts to the span. A range value is stored as its layout tuple (start, end, inclusive; `RangeType.Layout`). Elements that own memory are left out (the items are copied in). `replaceRange(r, items)` is BYN2230 with the fix `replace(at: r, by: items)`; SPEC's old form `replaceRange(r, with:)` does not parse, since `with` is a keyword.
315. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `remove(from:through:)`.** *Resolved (built in Chunk 3b, J24):* list `remove(from: a, through: b)` removes `[a, b]`; `a > b` or `b >= length` panics `slice out of range`, as `remove(from:until:)` does.
316. **Round 3 step 5.4a: list `remove(at:)`.** *Resolved (built in Chunk 3b, J24):* `remove(at: i)` removes one element (`index out of range` when `i` is outside the list) and `remove(at: range)` takes `a..b`, `a..=b` or a held `Range<i64>`. Both return nothing: SPEC §27 lists no result (Question 329).
317. **Round 3 step 5.4a: names of the `trimmed(from:)` and `equals(as:)` enums.** SPEC §16.4 writes only the cases (`.start`/`.end`, `.caseless`). *Current choice:* builtin `enum Edge { start, end }` and `enum Comparison { ordinal, caseless }`, not writable as type names yet (like `Radix`); `ordinal` is the default.
318. **Round 3 step 5.4a: names of the string view types.** SPEC §16.4 calls `runes`, `utf16`, `lines` and `parts` views without naming their types. *Current choice:* they appear in messages as `RuneView`, `Utf16View`, `LineView` and `PartView`; they are walked by `for` and cannot be written as type names. `runes.take(n)` returns the borrowed prefix of the first n runes as a `string` and `utf16.copy()` a `List<u16>`; `runes.skip(n)` and `runes.takeLast(n)` are the borrowed rest and suffix as a `string`; `length` on views is not built.
319. **Round 3 step 5.4a: rune arguments to the search and split members.** SPEC §3.2 writes `parts(by: ',')`. *Current choice:* `parts(by:)` takes a `string` or a `rune` (`parts(by: ',')`); `position`, `lastPosition`, `count` and `replaced` take a `string`, and a rune there is BYN2202, written `","` instead.
320. **Round 3 step 5.4a: empty texts and limits.** SPEC does not say what an empty needle or separator does. *Current choice:* `position("")` is the `from:` position (0 by default) and `lastPosition("")` is `length`; `count("")` is 0; `replaced("", by:)` and `parts(by: "")` panic; `parts(by:, limit: 0)` means no limit and a negative limit panics; `position(x, from: i)` traps when i is outside `0...length`. `lines` splits on `\n` and drops a `\r` before it; a final newline does not start an empty line, and `""` has no lines, while `"".parts(by: ",")` has one empty part.
321. **Round 3 step 5.4a: what `trimmed()` trims.** SPEC §16.4 does not name the characters. *Current choice:* ASCII whitespace (space, `\t`, `\n`, `\r`, `\v`, `\f`), like the ASCII case members; Unicode `White_Space` waits for `std.text`. `trimmed(by: runes)` trims the given runes at both ends.
322. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `mutableSpan()` exclusivity.** SPEC §16 says no other access to `xs` is allowed while a `mutableSpan()` view is live. *Current choice:* the view is a loan like `span`, so writes to `xs` while it is live are the existing borrow errors; reads of `xs` are still allowed.
323. **Round 3 step 5.4a: which side `padded` pads.** SPEC §3.2 and §16.4 write `padded(to: n, by: c)` without a side. *Current choice:* c is appended at the end until the text has n runes (start-aligned, like a string in a `width:` spec); text with n or more runes is copied unchanged. A start or centre form waits for a decision (`width:` with `align:` covers it in a spec).
324. **Round 3 step 5.4a: what `T.tryParse(text, as:)` accepts.** SPEC §6.2 says it takes the same `Radix` as `string(n, as:)`. *Current choice:* integer types only; digits in either letter case, no `+`, prefix, separator or space; `.decimal` (the default) takes a leading `-` on a signed type and checks the range; `.binary`, `.octal` and `.hex` read the type's bits with no sign, so `i8.tryParse("ff", as: .hex)` is -1, the inverse of `string(i8(-1), as: .hex)`. Empty or invalid text gives `null`. `T.parse(text)` fails with `ParseError`, which is 5.4b, so it is not built here.
325. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `toList()` on an array.** J80's rename is `copy()`, but an array has no `copy()` member. *Current choice:* BYN2230's fix for an array is `array.span.copy()`; `copy()` on a list or span takes an optional `to:` like `s.copy()`.
326. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `matches(re)` has no `Regex` type.** *Decided 2026-10-25 (revision 0011):* regexes arrive after v0.1 in `std.regex`, linear-time with no backtracking, and until then `matches` is an unknown member (BYN2003, labelled "`matches` arrives with `std.regex` after v0.1"). SPEC §21 lists `matches(re)` among the string assertions in v0.1 scope, but no `Regex` type exists in the compiler or the stdlib, and no plan step builds one. *Current choice:* `matches` is not built; a call is rejected as an unknown member. Decide whether v0.1 ships a `Regex` type (and in which step) or whether `matches(re)` moves to after v0.1.
327. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `Display.formatInto(ref StrBuf out, as FormatSpec spec)`: the parameter name and `FormatSpec`.** `out` is a keyword, so the SPEC §16.4 signature is BYN1001 and the plan gives no other spelling. *Current choice:* the goldens spell it `formatInto(ref StrBuf output, as FormatSpec spec)` (the lookup matches by types, so any legal name works). `FormatSpec` is a built-in value type a user cannot construct, with read-only fields `radix` (the built-in `Radix`, `.decimal` when the hole gives none), `debug` (`bool`), `width` (`i64`, 0 for none), `fill` (`rune`, `' '` by default), `align` (a built-in `Align` of `.start`/`.end`/`.center`, `.start` by default) and `digits` (`i64`, -1 for none). A struct with the two-parameter form receives the hole's specs and does its own padding (the compiler applies none around it), and `as: <radix>` and `digits:` are accepted on it; outside a hole with specs (`{x}`, `append(x)`, inside an optional) it receives the defaults. A struct with only the one-parameter `formatInto(ref StrBuf b)` keeps working, with the compiler padding around it; if a struct has both, the binder and the emitter use one rule: a hole with any spec calls the two-parameter form with a `FormatSpec` built from the hole's specs (no integer radix or digits formatting is applied to the struct), and a hole without specs (and `append(x)`) calls the one-parameter form. A struct with only the one-parameter form keeps BYN2021 for `as: <radix>` and `digits:`.
328. **Round 3 step 5.4a: format specs in a hole.** The plan names no code for a spec that is wrong. *Current choice:* reused codes: a spec that does not apply to the value's type, or an unknown spec name, is BYN2021 (`` `string` has no parameter `as: .hex` ``); `width` and `digits` must be constants (BYN2219) in 0–1024 and 0–15 (BYN2203); `fill` is a constant `rune`; `align` takes `.start`, `.end`, `.center` (otherwise BYN2720 "… is not a member of `align`"; there is no `Alignment` enum); a repeated spec is BYN2303. `width` counts runes; numbers align to the end by default and everything else to the start (SPEC's `{id, width: 6, fill: '0'}` → `000042`); `digits` rounds half away from zero and keeps the sign of a negative value that rounds to zero (`-0.00`); a radix writes lowercase digits with a leading `-` for negative values; `.debug` quotes strings and runes (escaping the quote, `\` and newline in both: `'\''`, `'\\'`, `'\n'`), shows a struct in its literal form `P { x: 1, name: "a" }` (fields in the debug view, recursively; `P {}` with no fields), with or without a one-parameter `formatInto`, and accepts a struct without `formatInto` when every field formats (otherwise BYN2225 names the field); a struct whose `formatInto` takes the `FormatSpec` gets `debug: true` and formats itself; other types show their plain view. BYN2225's help now suggests `{x, as: .debug}` (SPEC §13) instead of the BYN1068 input form `{x:debug}`, and is dropped under `as: .debug`. A formatted hole is cut before padding at the last code-point boundary at or before 1024 bytes, so the cut never splits a code point. Left out: non-constant spec values (`width: n` with a variable `n` is BYN2219), and lists, spans and arrays under `.debug` (still BYN2225).
329. **Round 3 step 5.4a: what list `remove(at: i)` returns.** SPEC §27 gives `removeFirst()`/`removeLast()` a `T?` result but none for `remove(at:)`. *Current choice:* `remove(at:)` returns nothing.
330. **Round 3 step 5.4a: `StrBuf` members.** *Current choice:* `insert(text, at: i)` takes a byte offset; an offset outside `0…length` panics `slice out of range` and one inside a rune panics `string slice splits a code point`, as a string slice does; `insert` is a structural modification like `clear` (it shifts the bytes a `view` borrows), and text borrowed from the buffer may be inserted into it. `StrBuf(capacity: n)` grows from `context.allocator` with room for `n` bytes (a negative `n` reserves nothing). `append(x)` takes any `Display` value and formats it straight into the buffer, as `append($"{x}")` does. `appendRepeated(c, by: n)` writes the rune `n` times and panics `repeated a negative number of times` for a negative `n`, as `string.repeated` does. `StrBuf.over(span)` is built although SPEC §5 line 262 says it "is not in v0.1" (the step asked for it): it writes into the span and, when outgrown, copies into a fresh block from `context.allocator`; it borrows the span like `StrBuf(span)` and the allocator like `StrBuf()`. SPEC's `stackalloc u8[n] uninit` does not parse (BYN1001 at `uninit`), so the golden passes `stackalloc u8[n]`.
331. **Round 3 step 5.4b: `ParseError` payloads.** SPEC §8 gives `badDigit(Bytes at)` and `overflow`; units are spec-only. *Current choice:* `union error ParseError { badDigit(i64 at), overflow }`, numbered after the user's sets (like `ValidationError`), so user codes still start at 9. `T.parse(text, as:)` on integer types reads as `tryParse` does (Question 324); `at` is the byte offset of the first bad digit, or the text's length when a digit is missing (`""` gives 0, `"-"` gives 1); a bad digit anywhere wins over `overflow`, which is reported only when every digit is good. Float parsers are not built (`f64.tryParse` does not exist either).
332. **Round 3 step 5.4b: the `Utf8Error` payload name.** SPEC §3.2 says the error reports the byte offset but names no field. *Current choice:* `invalidSequence(i64 at)`, the same name as `ParseError.badDigit`. `string.invalidUtf8At` (dropped by revision 0004 item 5, with no rename target in the plan) is kept; L010 cross-checks it against `at`.
333. **Round 3 step 5.4b: `Hex.decode`'s codec error.** SPEC §3.2 says `decode` "fails with a codec error" without naming one. *Current choice:* `List<u8> Hex.decode(string text) fails ParseError`: two digits, either case, per byte; `badDigit(at)` at the first non-hex character, or at the length when the count is odd; `overflow` is never raised.
334. **Round 3 step 5.4b: the lossy `Utf8.decode`.** SPEC names `invalid: .replace` but no type. *Current choice:* `invalid:` takes a built-in `enum Utf8Invalid { replace }` that users cannot name. One U+FFFD per invalid sequence: an invalid lead byte takes the continuation bytes it expects, so `C0 80` and the truncated `E2 82` give one each, and each stray continuation byte gives one (close to, not exactly, the WHATWG maximal-subpart rule).
335. **Round 3 step 5.4b: `ValidationError<T>`'s violation list.** *Built:* the check runs every rule and adds a `Violation<T>` for each broken one, then fails `.invalid(violations)` when the list is not empty (`run/validation-violations`). A field's rules all run; a struct rule reading a field whose own rule broke is skipped (J43, as the compile-time check does). A struct rule's `field` is its `at .field`, else the first field its condition reads (else the first field of the struct). The set of each struct is numbered when first named, after the user's sets. *Left:* decoders (spec-only, plan §11 (d)), so `try T { … }` and `with` are the only paths that fill it; `DecodeError<T>`; `T.rules`; `ValidationError<T>` for a distinct type with `requires` keeps the shared payload-less set (no `T.Field` exists for it).
336. **Round 3 step 5.4b: where the codec renames are reported.** *Current choice:* `string.from`, `string.fromUtf8` and `string.tryFrom` are BYN2230 at the member with a fix that rewrites `string.x` to `Utf8.decode` or `Utf8.tryDecode`; `try string(bytes)` (a byte span under `try`) is BYN2230 at `string` with the fix `Utf8.decode`; `string(bytes)` without `try` is unchanged. `Latin1` is spec-only, so `as: .latin1` gets no rename.
337. **Round 3 step 5.4b: the `Rule` cases built.** SPEC §7.9 lists `length(Range<i64> bounds)`, `range(Range<i64> bounds)`, `pattern(Regex re)`, `required`, `kind(TypeId id)` and `custom(RuleId id)`; J23 recognizes only `range` and `length`. *Current choice:* `union Rule { length(Range<i64> bounds), range(Range<i64> bounds), custom }`: a field rule `it in a..=b` is `range` and `it.runeCount in a..=b` is `length` when both ends are integer constants that fit `i64` (`..<` keeps its exclusive end); everything else, struct rules included, is `custom`, which has no `RuleId` payload. `Regex`, `TypeId` and `RuleId` do not exist, so `pattern`, `required` and `kind` are spec-only. `Range<T>` is not a writable type name and has no readers, so a program can match `.range(let bounds)` but cannot read the ends yet. `Rule` and `Violation<T>` (for a struct with `requires` only) are type names users can write.
338. **Round 3 step 5.4b: the check allocates without `uses alloc`.** The violation list is built from `context.allocator`, but a struct's `requires` check is treated as pure (`EffectAnalysis.IsCheck`), so `try T { … }` in a pure public function stays valid. *Current choice:* pure, like the other built-in failure payloads; the alternative (the check uses `alloc`, so every construction of a checked struct does) would break each pure function that builds one.
339. **Round 3 step 5.4b: a bare `fails ValidationError`.** *Decided 2026-10-25 (revision 0011):* a bare `ValidationError` is BYN2023, instantiations of the set compose and are matched by type, and diagnostics print the type arguments. Each struct with `requires` now fails with its own `ValidationError<T>`, so a bare `ValidationError` (still accepted, the shared payload-less set) no longer covers it (BYN2603, whose help then reads `fails ValidationError, ValidationError` because it prints the set's name). *Current choice:* no new diagnostic; `run/struct-requires`, `run/positional-requires` and `StateLiteralTests` now write `ValidationError<T>` as SPEC §7.9 does. `diag/literal-needs-try` still writes the bare form (its BYN3207 comes first). Open: reject the bare name (BYN2xxx wrong type-argument count), or let it cover every `ValidationError<T>`.
340. **Revision 0011: `ValidationError<T>` for a `T` without `requires`.** The revision removes the shared payload-less set but does not say what `ValidationError<i32>` or `ValidationError<Qty>` (a distinct type, which has no `T.Field`) is. *Current choice:* each such `T` gets its own payload-less set (`Compilation.ValidationErrorOf`), as distinct types need for their checks; `ValidationError<i32>` is accepted and never raised. Open: reject a `T` that has no `requires` (BYN2002 like `Violation<T>`).
341. **Revision 0011: what a type arm binds.** In `catch switch { ValidationError<Signup> e => … }` the binding `e` has the set's type, so `e.violations` is BYN2003; only a case arm (`.invalid e`, one instantiation) reaches the payload. SPEC §3.14 shows the type arm but not its body. *Current choice:* unchanged; a type arm is for telling the instantiations apart. Open: let `e` read the payload when the set has one case.
342. **Review round 3 (A1): a generic that replaces a `ref T` instantiated with a type that has states.** `void put<T>(move T v, to ref T x) { x = move v }` is fine on its template, but with `T = Order` (a struct with states) the assignment changes `x`'s state, which revision 0010 rule C forbids; the instance's BYN7012 used to stop the compiler with an internal error. *Current choice (conservative: reject):* BYN7012 is reported at the call that chose the type arguments (label "the generic code needs this of its type arguments"), with a related span labelled "in `put`" at the assignment when it is in the same file and help naming the generic. A call that would keep the state (the value given is in the place's known state) is still rejected, since the template cannot see states. *Open:* accept such instantiations when the argument is provably in the same state, or a constraint that excludes types with states.
343. **Review rv11: how a message tells apart two sets that display alike.** `ValidationError<a.Point>` and `ValidationError<b.Point>` both display as `ValidationError<Point>`. *Current choice:* where two sets a message names would render identically (the sets of one error union, a `fails` clause plus the set it lacks, the sets a BYN2228 help lists), every declared type in the type argument is qualified with its module (`ValidationError<a.Point>`, `ValidationError<List<a.Point>>`; `ErrorSetSymbol.DisplayNameAmong`), and a set without a type argument is qualified itself (`a.Err` beside `b.Err`); a set with no look-alike keeps the short form. Exhaustiveness and error-union equality key sets by symbol identity, not display text.
344. **Re-review rr6: `==` on an error set whose case holds a payload with no equality.** `union error ListError { bad(List<i64> items) }` has a case that cannot be compared, so comparing two `ListError` values cannot compare their payloads. *Current choice (conservative: reject):* `==` and `!=` on such a set (or an error union or `Result<T, E>` that includes it) is BYN2208, the diagnostic for any type without equality; `==` against a bare case (`l == .bad`) still compares the code (Question 312). Other sets compare as before; the C helper leaves such cases out. Open: compare the code only, or compare the comparable cases.
345. **Function value representation (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q114):* A function value is a (code pointer, environment pointer) pair; a non-capturing lambda and a named function carry a null environment; a capturing lambda's environment is a tuple of its captures living in the creating frame; `FunctionType.IsBorrow` is true so the existing region rules keep the value inside that frame. `Panic.onPanic` keeps its named-function path and codes. Kept.
346. **Function type placement (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q115):* Function types may be parameter types, `type` alias targets and local types; a field, return type, type argument, optional, span, list, map, array or tuple element of a function type is BYN2822 (SPEC §3.16's stored `(Line -> Money uses net) pricer` included). Kept.
347. **Captures (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q116):* A lambda reads outer locals whose `IsMutable` is false (`let`, `const`, `for`, pattern and `catch` bindings) and parameters without a modifier, by copy, seen as `let`; anything mutable, any `ref`/`out`/`in` parameter and `this` (explicit or implicit) is BYN2821. SPEC §3.16's borrowed captures are the later monomorphized-inline model. Kept.
348. **`it` (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q117):* An argument that mentions `it` outside a nested explicit lambda, where a one-parameter function type is expected, is a lambda with parameter `it`; a second one inside it is BYN2029; `it` elsewhere is BYN2001; a user local named `it` is still allowed but cannot be passed bare to such a parameter (write a lambda with a named parameter). `@` as a shorthand is rejected by round 3. Kept.
349. **Lambda parameters (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q118):* Lambda parameters are names only; types (SPEC §3.16's `Token t => …`), modifiers, particles and defaults are parse errors in 007 (BYN1001, Q363); arity mismatch is BYN2820; no expected function type is BYN2218. Amended (round 3: type-first spelling, particles).
350. **Inference from lambda arguments (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q119):* Lambda and `it` arguments are bound after type arguments are inferred from the other arguments and never contribute; a type parameter only they could fix is BYN2740. A function-typed *value* argument (a named function or a local) does unify its parameter and return types. Kept.
351. **`fails` on function types (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q120):* Parsed, typed and callable; a call through a failing value needs `try`/`catch` (BYN2602 otherwise); the lambda body is checked against the type's error sets as a named function would be; conversion requires equal error sets (a non-failing function is not a value of a failing type); error sets display with their type arguments and a bare `ValidationError` is BYN2023 (revision 0011). Amended (codes realigned, revision 0011).
352. **Function type grammar corners (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q121):* `->` in a type is right-associative; `?` and `[N]` bind tighter than `->`; an optional of a function type needs an alias (`type F = …` then `F? g` is still BYN2822 in 007); `=>` in a parameter type, alias target, local annotation or type argument is BYN1055 with a fix to `->`, and after a function's parameter list or a field's name it starts an expression body; a function type's `fails`/`uses` list in a parameter list ends at the closing parenthesis of the parenthesized type, and elsewhere takes one name unless parenthesised.
