Amended (round 3: `->`; J54: type-first parameters).
353. **No generic aliases (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q122):* Aliases have no type parameters (`ParseTypeAlias` takes none); `type Predicate<T> = T -> bool` from spec §3.16 waits for generic aliases. Kept.
354. **Named functions as values (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q123):* Module-level non-generic functions only, including those with particle-labelled parameters (round 3 §15: particles are part of the name, not of the type); a builtin, generic function, static or instance method, constructor (including a `@positional` one, revision 0008) or variant is BYN2824 with a wrap-in-a-lambda help. Kept; corners in Q364.
355. **BYN1028 and BYN1055 (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q124):* BYN1028 `DelegateDecl` was registered and raised with a `=>` text and no fix; 007 T1 rewrote its message, help and page to `->` and added the fix. BYN1055 `FatArrowFunctionType` is registered and raised by 007 T1. `bayan format` applies both fixes. One code, one text each. Amended (BYN1028 already raised; revision 0009).
356. **`.member` is not a lambda (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q125):* `.member` where a function type is expected is BYN2823 with a fix to `it.member`. Kept.
357. **Lambda bodies (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q126):* Expression or block; `return`, `break`, `continue` and `defer` are the lambda's own; a non-`void` expression body for a `void` return is BYN3201; `move () => …` goes through the existing "a fresh value needs no `move`" path (BYN2782). `dyn (A -> B)` was to get a 007 "not supported" diagnostic; as built it is the generic BYN1001 at `(` (006 parses `dyn` only before a name). Amended (round 3 §3 unused value; `dyn (A -> B)` stays BYN1001).
358. **No built-in lambda methods; codes (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q127):* Built-in collection methods that take a lambda stay out of v0.1 (spec §16); 007 ships function-typed parameters on user functions only. Codes BYN2820–2824; 2825–2829 spare; 2817–2819 unused (006 ended at BYN2816). Kept.
359. **Effects on function-typed locals (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q128):* Round 3 §13 makes parameters effect-polymorphic (a function taking a closure inherits its effects) and stored types an upper bound, and does not say which rule a local follows. A function-typed local takes the stored rule: its type's `uses` is an upper bound at the conversion (BYN6005 beyond it) and a call through the local has those effects. Conservative: a bound can later be relaxed to inference from the initializer without breaking programs. Effect variables stay Deferred (round 3). New; a bounded local passed to an unbounded parameter is Q368.
360. **Particles and function values (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q129):* A function-typed parameter takes a particle like any other non-object parameter (007's examples use `by`, "means"); function types carry no particles and calls through a value are positional, so a particle-labelled argument there is the missing-parameter diagnostic; a function whose parameters carry particles is a function value whose particles are dropped from its type (Q354). New.
361. **`it` inside `requires` (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q130):* In a `requires` rule (round 3 §11) `it` is the checked value, so an `it` shorthand in an argument there is BYN2029; write a lambda with a named parameter. As built, an explicit lambda there that reads the checked `it` is BYN2821 (it is read through `this`). Conservative: the ambiguous form is rejected, not given a meaning. New.
362. **Effects lowering (spec 007).** *Decided 2026-10-22 (spec 007 plan, was Q131):* `provide` lowers to a context slot set and restored around its body (`Lowerer.Provide`), not to hidden handler parameters, so a `uses` function value has the same C calling convention as any other; 007 adds no convention of its own. Amended (round-3 step 5.3d settled it).
363. **007 T1: parser corners the plan did not settle.** (a) `ParsePattern` does reach `ParsePrimary` for a bare name, so `case Foo => …` would parse as a lambda; *current choice:* a `_noLambda` flag turns lambdas off in patterns, switch-arm guards and `expects`, and back on inside call arguments. (b) A typed, modified or particle-labelled lambda parameter (`(i32 x) => …`, `(by x) => …`) is BYN1001 "expected a lambda parameter name"; no dedicated code. (c) A generic `delegate` gets the BYN1028 message but no fix (no generic aliases, Q353). (d) A function-typed parameter written without parentheses (`bool any(Token -> bool p)`) parses with no diagnostic; J54 spells it parenthesized. *Current choice:* accepted, since the unparenthesized form is unambiguous in a parameter list; a BYN1043-style input-form fix can be added later without breaking programs. New.
364. **007 T4: named functions as values, corners R3/R4 leave open.** (a) A function declared `fails` without a list has its sets inferred after binding, so at the conversion they are unknown. *Current choice (conservative: reject):* it is not a value of any function type (BYN2202, its signature shown with a bare `fails`); declare the sets to pass it. (b) A function with a `ref`, `out`, `move` or `in` parameter, or whose `fails` clause takes cases out (`except .c`), has no function type to match; BYN2202. (c) Of overloads (J65) the first whose signature matches the type is the value. (d) BYN2824's "constructor" covers a struct `S(…)` builds (a constructor, a distinct type, `@positional`); any other struct named as a value stays BYN2019. (e) The BYN2824 help's lambda takes as many parameters as the function type passes, named after the callee's, so a built-in's defaulted tail is left out (`text => print(text)`). New.
365. **007 T5: lambda names in BYN6005 and the typed dump.** A lambda is lifted as `<enclosing>$lambda<N>` (numbered per enclosing function in binding order), and BYN6005 on a lambda stored in a function-typed local names it that way ("`stored$lambda1` uses `console`, beyond the bound `pure` declared by `i64 -> void`"). *Current choice (conservative: keep):* the lifted name is shown as is, since it is also the name in `bayan types`; a message that says "this lambda" instead would need a second message form. New.
366. **007 T5: typed-dump version for `captures`.** Lambdas in `functions[]` gain a `captures` array (`name`, `type`, in first-use order); other functions do not have the field. *Current choice (conservative: keep version 1):* the field is additive and only appears on lambdas, which no earlier dump contained, so no existing reader sees a change. New.
367. **007 T6: where a lambda value's lifetime ends, and the done-when items the earlier tasks already settled.** (a) A lambda with captures borrows its environment, which lives in the creating frame and is reused by each iteration of the loop that creates it (plan risk *Environment temp per evaluation*, Q345); the captures' own borrows alone cannot catch a lambda capturing only `i` held into the next iteration, or a lambda returned from a lambda. *Current choice (conservative):* `RegionAnalysis` gives a capturing lambda a region named "the lambda on line N" at the innermost loop's iteration depth, or the function body outside a loop, so it may be held by any local in its iteration or frame (also from an inner block, as a borrow-free local) but kept into the next iteration is BYN3002 and returned (a lambda returning a capturing lambda) is BYN3003; a non-capturing lambda borrows nothing. (b) The T6 line asks for BYN3004 when the buffer a captured `string` borrows is *appended* to; `append` is not a structural change (Q30, Q43: a grown `StrBuf` leaves earlier text valid), so for any borrow, lambda or not, it is accepted; the golden appends (accepted) and then `clear()`s (BYN3004 naming the buffer). (c) A function value stored in a struct field (BYN3001) or returned from a named function (BYN3003) cannot be written: the field or return type is already BYN2822 (Q346, `function-type-placement`), so BYN3003 is shown for a lambda returning a lambda and BYN3001 has no golden. (d) A captured `unique` value's BYN2780 help offers only copying what the lambda needs into `let` values, with no fix: `move` and `.copy(to:)` would leave a unique local that is captured the same way. New.
368. **007 T8: a function-typed value with a `uses` bound passed to a parameter without one.** `let fixed: string -> string fails LexError uses alloc = …` passed to a `(string -> string fails LexError)` parameter is BYN2202, since function types match exactly (R3); R16's effect-polymorphic parameter speaks of "a function or lambda" and does not say whether a function-typed local counts. Built meanwhile (conservative): exact match, so BYN2202; the R15 program passes the lambda directly. Open: should a parameter without `uses` accept any value whose `uses` it then forwards to the caller, as it does for a lambda?
369. **007 T11: the "capture by pointer" mutation in L014's done-when is an equivalent mutant.** Locals live for the whole C function; a captured `let` is never written after it is set; capturing lambdas only exist as arguments consumed during the call; Q367 keeps a lambda value inside its loop iteration. Built meanwhile: the proof records the mutation and why it survives, and two mutations that do fail it. Open: whether a later escaping-closure spec owes a proof that does catch it.
370. **007 T11: L014's "nested `let` shadow" scenario cannot be written.** Spec 007 L014 and the T11 line ask that an accepted capture still print its creation value after "a later `let` shadow in a nested scope", but a `let` in a nested scope that hides an outer local is BYN2007 (Bayan does not let a local hide another one), so no accepted program has that shape. *Current choice (conservative: keep BYN2007, test the nearest legal shapes):* `tests/cases/run/lambda-capture-by-copy.byn` redeclares the captured name in the same scope after the lambda is created, with another type (the same type is warning BYN2028), and declares the name again in a sibling nested block after the source's scope has ended; `L014CaptureByCopyTests` checks both. The designer should either reword L014 to these shapes or say whether nested shadowing should become legal. New.
371. **`HashMap` or `Map` (spec 008).** 008 extends `Map` (new key types, `Symbol`) and does not add `HashMap`. *Current choice (conservative):* `HashMap<K, V>` is BYN2830 with a fix to `Map<K, V>`, wherever a type is written, and then resolves as `Map<K, V>` so it is reported once; `bayan format` does not apply the fix (a checker diagnostic). One map with deterministic iteration serves self-hosting (stage 2 and 3 byte-identical, L009); an unordered `HashMap` can be added later without breaking any program, while removing one could not. *Open:* whether v0.1 or a later version adds an unordered `HashMap` (SPEC §3.5 had one).
372. **Symbol identity (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* one table per program run; IDs are not observable (no `id` member, no casts), so their values can change between versions; literal IDs are the indexes of the literal table sorted by UTF-8 bytes with `""` first. Conservative: nothing can depend on an ID. Kept.
373. **Interned storage (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* allocated from the runtime's general allocator, never from `context.allocator`, not tracked by the debug ownership checker and never freed; `Symbol.intern` is `uses alloc` and restricted in a panic handler (BYN2612). Conservative: a symbol is valid everywhere and forever, so it needs no region rule; freeing can be added with an explicit table type later. Kept.
374. **Symbol semantics (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* `==` by ID, ordering by text (SPEC §3.3), default the symbol of `""`. Conservative: matches the spec; the default lets `slot` and defaultable structs hold symbols. Kept.
375. **Symbol conversions (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* only a non-interpolated string literal converts to `Symbol` implicitly; any other `string` is BYN2832 with a fix to `Symbol.intern(…)`; `Symbol` to `string` is `sym.text`, never implicit. Conservative: interning, which allocates, is always visible. Kept.
376. **`Map` key types (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* a closed structural set: integer types, `rune`, `bool`, `string`, plain enums, `Symbol`, and tuples and structs (not `@noEquality`) of those; BYN2831 names the part that rules a composite out, BYN2760 the rest. No user hashing or equality interface on spec 006, no `@equality(by:)` keys, no float keys (spec §17's `totalOrder` hashing waits). Conservative: every accepted key has one obvious equality; an interface-based key can be added later without changing these. Kept.
377. **Composite key hashing (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* field by field in declaration order, combined into the seeded FNV-1a state (`byn_hash_mix`), never over raw struct bytes; `Symbol` hashes its ID. Conservative: correct for padding without layout assumptions; a faster hash is an internal change. Kept.
378. **`Set<T>` (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* stays out of v0.1 (SPEC §16); the port writes `Map<T, bool>`. Conservative: no new collection in a spec about keys. Kept.
379. **`const` arrays of `Symbol` (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* not in 008 (BYN2229 as today); keyword tables are map literals built at start-up. Conservative: static data stays the kinds spec 004 allows. Kept.
380. **Symbol table and threads (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* the symbol table is single-threaded; SPEC §13 revisits it when threads land. Conservative: v0.1 has no threads. Kept.
381. **`Map` lookup members (spec 008).** *Decided 2026-10-25 (spec 008):* round-3 step 5.4 shipped `map.tryGet(at: k) ?? fallback` in place of `getOr` (J24, SPEC §16); 008 adds no lookup member, the existing ones work unchanged on the new key types. Conservative: 008 does not reopen a round-3 decision. Kept.
390. **008 T3: `@noEquality` is not implemented, and where a composite key is checked.** (a) R5 excludes a `@noEquality` struct from `Map` keys, but the compiler does not know the attribute: `@noEquality` is still BYN2770 and `==` on such a struct still binds. *Current choice (conservative):* `MapType.IsValidKey` already rejects a struct whose declaration carries `@noEquality` (alone BYN2760, as a field of a key BYN2831), so `diag/map-key-part` shows BYN2770 and the key diagnostic together; making the attribute known and removing `==` is left to the spec that builds §6.7's opt-out. (b) BYN2831 names the first disqualifying part at the top level only (`field `handle` is a `Handle``, not the field inside `Handle`), and an unnamed tuple element by its 1-based position. (c) A struct or tuple key resolved before every struct's fields are declared (a field `Map<Later, i32>` naming a struct declared later) is checked once they are, and its type stays `Map` meanwhile. (d) `Map<Weight, i32>` cannot be written outside generic code without BYN2831 at that spot, so the R9 criterion's `largest<K, V>(Map<K, V> m)` is reached through a generic caller `heaviest<K>(K key)` that builds a `Map<K, i32>`; BYN2831 is reported at the `heaviest(…)` call. New.
415. **008 T10: the padding case of L016 cannot be made to fail on this toolchain.** T10's done-when asks that a mutation back to `byn_hash_bytes(&k, sizeof k)` make the padding case fail. On zig cc and Apple clang (macOS arm64), no Bayan program I could write gives two `==` keys different padding bytes, in debug or safe mode. The reasons: compound literals zero their padding, small fields are masked in registers, every local starts as `= {0}`, and struct copies move every byte. Stack smearing, separate frames, field-by-field writes, `i8` narrowed from wide registers, list and map storage and `-ftrivial-auto-var-init=pattern` all keep the padding equal. *Current choice (conservative):* L016 keeps the padding rows (`PaddedKeysBuiltApartAreOneEntry`) as a guard for other compilers, and the mutation is killed through `string` parts (raw bytes hash the pointer). The proof notes say the padding half holds by construction, not by a failing mutation.
430. **009 T1: the CLI has no package root, so the self-hosted parser is built through the API.** `import lexer` in `selfhost/parser/` resolves to `<package root>/lexer`, and `bayan build <dir>` (`Compilation.FromPath`) uses the built directory itself as the package root, so `bayan build selfhost/parser` cannot find the lexer. *Current choice (conservative):* `SelfhostParserTests` loads `selfhost/parser/*.byn` and calls `Compilation.Create(sources, packageRoot: selfhost/)`, then `CliApp.EmitC` and `Toolchain.Build` in fast mode, with no new CLI flag. *Open:* whether `bayan build` gains a package-root option or looks for one upward (a `package.byn`), which T13's `bayan-parse` instructions would then use. New.
431. **009 T1: what the parser needed from the lexer, and the friction met.** (a) Made `public`: `TokenKind`, `isKeyword`, `isStringLiteral`, `kindText`; `Token`, all six of its fields and `end`, `hasDoc`, `hasTriviaBefore`, `hasNewlineBefore`; `Keywords` and `Keywords.build`; `sameBytes`; `TextSpan`, `start`, `length`, `end`, `fromBounds`; `SourceText`, `path`, `bytes`, `length`, `create`, `getLineIndex`, `getLineSpan`, `getLinePosition`, `getText`; `Diagnostic` and all eight of its fields; `renderAll`, `sourceOrder`; `lex`, `LexResult` and its three fields; `escape`. Each public function that allocates gained `uses alloc` (a public function is checked against the effects it declares); no body changed. (b) A struct literal cannot name its type through a module (`lexer.TextSpan { … }` is BYN1001), so `parser.byn` declares `type TextSpan = lexer.TextSpan` and the like for the seven lexer types. (c) The particle rule (BYN5004/BYN5006) rejects the plan's free-function shape `report(ref Parser p, code, span, …)`: `p` is the object, so every other required parameter needs a particle. *Current choice (conservative):* the cursor, `report`, `reportFix`, `describe`, `expect` and `errorCount` are `ref this` methods of `Parser` (the lexer's `report` shape: `p.report(.expected, at: span, arg0: …)`); free parsing functions keep `ref Parser p` as the object and label the rest (`parseDeclaration(ref p, topLevel, for: name)`, `dump(ref unit, from: ref p, to: ref sb)`, `recoverIfNeeded(ref p, from: before)`, `checkSpans(ref unit, until: length, to: ref sb)`). (d) A tuple default is not a constant (BYN2219), so `report` takes `arg0`/`arg1`/`arg2` strings defaulting to `""` in place of the plan's `by (…) args`; `format` still takes the tuple. (e) An unused result is BYN3201, so the C# statement calls `Report(…)`, `Advance()` and `RemoveAt` become `let _ = …`. (f) The build has three BYN5014 warnings, for `lambda`, `extern` and `condition` in the flag names kept from C# (`noLambda`, `inExtern`, `conditionStart` and their `set…` helpers); there is no `package.byn` under `selfhost/` to declare them in, and a warning never blocks. No diagnostic came from the lexer's `main.byn`, so there is no Q432. New.
433. **009 T1: the plan's code count and the smoke text.** (a) `DiagnosticCodes.cs` defines 69 parser codes, not 65: 60 `BYN1…` (retired ones included, `postfixOnNewLine` among them) and 9 the parser reports outside that range (`reservedKeyword`, `duplicateDeclaration`, `refThisNotFirst`, `requiresMixesFields`, `unknownParticle`, `noallocRemoved`, `contextBlockInput`, `singleStateInline`, `missingBecause`). `codes.byn` holds all 69 in file order. (Spec 013 T2 adds BYN1069 `statementAttribute`: now 70 codes, 61 `BYN1…`.) Two templates use `{2}` and three use `{{`/`}}`, which the three-argument `format` covers. (b) The T1 done-when expects `CompilationUnit\n\n` for an empty file, but `AstDump.Dump` (and so `bayan parse --ast`) prints `CompilationUnit\n` when there are no diagnostics. The smoke test asserts the C# text and compares it with `AstDump.Dump` directly. (c) Additions to the plan's interface: `peek(n)` returns a `TokenKind` and `peekToken(n)` a `Token` (C# `Peek`/`PeekToken`); `textOf` is C# `Text` as a `string` and `text` returns the bytes; `spanOf(token)` is C# `Token.Span`; `count` and `conditionStart` are fields. New.
435. **009 T2: the tree shapes that shipped.** Every shape in the plan compiled and ran, so the index-arena fallback is not used. Proven by `SelfhostParserTests.NodeShapesBuildAndReadBack` (`FunctionDecl` → `BlockStmt` → `BinaryExpr` of two `LiteralExpr`, under `provide allocator: arena`, read back through `.value`): the five tree unions of `Owned<…>` variants plus `none` (and `InterpolationPart`, without `none`); `List<Stmt>` and `List<Decl>` of those unions; a union child set to `.none`; struct field defaults `List<T>()`, `.none`, `null` and `false`, so a C# `{ get; init; } = []` property may be left out of a struct literal. A scratch program also ran `TextSpan?`, `string?`, an optional struct (`FailsClause?`) and `List<…>?` as fields. Not tried: `Owned<T>?` (the `none` variants make it unnecessary). New.
436. **009 T2: a node union is unique and an `Owned` payload is read-only.** (a) A union whose payload struct holds a `List` is unique, so passing or binding a child by value is BYN2780 (implicit copy); build children into locals and `move` them into the parent. (b) `.value` of an `Owned` cannot be passed `ref` (BYN2106 "an `Owned` value is read-only"), so a child cannot be mutated once wrapped: a parser sets every field (including the init-only ones) before `Owned(…)`. (c) A reader takes the node `in` (`string exprText(in Expr e)`, called as `exprText(in n.value.left)`), which builds and runs. The T1 stubs `dumpExpr(ref Expr e, …)`, `dumpType(ref TypeSyntax t, …)` and `dumpPattern(ref Pattern pattern, …)` build but cannot be called on a child; T11/T12 should change them to `in` (not changed here, those files are theirs). `dump` and `checkSpans` take the root `CompilationUnit`, which is not `Owned`, so `ref` works there. New.
437. **009 T2: names in `nodes.byn` that differ from the plan or from C#.** (a) A union variant is the record's name with its first letter lowered (`Decl.importDecl`, `Stmt.blockStmt`), not the plan's `import(…)`/`function(…)`: `import`, `struct`, `if` and others are keywords. (b) A C# name that is a Bayan keyword or reserved word takes the suffix `Keyword`, as `ParseCode.gotoKeyword` does: fields `defaultKeyword`, `failsKeyword`, `usesKeyword`, `requiresKeyword`, `becauseKeyword`, `exceptKeyword`, `returnKeyword`, `usingKeyword`, `elseKeyword`, `tryKeyword`, `unlessKeyword`, and enum members such as `ParamModifier.refKeyword`, `BindingKind.letKeyword`, `AssignOp.andKeyword`, `UnaryOp.notKeyword`, `Likelihood.neverKeyword`, `LiteralKind.trueKeyword` and `LiteralKind.floatKeyword` (`float` is reserved, BYN0012). (c) `Modifiers` is `type Modifiers = u16` with consts `modifierNone` … `modifierUnsafe` (`public`, `static` and the rest are keywords). (d) A C# child typed as one node kind (`BlockStmt`, `NamedType`, `TargetMemberExpr`) is its union (`Stmt`, `TypeSyntax`, `Expr`), as the parsing entry points return it. (e) The base `Decl`'s `Doc` and `Attributes` are the last two fields of each declaration struct. (f) The enum text functions the plan's Approach mentions are left to the dump owners (`dump2.byn` lists `AssignText`, `BinaryText`, `UnaryText` for T12). New.
440. **009 T3: `unreport` without `removeAt`.** `List` has no `removeAt`, and the diagnostic C# `Unreport` removes is not always the last one, so `unreport(ref p, at: index)` sets the entry's `code` to `""` (a tombstone); `errorCount` (T1) skips it and the dump (T11) must drop it before `renderAll`. An index of -1 is the C# `null` and does nothing. C# `Unreport` is only `_diagnostics.Remove(d)`: it does not decrement `_syntaxErrors` or reset `_lastErrorAt`, so neither does the port, although the 009 task line and plan say it decrements `syntaxErrors`. The one call site (`ParseUnless`) unreports BYN1017, an input form that never counted, so both readings print the same; `SelfhostParserT3Tests.RecoveryAndLineStructure` pins the C# behaviour. New.
441. **009 T3: cross-file helpers that have no T1 stub, and the signatures `recover.byn` exports.** (a) `patterns.byn` calls five C# helpers that sibling files own and T1 did not stub: `ParseBinary(Prec.Shift)` and `ParseBinary(Prec.Range)` (T9), `ScanType` (T6), `BraceLiteralAllowed` (T7) and `ExpectClose` (T4). A module cannot define a function twice, so `patterns.byn` calls them through stand-ins in a marked section at the end of the file, `struct T3 { static … }` (`T3.shiftOperand`, `T3.rangeOperand`, `T3.scanType`, `T3.braceLiteralAllowed`, `T3.expectClose`); the two `ParseBinary` stand-ins return `.none` and `T3.scanType` returns -1 until T15 points each `T3.` call at the sibling's function and deletes the struct; the other two are ports of the C# bodies. Until then a constant or relational pattern has no value, and `Type { … }`, `Type(…)` and `Type name` patterns parse as constants. (b) Signatures in `recover.byn` siblings should call (the particle rule fixed the labels): `expectEnd(ref p)`, `reportSemicolon(ref p, for: token)`, `indentAt(ref p, at: offset)`, `breaksLine(ref p, at: i)`, `hasBlankLineBefore(ref p, at: i)`, `isWasl(ref p, at: i)`, `lineContinues(ref p, at: i)`, `stopsHere(ref p)` (C# `StopsHere`, in the same block, so it lives here and not in `exprs.byn`), `endsBefore(ref p, at: i)`, `inGroup(ref p, at: open, for: kind)`, `expectName(ref p, "what")` returning the name's `TextSpan`, `nameOf(token)`, `isName(kind)`, `isStatementKeyword(kind)`, `unreport(ref p, at: index)`, `isContextualKeyword(kind)`, `isCSharpPrimitive(text)`, and the sets as predicates `isItName(text)` and `isParticle(text)` (strings, as C# compares `Name.Text`). (c) A missing name is the empty span at the current token; C# prints it as `<missing>`, so T11/T12 must print `<missing>` for a zero-length name span. New.
442. **009 T3: `char.IsUpper` in `ParsePrimaryPattern` is ASCII only.** C# tests the first UTF-16 unit of the identifier with `char.IsUpper`, which is true for non-ASCII upper-case letters (`Ä`, `Δ`, `Ж`). Bayan has no Unicode case table (the lexer's tables cover identifier categories only), so `startsUpper` checks `A`–`Z`; a pattern starting with a non-ASCII upper-case name parses as a constant where C# tries a type. *Current choice (conservative):* ASCII, recorded here; T14's generator should not emit such names until a `Lu` table exists. New.
445. **009 T4: the `T4` stand-ins in `decls.byn`.** Helpers that other wave files own are stand-ins in `struct T4 { static … }` at the end of `decls.byn`, under `// ── T4 stand-ins (T15 deletes) ──`, with the C# name in camelCase and the C# parameter order; T15 deletes the struct and drops the `T4.` prefix. Ported in full: `isName` (with the `IsContextualKeyword` list), `expectEnd`, `reportSemicolon`, `endsBefore`, `breaksLine`, `indentAt`, `particles`, `itName`, `atContextual`, `matchingClose`, `parseBareCondition`, `nextCase` and T5's `expectClose`. Conservative: `expectName` skips the C# primitive check (BYN1004); `scanType` reads a qualified name and an optional `?`, and `scanTypeArgs` returns -1; `parseTypeWith` parses a plain or qualified name itself and otherwise calls the T6 stub; `typeSpan`, `exprSpan` and `stmtSpan` switch over every variant; `parseArguments` and T5's `parsePayload` return an empty list; T5's `parseFieldOrProperty` and `parseErrorUnion` return `.none`; `reportKeywordOrder` and `reportCaseCommas` do nothing; T5's other entry points call nothing. So the T4 test (`SelfhostParserT4Tests`) avoids non-name types outside parameters, expressions, blocks, attribute arguments, payloads and fields. Break-test: changing `p.pos - 2` to `p.pos - 3` in the `noallocRemoved` fix span (decls.byn:914) made the T4 test fail (BYN6001 fix `3+14` instead of `9+8`); the line was restored from a backup copy (a checkout would have reverted the uncommitted port) and the test passed again. New.
446. **009 T4: the O3 step of `ParseStruct` is deferred to T15.** C# (Parser.cs:759–775) moves each field rule that names another field, or has `at .f`, into `StructDecl.Rules`, rebuilds the field with only its own rules (`field with { Requires = own }`), and sorts the struct's rules by span start. The port cannot: a field reaches `parseStruct` from T5's `parseFieldOrProperty` already wrapped in `Owned<FieldDecl>`, and nothing can come back out of an `Owned`. `.value` is read-only (BYN2106, "an `Owned` value is read-only"), and copying a child is BYN2780: `RequiresRule` is unique because of `condition`, `TypeSyntax` because of `namedType`, `Expr` because of `literalExpr` (checked by adding `rules.append(f.value.requiresKeyword[k])`, `let ty = f.value.type` and `let de = f.value.defaultKeyword` to the O3 loop). `List.copy()` refuses unique elements (`CopyUniqueElement`). The port still reports BYN3218 as C# does and leaves the rules on the field, at the marked `// O3: deferred to T15 (Q446)` site in `parseStruct`. Fix (launcher ruling, 2026-10-26): T15 has `parseFieldOrProperty` (decls2.byn) split a field's rules before wrapping it in `Owned`, and `parseStruct` moves them into `rules` and sorts by start. Until then a struct with field `requires` rules differs from C# (golden `requires-rules`, Q449). New. 011 T13 ported O3 as C# does it (Q819): `parseFieldOrProperty` hands the field to `parseStruct` unwrapped.
447. **009 T4: names the port synthesises.** C# builds some names as strings that have no source span. In the port, a `[Bracket]` attribute keeps its source name span, and the camelCase name lives only in the BYN1045 fix text. The implicit `void` of a name-first function is a zero-length span at the name. The `ReadOnlySpan<T>` of a `T... xs` or `rest T xs` parameter is the element type's span. A reader that needs the C# text must rebuild it. New.
448. **009 T4: `parseDeclaration`'s struct name.** C# passes `string? structName`; the port passes `for TextSpan? structName` (the name's span), as nodes hold spans. A caller compares the text through `p.lexed.source.getText`. New.
449. **009 T4: other shapes that differ from C#.** (a) The `ParseParams` overload with the extra outputs is `parseParamsWith(to ref refThis, through ref moveThis, for ref receiverStates, allowRefThis)`; `parseParams` calls it. (b) `DelegateAlias` returns the alias name and writes the type text through `to ref string type`. (c) C# `HashSet<string>`s are `List`s searched in order. (d) Of the three `ParseBody(string, …)` sites only `struct` (Parser.cs 731) is T4's; its body loop is inlined in `parseStruct` and calls `parseStatesBlock`, the state-line check and `parseDeclaration` directly, with no stored callback. The `interface` and `extension` sites are T5's. (e) A name-first function is only a `FunctionDecl` when `{` or `fails` follows `)` (`IsNameFirstFunctionStart`), so `f() uses alloc {}` at the top level is not a function in C# either; the T4 cases put `fails` first. (f) No parse golden passes on this branch: every function golden has a body (T7's `parseBlock`) and types and expressions (T6, T8), and the dump runs through T11/T12. Goldens in `tests/cases/parse/` whose top level is only functions and structs, for T15 to check against T4's declarations: `assert`, `control-flow-bare`, `control-flow-brace-gate`, `control-flow-same-line`, `defer-family`, `except-in-case-left`, `input-forms-one-line`, `interpolation-specs`, `lambdas`, `particles`, `particles-for-as`, `postfix`, `provide-become`, `receiver-states`, `ref-this`, `requires`, `requires-bare-condition`, `rest-params`, `statements`, `structs`, `switch`, `uses-becomes`, `where-becomes-uses`, `word-booleans`. `requires-rules` (a struct with field `requires` rules, plus a type alias from T5) needs the O3 step (Q446). New.
450. **009 T5: sibling helpers with no stub are called through `T5.` shims.** `decls2.byn` calls about thirty helpers owned by T3 (`isName`, `expectName`, `expectEnd`, `reportSemicolon`, `endsBefore`, `hasBlankLineBefore`, `indentAt`), T4 (`docOf`, `parseAttributes`, `isAttributeStart`, `parseModifiers`, `rejectModifiers`, `isFunctionStart`, `isNameFirstFunctionStart`, `parseFunction`, `isNameThenType`, `parseNameThenType`, `isTypeThenName`, `parseTypeParams`, `parseBases`, `parseWhere`, `parseRequiresRule`, `parseParams`, `parseRefinement`), T6 (`scanType`, `ParseType(fatArrow:, lists:)`, `TypeSyntax.Span`), T8 (`atContextual`) and T9 (`parseArguments`); T1 stubbed only the plan's cross-file entry points, so none existed. A stub of the real name would collide with the owner's function when both land. *Current choice (conservative):* every such call is `T5.name(…)`, static methods of an empty `struct T5` at the end of `decls2.byn` with just enough body for the T5 test; T15 deletes the struct and drops the `T5.` prefix, adjusting any call whose owner chose other particles. Guessed shapes to check then: `expectName(ref p, what: …)`, `rejectModifiers(ref p, for: modifiers, by: allowed, at: index)`, `parseFunction(ref p, at: start, by: modifiers, allowNoBody: …)` returning `FunctionDecl`, `docOf(ref p, for: token)`, `atContextual(ref p, for: word)`, `reportSemicolon(ref p, for: token)`, `endsBefore`/`hasBlankLineBefore`/`isNameThenType`/`isTypeThenName`/`scanType(ref p, at: index)`, `indentAt(ref p, at: offset)`, `parseRefinement(ref p, from: move type, name: …)`; `parseNameThenType(ref p, to: ref type)` returns the name because a tuple element cannot be moved out of (BYN2782) and `let (a, b) = …` does not parse; `T5.parseTypeWith(ref p, fatArrow:, lists:)` stands for the C# overload the `parseType` stub lacks; `T5.typeSpan(in t)` is a real switch over the eight `TypeSyntax` variants and should move to whoever owns a span accessor (T6 or T12). New.
451. **009 T5: how `doc` and `attributes` reach a declaration, and the shared helpers in `decls2.byn`.** An `Owned` payload is read-only (Q436), so the C# `decl with { Doc = doc, Attributes = attributes }` in `ParseDeclaration` cannot run after the fact. *Current choice:* a C# parser that returns one node kind returns its struct (`InterfaceDecl parseInterface(ref p, at: start, by: modifiers)`, likewise `parseExtension(ref p, at: start)`, `parseConstructor`, `parseErrorComposition`, `parseEnum`, `parseUnion`, `parseTypeAlias`, `parseEffect`, `parseTest(ref p, at: start)`), and T4's `parseDeclaration` sets `doc` and `attributes` on it before `Decl.xxx(Owned(move d))`; the two that return a `Decl` of several kinds take them: `parseFieldOrProperty(ref p, at: start, by: modifiers, through: move attributes, doc: doc)` and `parseErrorUnion(…)` alike (a `List` parameter default is not a constant, BYN2219, so `attributes` is required and needs a particle). `parseInterfaceMember` returns `.none` for the C# `null`. The interface and extension `ParseBody` sites are inlined. Helpers here that other files call: `expectClose(ref p, from: open, for: what)` (T3, T4, T7, T8, T10), `parsePayload(ref p, for: variant)`, `nextCase(ref p, to: ref commas)`, `reportCaseCommas(ref p, for: typeName, from: open, through: in cases, by: in commas)` and `reportKeywordOrder(ref p, from: modifier, to: kind, as: canonical)` (T4's structs and states), `parseRequiresLines(ref p)`; their line range is T5's, so a sibling that also ports one leaves a duplicate for T15. New.
452. **009 T5: small differences from the C# forced by the language.** (a) `ParsePayload`'s `Name(…, "<missing>")` for a type without a name is a zero-length span at `prevEnd`, like every other name (T2's span-names choice); the dump must print `<missing>` for it if the C# does (T11). (b) `KeptComment` slices the gap with `gap[first..last]`; the lexer's `utf8` is not public. (c) `ReportKeywordOrder`'s `TrimStart()` trims ASCII white space only (space, tab, CR, LF, VT, FF); C# also trims Unicode spaces, which cannot occur between two keywords outside a comment. (d) `decodeString(p.text(token))` borrows `p` (BYN3004 when `p` is used again), so the test title is copied with `$"{…}"`, the lexer's idiom for `finish()`. (e) Locals named `where` are fine; `requires` and `except` are keywords, so those locals are `rules` and `exceptNames`, and `distinct` is `isDistinct`. (f) The build adds BYN5014 warnings for the C# method names (`parseAttributes`, `isFunctionStart`, `atContextual`, …), as Q431 (f) notes for the flags; a warning never blocks. New.
455. **009 T6: how a decoded `string` is built and stored.** `StrBuf.finish()` returns a view that borrows the buffer, so returning it from a decoder is BYN3003; each decoder (`literals.byn`) returns `$"{sb.finish()}"`, a copy in the context allocator (the arena), as the lexer's `utf8` (`source.byn`) already does. The decoders work on a `List<rune>` first (C# indexes chars; `runesOf` decodes the bytes as `Encoding.UTF8` does), and `stringOf(move List<rune>)` makes the `StrBuf`: a `List` returned from a function that takes a borrowed span counts as a borrow of that span (rule 4, §9), so a helper that returned one, or took the runes as a span of a local, was BYN3003 inside the decoder. The returned `string` still counts as a borrow of the token bytes it was given, which are `p.lexed.source`; a node can hold it while the source lives, which is how the tree is used. T6 stores no decoded string in a node; if T10 (`LiteralExpr`) or the declaration owners (doc text) hit a region error there, the fallback is to keep the token span in the node and decode in the dump. New.
456. **009 T6: C# name rewrites in `NamedType`.** C# `ParseNamedType` builds `Name`s whose text is rewritten (`CSharpTypeNames`: `int` to `i32` and the rest; `char` to `rune` after BYN1048; `<missing>` for `MissingType`). `NamedType.path` is `List<TextSpan>` (`nodes.byn`), so the text cannot be stored: `types.byn` exports `cSharpTypeName(string) -> string` (empty when not a C# name) and the dump (T12) must apply it, the `char` rewrite, and `<missing>` for a zero-length path span. A zero-length name from `expectName` is the same shape as a missing type's; the C# prints `<missing>` for both only when the text is empty, so the dump can test the length. New.
457. **009 T6: `ReportPointerOutsideExtern` bypasses `report`.** The C# calls `_diagnostics.Report` directly, so BYN1067 neither moves `lastErrorAt` nor counts as a syntax error for `recoverIfNeeded`. `types.byn` appends the `Diagnostic` to `p.lexed.diagnostics` itself with `codeText`/`messageFormat`/`format`; if T1 adds a `reportQuiet` (or similar) to `parser.byn`, T15 can switch to it. New.
460. **009 T7: helpers with no T1 stub, and the signatures T7 assumed.** `stmts.byn` calls 28 helpers that siblings own but T1 did not stub. *Current choice (conservative):* they are statics of `struct T7` at the bottom of `stmts.byn`, called as `T7.name(…)` so they cannot collide with the real ones. Each has the smallest body that builds, and the C# one-liners (`breaksLine`, `endsBefore`, `isNameThenType`) are ported so the T7 tests run. `exprSpan` (T9) is one of them too, because the T7 and T10 tests build the parser without `exprs.byn`; the plain-named `inGroup` and `exprSpan` copies were removed at merge, since T3 and T9 own them. On merge, T15 deletes the struct and drops the `T7.` prefix; a sibling whose signature differs changes the call site. The assumed signatures: T3 `expectEnd(ref p)`, `reportSemicolon(ref p, at: Token)`, `breaksLine/lineContinues/endsBefore(ref p, at: i64)`, `expectName(ref p, string what = "a name") -> TextSpan`, `nameOf(Token) -> TextSpan`, `isName(TokenKind)`, `unreport(ref p, at: i64)` (must accept -1; the stand-in marks the entry removed with code `""`); T4 `isFunctionStart(ref p)`, `isTypeThenName/isNameThenType(ref p, at: i64)`, `expectClose(ref p, from: Token open, for: string what)`; T5 `parseRefinement(ref p, from: move TypeSyntax) -> TypeSyntax`; T6 `isTypeNameToken(TokenKind)`, `scanType(ref p, at: i64) -> i64`; T8 `parseSwitchStatement/parseDefer/parseContext/parseGoto/parseSimpleStatement(ref p, from: i64 start)`, `finishSimpleStatement(ref p, from: start, by: move Stmt)`, `rejectPostfixAfterCompound(ref p, by: move Stmt)`, `atContextual(ref p, for: string)`; T9 `canStartExpression(TokenKind)`, `parseArguments(ref p) -> List<Argument>`; T10 `isPatternExprStart(ref p)`, `parsePatternExpr(ref p) -> Expr`. T6's `parseType(ref p)` stub has no `fatArrow`/`lists`, so `parseLocal` calls it bare with a comment naming the C# arguments; T15 restores them. `stmtSpan`, `exprSpan` and `typeSpan` (the C# `Node.Span` of a union child) belong to no task, so `stmts.byn` defines them for real. The stand-in methods draw BYN5014 warnings (`semicolon`, `function`, `defer` and others), as in Q431(f). New.
461. **009 T7: C# parser fields and by-reference returns that do not carry over.** (a) The C# fields `_bracesReport` and `_bracesFix` cannot be added to `Parser` (T1's file). *Current choice (conservative):* a `BracesReport { report, hasFix, fixSpan, fixReplacement }` that the caller passes down through a third overload, `parseBody(ref p, by: keyword, to: ref header, for: ref braces)`; only `parseUnless` uses it, and C#'s `_bracesReport?.Span == body.Span` test becomes "this body's own report". (b) A `Diagnostic?` is its index in `p.lexed.diagnostics` (-1 for `null`), and `Replace(d, d with { Fix = … })` sets that entry's `hasFix`/`fixSpan`/`fixReplacement` in place. (c) `Unwrap(Expr)` cannot return a union child by reference, so `checkUnlessCondition` recurses through `.parenExpr`. (d) `ParseParenFor(…) with { Try = isTry }` becomes a `tryKeyword` parameter set before the node is wrapped. (e) The C# local `fails` is a keyword and is `failure`. New.
462. **009 T7: range taken and what is left to T8.** T7 ports lines 2116–2776, not "about 2665": `ParseFor`, `IsTupleLoopVariables`, `ParseParenFor` and `SkipPastCloseParen` are loops (the task line lists `for`), so T8 should not port them. The guarded statement (`x unless c`) is built in `FinishSimpleStatement` (line 3094), which is T8's; T7 provides what it calls: `checkUnlessCondition`, `skipUnlessLikelihood`, `atUnlikely` and `braceLiteralAllowed`. New.
463. **009 T7: a missing name is an empty span, not `"<missing>"`.** C# `ExpectName` returns `Name(span, "<missing>")`, and messages and fixes that print a missing name (BYN1043 in `reportTypeFirstLocal` and `for T x`, the BYN1019 fix) include that text; a `TextSpan` gives `""`. A tuple loop variable is the group's span where C# names it `"_"` (the dump prints `names` instead). *Current choice (conservative):* left to T3's `expectName` and T11's dump; on a well-formed input nothing differs. *Open:* whether `nodes.byn` should mark a missing name, so the dump and these messages can print `<missing>`. New.
464. **009 T7: which goldens test the statements, and why none pass yet.** The parse goldens whose statements are only T7's are `tests/cases/parse/control-flow-brace-gate` and `control-flow-same-line`. They also need a function declaration (T4), calls, `is` and struct-literal expressions (T9, T10) and the dump (T11), so neither can pass until those merge; T15 checks them. `control-flow-bare` and `statements` also use `switch`, assignments and increments (T8). Until then `SelfhostParserT7Tests.StatementsMatchTheCSharpParser` compares 30 statement-only inputs (shapes with spans, diagnostics with fixes) against `SyntaxTree.Parse`, through a small expression parser in place of `exprs.byn`. A stray `else` is left out, because what follows it depends on T3's `recoverIfNeeded`. New. Break-test record: at 546882a, the BYN1041 fix replacement at `selfhost/parser/stmts.byn:537` changed from `" "` to `""` made `SelfhostParserT7Tests` fail 1 of 30; `git checkout -- selfhost/parser/stmts.byn` restored it with `git diff --quiet` clean, and the rerun passed 30/30 (run by the launcher; the worker hook blocks `git checkout --`).
465. **009 T8: the T7/T8 boundary is by topic, not line number.** The task line names `assert`, `become`, labeled statements, `EmptyStmt` and `ErrorStmt`, but those are inline cases inside `ParseStatement` (stmts.byn, T7's "ParseStatement dispatch"), with no method of their own, and lines 2667–2777 (`ParseFor`, `IsTupleLoopVariables`, `ParseParenFor`, `SkipPastCloseParen`) are T7's loops. *Current choice:* `stmts2.byn` ports the methods those dispatch cases call plus `Parser.cs` 2778–3136 (`ParseSwitchStatement`, `ParseSwitchLabel`, `ParseArmPattern`, `ParseDefer`, `StartsDeferBody`, `IsBinding`, `AtContextual`, `ParseContext`, `ParseGoto`, `ParseSimpleStatement`, `ParseJumpLabel`, `ReportOnNewLine`, `IsStatementExpression`, `TryAssignOp`, `CheckAssignable`, `FinishSimpleStatement`, `RejectPostfixAfterCompound`). T15 verifies the dispatch cases in T7's file cover every name on the T8 line. New.
466. **009 T8: node spans need a helper the C# does not have.** The C# `Expr.Span`/`Pattern.Span` properties have no Bayan counterpart on a union, so `stmts2.byn` defines `TextSpan exprSpan(in Expr)` and `TextSpan patternSpan(in Pattern)` (one arm per variant) for `CheckAssignable`, `ParseSimpleStatement` and `ParseArmPattern`. T11/T12 (dump) will need the same accessors; T15 may hoist them into a shared file and delete T8's copies. New. At merge, T8's own `exprSpan` became the stand-in `T8.exprSpan` (exprs.byn owns the real one; the T10 test builds without exprs.byn); T15 drops the prefix.
467. **009 T8: stand-in particles are guesses until T15.** The `struct T8` stand-ins for T3/T5/T7/T9 helpers keep the C# names and parameter order, with particles chosen by meaning (`for`/`at`/`as`/`through`/`to`; notably `reportBraceless(ref p, for: keyword, at: gapStart, through: in body, clean:, to: header)`). When T15 drops the `T8.` prefix, those call sites must match the owners' real signatures; any mismatch is resolved there, not here. `atContextual` is T8's own (line 2895), not a stand-in, though T7's `AtUnlikely` calls it. New.
468. **009 T8: parse goldens and T15-only coverage.** No parse golden can pass before the wave merges: `tests/cases/parse/switch.byn`, `defer-family.byn`, `provide-become.byn` and `postfix.byn` (and `statements.byn`, mixed) exercise the T8 statements but route every expression, pattern and nested statement through sibling stubs (`parseExpression`, `parsePattern`, `parseStatement` return `.none`), so the dump would not match the C# `.ast`; T15 runs them after rebasing. The T8 methods that only run through those stand-ins are therefore T15-only (`parseSwitchStatement`, `parseSwitchLabel`, `parseArmPattern`, `parseDefer`, `parseContext`, `parseSimpleStatement`, `parseJumpLabel`, `reportOnNewLine`, `finishSimpleStatement`, `rejectPostfixAfterCompound`); the self-contained pieces — `tryAssignOp`, `parseGoto`, `exprSpan`, `patternSpan`, `isStatementExpression`, `checkAssignable` — are exercised by `SelfhostParserT8Tests.SelfContainedStatementsBuildAndRun`. New.
470. **009 T9: stand-ins for helpers other tasks own.** `exprs.byn` calls helpers that no sibling had stubbed when T9 ran, so its last section, "T9 stand-ins", defines them as static members of `struct T9` (called `T9.name(…)`, so they cannot collide with the owners' top-level definitions) with the signature T9 assumes: `isContextualKeyword(TokenKind)`, `isName(TokenKind)`, `breaksLine(ref p, at:)`, `hasBlankLineBefore(ref p, at:)`, `stopsHere(ref p)` (complete ports); `isWasl(ref p, at:)` without the `where`/`becomes`/`expects` cases, `expectName(ref p, what:)` without BYN0012, `expectClose(ref p, for: open, as: what)` without the help (partial); `parseBecause(ref p, for:, at:)` (returns `null`), `scanType(ref p, at:)` and `scanExprTypeArgs(ref p, at:)` (return -1), `parseTypeArgs`, `parseFieldInits` (empty lists), `parseArmPattern(ref p, for:)` (calls `parsePattern`), `atContextual(ref p, for:)`, `braceBodyHasStatementBreak` (returns `false`). `exprSpan(in Expr)` and `blockSpan(in Stmt)` belong to T9 and stay. A cast's type span is `spanFrom(typeStart)`, which equals the C# `TypeSyntax.Span` only while types end at the last token consumed. *Current choice (conservative):* T15 deletes the struct and drops the `T9.` prefix at each call. As members, the names are checked by BYN5014 (`contextual`, `wasl`, `here`, `because`, `arm`, `brace`, `statement`); `SelfhostParserT9Tests` ignores BYN5014 inside the struct only. New.
471. **009 T9: a child cannot be moved out of an `Owned` payload.** `ParseBinaryRest` rebuilds a parsed constant (`a except 1..2`) as a range bound, which in C# reuses the node; in Bayan `move constant.value.value` is BYN2782 (cannot move out of a field). *Current choice (conservative):* `reparseConstant` rewinds to the constant's first token and parses it again at `precRange` with `noLambda` set, dropping the diagnostics of the second parse and restoring `pos`, `prevEnd`, `syntaxErrors` and `lastErrorAt`. Same tree and diagnostics as C# on the rows tested; a `take` on `Owned` would remove the rewind. New.
472. **009 T9: call-site friction in `parser.byn`'s helpers.** A bool literal argument must be named (BYN2305), so `p.setNoLambda(value: true)`; an optional compares with `is null`/`is not null` (`== null` is BYN2027); `unless` takes no `&&`/`||` (BYN1022). *Current choice:* written that way; no change to `parser.byn`. New.
473. **009 T9: C# spans that end before a child.** C# evaluates `new X(SpanFrom(start), ParseY())` left to right, so `move`, `fail`, `break`/`continue` with a label, `except` and `?.` take their span before parsing the child and end at the keyword or operator. *Current choice (conservative):* the port takes the span at the same point, so the dumps agree; these children fall outside their parent, which L018's child-within-parent check (`spans.byn`, T12) will flag; recorded in work/todo.md. New.

475. **009 T10: C# renames a span cannot hold.** A name is its `TextSpan` (Q437), so a C# `Name` whose `Text` is not its source text is lost: (a) `ParseTypeNameOnly` renames `stackalloc int[n]` to `i32` (the eight `CSharpTypeNames`) and `stackalloc char[n]` to `rune` after BYN1048; (b) `ParseCompactSpec` names the spec `as` or `digits` at the colon's span, so `{n:hex}` dumps `(as: .hex)` in C# and would dump `:` from the span. `diag/compact-format-spec.byn` is the one golden input affected (no golden uses `stackalloc` with a C# type name); T6's `ParseType` has the same rename. (c) `char.IsUpper`/`IsLower` on a name's first character (struct and state literals) is ASCII-only here. *Current choice (conservative):* `exprs2.byn` keeps the spans, reports the same diagnostics and fixes, and does not edit `nodes.byn`. *Open, for T12/T15:* either the dump maps a one-segment `NamedType` without arguments through `CSharpTypeNames` and `char` → `rune` (the C# renames under exactly that condition), and prints a format-spec name whose source is `:` as `as` when its value is a `targetMemberExpr`, else `digits`; or `nodes.byn` gains a `string?` text override. New.
476. **009 T10: helpers `exprs2.byn` needs that T1 did not stub.** The port calls `IsName`, `IsContextualKeyword`, `BreaksLine`, `ExpectName` (T3), `TokensText`, `ExpectClose` (T4), `IsTypeNameToken`, `ScanTypeArgs`, `ScanExprTypeArgs`, `ParseTypeArgs` (T6), `MatchingClose`, `BraceLiteralAllowed` (T7) and `AtContextual` (T8); none has a stub, so the file would not build. *Current choice (conservative):* a marked *Stand-ins* section at the end of `exprs2.byn` defines each as a `static` of `struct T10`, called as `T10.isName(…)`, with a guessed signature (`isName(kind)`, `breaksLine(ref p, at: i)`, `expectName(ref p, for: what)`, `tokensText(ref p, from: a, until: b)`, `expectClose(ref p, from: open, for: what)`, `scanTypeArgs(ref p, at: i)`, `scanExprTypeArgs(ref p, at: i)`, `parseTypeArgs(ref p)`, `matchingClose(ref p, from: i)`, `braceLiteralAllowed(ref p)`, `atContextual(ref p, for: word)`): the C# body where it is short, a stub for the three type scanners (never type arguments) and `expectName` without the C# primitive-name check. T15 deletes `struct T10` and drops the `T10.` prefix at the call sites, matching the owners' signatures; the struct keeps the names from colliding with the owners' definitions at merge. No parse golden passes on this branch: `parseCompilationUnit`, `parseExpression` and the dump are stubs until the siblings merge. T15 candidates whose inputs are expression-heavy: `parse/collection-literals`, `contextual-keywords`, `expressions`, `interpolation-specs`, `lambdas`, `lambdas-recovery`, `null-checks`, `struct-literal-colon`, `word-booleans`; `diag/compact-format-spec` waits on Q475. `NameOf(token)` is `spanOf(token)`, so it needs none. Siblings call these of mine: `parsePrimary(ref p)`, `isPatternExprStart(ref p)`, `parsePatternExpr(ref p)` (T7, `ParseLocal`), `braceBodyHasStatementBreak(ref p)` and `parseFieldInits(ref p) -> List<FieldInit>` (T9, `with` and `catch`). New.
477. **009 T10: two shapes forced by the checker.** (a) Storing `decodeInterpolatedText(p.text(token))` in a node inside the `parseInterpolated` loop is BYN3004 (`p` modified while `parts` borrows it): a function's `string` result taking a span is assumed to borrow it. The literal cases of `parsePrimary` return at once and build; the interpolation text is copied with `$"{…}"`. T6 may see the same (Q455). (b) `move first.value` out of a local `TupleElement` is BYN2782, so `parseParenOrTuple` parses the first element through `parseTupleName` plus `parseExpression` (what `parseTupleElement` does) and builds the `ParenExpr` or `TupleElement` from the parts; behaviour is unchanged. New.
480. **009 T11: nullable node fields and function/parameter names in the dump.** (a) Bayan flow typing narrows a local or parameter, not a field path: `if d.value.failsKeyword is not null { … d.value.failsKeyword.errors … }` still sees `FailsClause?` (BYN2211); the idiom is to bind the field, `if (d.value.failsKeyword is { } fails) { … fails.errors … }`, which borrows without copying the unique payload. (b) `for` over `List<Param>` must bind by borrow; `let param = parameters[i]` is BYN2780 because `Param`'s `type` field is a unique union. (c) A function whose parameter shares its own name (`void decl(in Decl decl, …)`) shadows the function, so recursive `decl(…)` calls resolve to the parameter and report `Decl` cannot be called (BYN2220); the parameter is named `node` instead. (d) The enum text functions the C# spells by `ToString()` (`BindingKind` → `Let`/`Var`/`Const`) are private helpers here; only `AssignText` is T12's, called through the `T11.assignText` stand-in. New.
485. **009 T12: `BlockExpr` calls T11's statement dump, which has no stub.** The C# `Expr`'s `BlockExpr` case flattens `new Writer().Stmt(0, s)` per statement. T11's `dump.byn` owns `Stmt`, but the plan's cross-file entry points list only `dump`, so there is no `stmt` stub on this branch. *Current choice (conservative):* `dump2.byn` calls a stand-in `T12.stmt(in Stmt s, at i64 depth, from ref Parser p, to ref StrBuf sb)` (empty body) at the end of the file, and `dumpBlockExpr` flattens its output (`appendFlattened` trims trailing `\n`, trims each line, joins with `"; "`). T15 deletes `struct T12` and drops the prefix once T11's real `stmt` signature is known; if T11's signature differs, rename the call site then. `BlockExpr`'s exact text is therefore only checkable after T11 merges (`@T15-only`). New.
486. **009 T12: `is`-pattern syntax gotchas, one of which crashes the bootstrap C# parser.** (a) An empty-property-pattern `is` test must be parenthesized: `if (x is { } n)` parses, but `if x is { } n {` is read with `{ }` as the body block and fails with BYN1002. (b) A payload variant in an `is` test needs a pattern: `x is .mapEntryExpr(_)`, not `x is .mapEntryExpr` (BYN2705 "variant carries a payload"); `none` needs none. (c) A pattern binding must not be a keyword: `if (m.args is { } as)` (binding named `as`) misparses `as` as the `as` keyword, and the resulting braceless `if` body makes the bootstrap C# parser throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` in `Parser.ReportBraceless` (Parser.cs:2408, `FromBounds(body.Span.Start, _prevEnd)`). This is a crash on invalid input rather than a behaviour mismatch, so it is not matched in the port; it is recorded as a `work/todo.md` line, and the workaround is renaming the binding (`args`). Siblings writing `is { }` on a keyword should do the same. New.
487. **009 T12: `Sexp` is inlined, and `TypeNames`/`CalleeNames` are not ported.** The C# `Sexp(StringBuilder, string, params Expr?[])` has no Bayan shape — there is no `params`, and the children are move-only unions that cannot be put in a list — so each S-expression is written inline at its call site, a `none` child printing `_` (the C# `null`). The C# `TypeNames`/`CalleeNames` thread-static side collections (used by `AstDump.TypeNames`/`CalleeAndReceiverNames`) are not part of the dump text, so the `TypeNames?.Add(only)` and `CalleeNames?.Add(...)` side effects are dropped; the self-hosted dump has no such collectors. Both are noted in `dump2.byn`'s header. New.

488. **009 T12: break-test performed and restored.** Broke `binaryText`'s `.add` arm from `"+"` to `"-"` in `dump2.byn`; `SelfhostParserT12Tests.DumpExprTypePatternAndCheckSpans` failed with `expr (- a b)` against `expr (+ a b)`; restored from `tmp/dump2.bak` and confirmed byte-identical with `cmp`, after which the test passed again. The comprehensive `DumpCoversEveryExprTypeAndPatternCase` test was then added, which also breaks on a misspelled operator text. New.
489. **009 T12: no parse golden can pass on this branch.** The `parse/*.byn` → `.ast` goldens need the parsing tasks T3–T10 (declarations, types, statements, expressions) and T11's declaration/statement dump, all still stubs, plus T13's `bayan-parse`; T12's `dump2.byn`/`spans.byn` are exercised only in isolation (`SelfhostParserT12Tests`). Full byte-identical golden parity is T15's. New.

490. **009 T13: `--many`/`--time` exit codes, and the dump/span-check order.** The plan's "exit 0 or 1 like `CliApp.Parse`" is the single-file mode: exit 0 with no diagnostics, 1 with any, 4 when the input cannot be read. `--many` and `--time` mirror `bayan-lex` instead: exit 0 on success and 2 on an unlistable/missing path, so a file with parse errors still dumps and `--many` ends 0 (the per-file exit is not aggregated). `--many` writes the dump before the `checkSpans` lines (as the plan's "`== <name>\n` + dump + span-check lines"), unlike `bayan-lex --many`, which writes span-check lines first. *Open:* whether `--many` should exit 1 when any file has a diagnostic, and whether the span-check lines should precede the dump to match the lexer. New.
491. **009 T13: `DiagGolden` uses the single-file parse as the reference.** 85 `diag/*.diag` files contain `BYN1`, one in a subdirectory (`input-fails-qualified/main.diag`). For each, the sibling `.byn` is parsed alone (never the semantic `.diag`), the C# `AstDump.Dump` is written under `tmp/parser-ref/<case, `/` as `_`>.byn.ast`, and `Golden.Compare` names the input and the first differing line. *Open:* whether a subdirectory `.diag` whose `BYN1` arises only in an imported file should still be checked by parsing the entry `main.byn` alone. New.
492. **009 T13: the timing test's 1 MB input until T14 merges.** `OneMegabyteWithinTenTimes` is the lexer's timing test shape (median of 5, `BAYAN_SKIP_TIMING=1`) against `SyntaxTree.Parse` + `AstDump.Dump`; the input is `LexerTests.OneMegabyte()` (a repeated struct and function, valid parser input) as the local placeholder for T14's `SelfhostParserGenerator.OneMegabyte()`. T15 swaps it and records the ratio in Q500. New.

493. **009 T13: break-test record.** At 4291a28, `selfhost/parser/main.byn:105` `"--codes"` changed to `"--codez"` made `CodesMatchDiagnosticCodes` fail (1 of 1); `git checkout -- selfhost/parser/main.byn` restored it with `git diff --quiet` clean, and the rerun passed. Run by the launcher, because the worker hook blocks `git checkout --` and a read-only gate cannot see a writer's log.
495. **009 T14: the generator's mutation sensitivity, verified by a runnable test.** The done-when asks that a deliberate C# change made and reverted locally makes at least one seed fail. A committed test `GeneratedCorpusReferenceIsPinned` pins the SHA-256 of `AstDump.Dump(SyntaxTree.Parse(...))` over the whole valid + corrupted corpus, so a C# change is seen as a seed failure without the self-hosted parser. Two changes were made and reverted: (a) in `AstDump.cs`, the `LiteralExpr` default case drops the literal's `Text` field — the pinned hash changed `59685440…` → `543C80D2…` and the test failed; (b) in `Parser.cs`, the `Synchronize()` call inside `RecoverIfNeeded` is moved ahead of its clean-restart guards (a moved recovery point, not a removal) — the hash changed `59685440…` → `F0D39D68…` and the test failed. Both were reverted and the test passed again. `GeneratedSeedsAgree` (the end-to-end comparison) still awaits T13's `--many` and T15's parity. New.
496. **009 T14: four node kinds are only reachable through a diagnostic, and the valid corpus still covers them.** `CastExpr` (`(T)x`, the input form), `EmptyStmt` (`;`), `ErrorStmt` (a stray `else`) and `ErrorExpr` (`()`) never occur in a clean parse. R7 says the valid corpus covers "every node kind", so the generator's one-template-per-type includes these four, each parsing to a complete tree with a single BYN1 diagnostic. *Current choice (conservative):* "valid" means assembled from a template, not token-corrupted, so the diagnostic-carrying templates belong in the valid corpus; `GeneratedSeedsAgree` compares dumps including diagnostics, so they are still checked end to end. New.
497. **009 T14: `GeneratedSeedsAgree` skips until `bayan-parse --many` lands.** The end-to-end comparison probes the built parser with `--many`; on the T1 stub the probe exits 2 (usage), so the test prints a skip line and returns. `EveryNodeRecordTypeIsInstantiatedByTheValidCorpus`, the determinism and the corruption tests and `GeneratedCorpusReferenceIsPinned` (the mutation-sensitivity proxy, Q495) all run now; full byte parity over the valid and corrupted corpora is T15's. New. Once T13 landed `--many`, the probe passed and the test ran against a parser still missing T7/T8, so it now carries the same `Skip` as `ParseGolden`/`DiagGolden` ("T15 enables once every parsing file has landed"); T15 removes it.

500. **009 T15: `OneMegabyteWithinTenTimes` and the `--time` breakdown.** The input is `SelfhostParserGenerator.OneMegabyte()` (T14's generator, swapped in here). Median of 5: `bayan-parse` 50,882,000 ns, C# `SyntaxTree.Parse` + `AstDump.Dump` 188,772,500 ns, ratio **0.27** (passes, ≤ 10). `bayan-parse --time` on the same 1 MB input also prints the per-phase breakdown on stderr (`lex … parse … dump …`, added this milestone): lex 4,895,000 ns, parse 29,727,000 ns, dump 19,717,000 ns (total 54,339,000 ns, one run). New.

501. **009 T15: hard-coded per-task expectations corrected to C#, not stubs.** The run-2 changes to `SelfhostParserT3Tests` and `SelfhostParserT10Tests` replace values that the deleted `struct T3` stand-ins had pinned (`shiftOperand`/`rangeOperand` returned `.none` without consuming, Q441). C# justifies each new value: `.percentOff when` → `const pos 2` because `ParsePrimaryPattern` falls through to `ParseBinary(Prec.Range)`, which consumes the `.percentOff` target-member expression; `< 3` → `(rel lt) pos 2` because `ParseBinary(Prec.Shift)` consumes `3`; `pattern Foo` → `pattern @2` because `ParsePatternExpr` → `ParsePattern` → `ParseBinary(Prec.Range)` consumes `Foo`. New.

502. **009 T15: `GeneratedSeedsAgree` span-check lines are Bayan-only.** `--many` appends `span out of range:` lines from `checkSpans` (L018, "New code, no C# counterpart"), which `AstDump.Dump` never emits, so a corrupted corpus whose C# `ErrorExpr` span falls outside its parent's span (e.g. `x = ` dropped its value) would otherwise fail byte parity. The test now compares the dump up to the first `span out of range:` line and ignores the remainder, and iterates in `Io.listDir` byte order (the corpus is sorted by `StringComparer.Ordinal`). New.

503. **009 T15: dump reconstruction of C# names a `TextSpan` cannot hold.** `dump.byn`/`dump2.byn` rebuild the C# `Name.Text` the parser stores only as a span: a one-segment `NamedType` without args goes through `cSharpTypeName` and `char` → `rune`; a zero-length name prints `<missing>` (`nameText`); a name-first function's implicit return is `void` (checked in the function head against the name span); a `rest T… xs`/`T[] xs` parameter is `ReadOnlySpan<T>` (a one-name `NamedType` whose name span starts at its element and extends past it); a compact format spec's name is `as`/`digits` (source `:`); a bracket attribute prints its camelCase name (its span starts at `[`). New.

504. **009 T15: break-test record.** Broke the O3 split at `selfhost/parser/decls2.byn:204` by replacing `if rule.at is null { own.append(move rule) } else { structRules.append(move rule) }` with an unconditional `own.append(move rule)`; `SelfhostParserGeneratorTests.GeneratedSeedsAgree` failed (1 of 1) on `valid-RequiresRule.byn` (the field's `at .password` rule stayed on the field). Restored from `tmp/scratch/decls2-backup.byn` with `cmp` clean; the rerun passed. New.

505. **009 T16: L017's random corpus found the diagnostic word-wrap bug.** With diagnostics rendered at width 100, C# `DiagnosticRenderer.Wrap` (`src/Bayan.Syntax/Diagnostics/DiagnosticRenderer.cs:206`) treats backticked code as one word, but `wrap` in `selfhost/lexer/diagnostics.byn:205` splits at every space, including inside backticks, so a diagnostic whose prose holds multi-word code can break inside it: a `parse/`-derived random input makes the actual dump break `… is an input form; write i64 -> bool fails` where C# keeps the code whole. L017 does not drop such inputs wholesale: it counts a dump that differs only in line wrapping and compares everything else, so 2047 of 2048 inputs are compared under each seed (1 wrapping-only input in seed A, `9E3779B97F4A7C15-01150`, and 1 in seed B, `0123456789ABCDEF-01378`). The fix is to make `wrap`'s word splitter skip spaces inside backticks, as the C# `Words` does. New.

506. **009 T16: the C# reference throws on Q486 inputs, and the Bayan port panics on one of them.** Four random candidates (1 seed A, 3 seed B) make `SyntaxTree.Parse`/`AstDump.Dump` throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` from `SourceText.GetText` — via `Parser.ReportBraceless` (the Q486 bug at `Parser.cs:2408`) or `DiagnosticRenderer.Render` — so L017 has no reference dump; `bayan-parse` exits 1 on three of them and panics `slice out of range` at `selfhost/lexer/source.byn:80` on `0123456789ABCDEF-01074` (exit 134). L017 and L018 both replace these candidates before `--many`, so the panic is outside both proofs until Q486's C# fix (or a bounds check in `getText`) lands; a run keeps the candidates under `tmp/l017/skipped/`. New.

508. **009 T18: the proof caps nesting because both parsers recurse unboundedly.** `SelfhostParserGenerator.NestingCap` is 8, and the random-byte corpus caps its `if true { ... }` nesting at the same depth. `Parser.cs` and the port have no nesting limit, so a deep input overflows the stack in both; the law proof excludes stack overflow and says so in the notes. *Current choice:* keep the shared unbounded recursion (a shared limit is a later spec); the proof stays within the cap. New.

509. **009 T18: L018 is false of C# on two counts, and the port keeps matching C#.** (a) Child-within-parent: `move`, `fail`, labeled `break`/`continue`, `except` and `?.` end before their child (Q473) and a dropped value's `ErrorExpr` sits outside its parent (work/todo.md); over the proof corpora this is 28 of 128 corrupted and 1,056 of 4,000 random inputs, each verified against a C# tree walker in the test. The 28 corrupted inputs are `corrupt-valid-AssignStmt.byn`, `corrupt-valid-BecauseClause.byn`, `corrupt-valid-BinaryPattern.byn`, `corrupt-valid-CatchExpr.byn`, `corrupt-valid-CollectionExpr.byn`, `corrupt-valid-ErrorExpr.byn`, `corrupt-valid-ErrorVariant.byn`, `corrupt-valid-FieldInit.byn`, `corrupt-valid-ForStmt.byn`, `corrupt-valid-ImportDecl.byn`, `corrupt-valid-IncDecStmt.byn`, `corrupt-valid-LabeledStmt.byn`, `corrupt-valid-MapEntryExpr.byn`, `corrupt-valid-PropertySubpattern.byn`, `corrupt-valid-RelationalPattern.byn`, `corrupt-valid-SwitchArm.byn`, `corrupt-valid-SwitchLabel.byn`, `corrupt-valid-TargetMemberExpr.byn`, `corrupt-valid-TypeAliasDecl.byn`, `corrupt-valid-VarPattern.byn`, `corrupt-valid-WhileLetStmt.byn`, `corrupt-valid-seed-000.byn`, `corrupt-valid-seed-001.byn`, `corrupt-valid-seed-002.byn`, `corrupt-valid-seed-003.byn`, `corrupt-valid-seed-004.byn`, `corrupt-valid-seed-005.byn`, `corrupt-valid-seed-007.byn`. The 1,056 random inputs are listed in `docs/laws/018-no-parser-panic.md` (*Counterexample inputs*) (one `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 <index>` per line, sorted; first ten: `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00010`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00013`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00020`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00026`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00027`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00031`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00035`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00041`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00042`, `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 00043`). (b) No-panic: two random candidates crash C#'s `Parser.ReportBraceless` (`ArgumentOutOfRangeException`) and the port panics identically (`slice out of range` at `lexer/source.byn:80`): `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 02184` and `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 02482` (bytes in the notes); the generator replaces a C#-crashing candidate with an empty input. *Current choice:* L018 stays `proposed`; the test proves no panic and C#-matching spans over the non-crashing corpus. New.

510. **009 T19: L018 is not enacted.** T18's notes (Q509) list C# counterexamples on both counts (child-within-parent spans, and two `Parser.ReportBraceless` crashes), so T19's own condition keeps the law `proposed`; enacting it would require changing the C# parser, which 009 does not own. *Current choice:* L018 stays `proposed` with its passing non-crashing-corpus proof; fixing the C# spans and crash is a todo for whoever owns the C# parser. New.
511. **009 review: three port spans differed from C#.** C# builds `NotPattern`, `VarPattern` and a block-bodied `PropertyDecl` with `SpanFrom(start)` evaluated before the operand, the name or the block (argument order), so each span stops before its last child; the port took the span after it, so L018's span walker missed the C# child-outside on `x is not null`. The L018 proof only checked that the port's reports were a subset of C#'s. *Current choice:* the port takes these spans in C#'s order, like the other early-span sites (Q473), and the proof checks per-file equality both ways; `SpanTakenBeforeTheLastChildLeavesItOutside` pins all three. New.

520. **010 T1: `public const` does not parse, so a module constant cannot be exported.** `public const answer: i64 = 42` is BYN1001 ("expected a declaration after the modifiers, found keyword `const`"), and an unmarked constant is BYN2005 from another module ("module constants are not visible outside their module"), so `nodes.byn`'s modifier bits (`modifierPublic` … `modifierUnsafe`) and every other parser constant stay private even though the checker reads them: `parser.modifierPublic` is the break-test's BYN2005. T1 made every parser struct, union, enum, type alias and struct field `public` instead (579 lines in `nodes.byn`, 19 in `parser.byn`). *Open, for whichever task first compares modifiers (T12/T38) or needs a parser code table:* either `ctx.byn` redeclares the bits it reads, or a `public` function returns them. T1 also made `parser.cSharpTypeName` `public` (`types.byn:162`): the port keeps source spans where the C# parser rewrites node text (`int` → `i32`, a `rest` parameter → `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, a missing return type → `void`, a lowercased attribute name), so semantics calls the helper rather than reading span text, as `dump.byn`/`dump2.byn` do when printing (Q475/Q503). New.
521. **010 T1: `SourceFile` gains `isTestFile` and the per-file imports.** The C# `FileContext` (`Symbols/Symbols.cs:69-80`) keeps the module, the tree, the source, a per-file `Imports` dictionary and `IsTestFile`; the plan's `SourceFile` list had no home for `IsTestFile` and put imports on `Mod`. Two files of one module can import different names in C# (`TypeResolver.cs:275`, `BinderExpressions.cs:542` and `:568` read `file.Imports`), so a module-wide map would let one file see a sibling's import. *Current choice:* `SourceFile` has `bool isTestFile` and `Map<string, ModId> imports`; `Mod` keeps only its name and files. New.
522. **010 T1: what parser visibility the checker's tests pin.** `ParserTypesArePublic` builds a scratch entry module (one in-memory `SourceText`, `Compilation.Create(…, packageRoot: selfhost/)`, so `import parser`/`import lexer` resolve, Q430) that names `parser.Parser.create`, `parser.parseCompilationUnit` and the type `parser.CompilationUnit`, and asserts no diagnostics; calling `parser.parseCompilationUnit` from a plain `main` needs no `uses alloc` at the call site, so the two `uses alloc` annotations the plan asks for cost the checker nothing. `PrivateParserSymbolIsNotVisible` names `parser.parseBlock` (a parser entry point the checker does not call, so it stayed private) and pins BYN2005 with `parseBlock` in the rendered message. *Open:* which further parser functions later semantics tasks call (the classification in `naming.byn`, `fold.byn` and `manifest.byn` may want the parser's own helpers rather than copies) is each task's to raise; T1 made only the types, fields and the three entry points public. New.
523. **010 T1: `Binder`'s tuple-typed collections compile verbatim.** `List<(FuncId, List<BExpr>)>`, `List<(i64, Type)>`, `List<(i64, LocalId, Type)>` and a `List<Map<string, LocalId>>` all parse and check (an unnamed tuple element type is legal inside `List<…>`, unlike a tuple-typed struct field, which BYN1001 reads as a function type), so no named structs were introduced and the plan's field types are kept as written. `List<string>? capabilities` and `Map<FileId, i64>` likewise. `enum WorkKind`'s first case is spelled `where` in the plan and in `ctx.byn`, and a keyword is legal as an enum case there (it is not, as a union case, Q437), so T11 should not rename it. New.
524. **010 T1: break-tests performed and restored.** (a) `selfhost/semantics/main.byn:7` `i32 main() => 0` changed to `=> 1`: `SelfhostSemanticsTests.MainReturnsZero` failed (exit 1 against 0); restored from `tmp/probe/main.bak` with `cmp` clean, and the rerun passed. (b) `selfhost/parser/decls.byn:12` lost `public` on `parseCompilationUnit`: `SelfhostSemanticsTests.ParserTypesArePublic` failed with BYN2005; restored from `tmp/probe/decls.bak` (`cmp` clean) and the rerun passed. With the parser edits in place: `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~SelfhostParser"` 270/270, `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~SelfhostSemanticsTests"` 4/4, `--filter "Law=L017|Law=L018"` 2/2. New.
525. **010 T2: the diagnostic table and renderer landed at ~1,380 Bayan lines, over the plan's ~1,250.** `codes.byn` is 816 lines (the 252 descriptors as three switch tables) and `diag.byn` 566 (`report`, `addDiag`, `pushBag`/`popBag`, `removeRepeats`, `render`/`renderAll`, plus private copies of the lexer's wrap, fix, display, UTF-8 and line helpers). The table was generated once from `DiagnosticCodes.cs` with a throwaway script under `tmp/` (not kept); every function was probe-compiled in `tmp/probe/t2e/` before it landed. *Current choice:* one serial writer as the task allows; Q526 records the signatures that had to change. New.
526. **010 T2: four signatures could not be written as the plan has them.** (a) `report`'s `TextSpan fixSpan = TextSpan { start: 0, length: 0 }` is BYN2219 (a parameter default must be a compile-time constant), so it is `TextSpan? fixSpan = null` and `report` unwraps with `fixSpan ?? TextSpan { start: 0, length: 0 }`. (b) Every required parameter after the object needs a particle (BYN5004/BYN5006), so: `void report(ref Ctx c, for SemaCode code, from FileId f, at TextSpan span, by (string a0, string a1, string a2, string a3, string a4) args, string label = "", string help = "", bool hasFix = false, TextSpan? fixSpan = null, string fixReplacement = "")`; `void addDiag(ref Ctx c, by move Diag d)`; `void popBag(ref Ctx c, to i64 previous)`; `string render(in Ctx c, for in Diag d, by bool includePath)`; `string renderAll(in Ctx c, from in List<Diag> diags, by bool includePath, until i64 errorLimit, to ref i64 omitted)`. (c) `render`/`renderAll` take `in Ctx`, not `ref Ctx`: `renderAll(ref c, from: c.diagnostics, …)` is BYN3005 (`c` is passed by `ref` and again in the same call) and every render call site is exactly that pair; two shared borrows compile. Call sites: `report(ref c, for: .x, from: f, at: span, by: args)`, `addDiag(ref c, by: d)`, `renderAll(in c, from: in c.diagnostics, by: …, until: …, to: ref omitted)`. New.
527. **010 T2: 252 descriptors, and three of them are not in `DiagnosticCodes.All`.** `DiagnosticCodes.cs` has 325 declarations; 249 carry a BYN2000–BYN8999 code and 246 of those are registered (the task's 259 matches no count I could derive; 249 in range plus the three BYN1 codes is 252). The three unregistered ones are second message forms built with `new(...)` and "registered once, as" their sibling: `ConversionMember` (BYN5009, reported by `Naming.cs:120`), `BecomeOtherState` and `BecomesCallUndeclared` (BYN7003, reported by `Binding/BinderStates.cs:41` and `:57`). *Current choice:* the port carries all 252 so T7 and T22 can report those messages; `CodeTableMatchesDiagnosticCodes` and `FormatMatchesStringFormat` compare the `DiagnosticCodes.All` entries in order and fetch the three extras by reflection at their declared positions (right after the registered descriptor with the same code). New.
528. **010 T2: display paths sort by UTF-8 bytes, not UTF-16 code units.** `DiagnosticRenderer.Sort` uses `StringComparer.Ordinal` on `SourceText.Path`, which orders UTF-16 code units; `pathLess` in `diag.byn` compares UTF-8 bytes. They agree for ASCII and differ only where a path mixes a supplementary scalar (U+10000 and above) with U+E000–U+FFFF (UTF-16 puts the surrogate pair first, UTF-8 the BMP character); no `tests/cases/diag` path is non-ASCII. *Current choice:* keep the byte comparison and record it rather than decode to code points in the sort. New.
529. **010 T2: break-tests performed and restored.** (a) `selfhost/semantics/diag.byn:272` swapped `severityName`'s `"warning"`/`"error"`: `EveryDiagCaseRendersLikeCSharp` failed. (b) `diag.byn:219` changed `errors > errorLimit` to `>=`: `ErrorLimitCapsErrorsNotWarnings` failed. (c) `diag.byn:65` dropped `d.message` from the `removeRepeats` key: `RemoveRepeatsMatchesCSharp` failed. (d) `diag.byn:461` counted two lines per newline in `lineIndex`: `EveryDiagCaseRendersLikeCSharp` failed. (e) `diag.byn:397` removed the backtick toggle in `splitWords`: `EveryDiagCaseRendersLikeCSharp` failed (the C# `Words` keeps backticked code whole). (f) `diag.byn:368` used `widths.first` for every wrapped line: it survived at first because no golden message wraps past its first line, so a synthetic long-message diagnostic was added to `EveryDiagCaseRendersLikeCSharp` and the mutation then failed. Each was restored from `tmp/t2/diag.bak` (`cmp` clean) and the rerun passed; the guard then ran 8 further mutations of `diag.byn` (8/8 killed). New.
