530. **010 T3: size and the two-file split.** `symbols.byn` (815 lines: every `Symbols.cs` class plus `AliasPlaceholder` and `TypeParam`) and `types.byn` (~900 lines: `Types.cs`, `typeDisplay`, `typeEquals`, interning, `range` over `Big`) plus the `ctx.byn` additions total ~2,100 lines, over the plan's ~1,720 because each symbol struct carries its full field set and every function takes `ref Ctx c` plus a particle (Q532). The two-file split is kept as the plan accepts for one serial writer. New.
531. **010 T3: the `of`/`indexOf` renames and the keyword-forced renames.** The plan's `of` is `errorUnionOf` and `indexOf` is `tupleIndexOf` (the plan's Q531). Bayan keywords forced more: `never` → `PrimitiveKind.neverKind`; `fails`/`uses`/`enum`/`union` are not usable as field or parameter names, so `FunctionSymbol.fails` became `hasFails`, `FunctionData.fails`/`uses` became `errorSets`/`effects`, and `EnumFieldSymbol.Enum`/`EnumMemberSymbol.Enum`/`UnionVariantSymbol.Union` became `owner` (each in its own arena, so the name is unambiguous); `FunctionSymbol` drops the C# `uses` list because it is `.Decl` syntax re-read through `declIndex`. New.
532. **010 T3: every function after the unlabeled `ref Ctx c` needs a particle.** BYN5004/BYN5006 reject two unlabeled non-`bool` parameters, so the plan's `typeDisplay(ref Ctx c, Type t)`-shaped signatures each take a particle: `by:` for the operand handle/type, `for:` for a name, `to:`/`at:`/`as:`/`for in:` for the rest — `makeType(TypeKind kind, at i64 index)`, `internMap(… by Type key, to Type value)`, `internTuple(… for in List<TupleField> fields)`, `internFunction(… for in List<Type> parameters, to Type ret, by in List<ErrorSetId> errorSets, as in List<string> effects)`, `internState(… by StructId s, for in List<VariantId> states)`, `errorUnionOf(… for in List<ErrorSetId> sets, as in List<VariantId> excluded)`. Later tasks call those labels. New.
533. **010 T3: enum ordinals are `i32`, and three C# habits have no direct spelling.** (a) `enum.ordinal` returns an `i32`, so `kind.ordinal << 32` wraps to a shift by zero and every constructed type collapsed onto its first part; `makeType` casts first, `(i64(kind.ordinal) << 32) | index`. `kindOf` is a `switch t >> 32` over the 25 ordinals and `primKindOf`/`textViewKindOf`/`builtinKindOf` do the reverse, because `TypeKind(x)` and `i64(enum)` are BYN2220/BYN2206. (b) `List` has no `contains`, so `listContains`/`listContainsString` walk in order (Q449). (c) enums cannot compare with `<`/`<=`, so the integer predicates use the raw ordinal (`isInteger` is `typeIndex` 0..9). (d) the borrow checker forbids `ref c` and `in c.field` in one call (BYN3005), so display/computed functions copy scalar fields into locals and member lists into `copyIds`/`copyStrings` before any `ref Ctx` call. New.
534. **010 T3: the oracle builds symbols by hand, and what the five tests pin.** `SelfhostSemanticsT3Tests` reconstructs the symbols with the `Builtins` pattern (`SyntaxTree.Parse` of a one-declaration source → `StructSymbol`/`EnumSymbol`/`UnionSymbol`/`ErrorSetSymbol`/`InterfaceSymbol`) rather than reading them from a `Compilation`, because `DisplayName`/`Equals`/`IsValidKey` are identical either way and manual construction keeps names/modules/tags/codes in lockstep with the generated `main.byn`; `QualifyModules` is toggled by reflection (it is `internal [ThreadStatic]`). 183 types (every primitive, `error`, `null`, every text view and builtin, 12 named types, one/two/three-level constructed types, and a type-parameter leaf in each constructed kind so `occurs`'s true path is covered) print `typeDisplay` in both qualify modes; 28 interning pairs, the ranges/byName/bits/predicates, and the keys/occurs/isBorrow/invalidKeyPart walk compare against `MapType.IsValidKey`/`InvalidKeyPart`, `TypeParameterType.Occurs`, `TypeSymbol.IsBorrow` and `TupleType.IndexOf`; 666 printed lines. `joinIds` is observed directly (the guard's first surviving mutant was its comma separator, which the intern keys alone could not see). Break-tests: `types.byn` `case .char: return "rune"` → `"runeX"` failed `PrimitiveRangesMatchCSharp`; `case .optional: return occurs(…)` → `false` failed `KeysAndOccursMatchCSharp`; `internOptional` key `string(inner)` → `"x"` failed `InterningIsCanonical`; `symbols.byn` `findField` early `return -1` failed `SymbolLookupsMatchCSharp`. New.
535. **010 T4: kind, field and constructor names, and what the structs add.** `BoundKind` lists the 74 `BoundNodes.cs` records in file order, then `methodGroup`, `variantGroup`, `builtinGroup` (the `internal` records of `BinderExpressions.cs`, in that file's order): 77 kinds. Keyword names take a suffix: `defaultValue`, `thisRef`, `withExpr`, `isExpr`, `moveExpr`, `tryExpr`, `catchExpr`, `returnStmt`, `failStmt`, `becomeStmt`, `breakStmt`, `continueStmt`, `ifStmt`, `whileStmt`, `forStmt`, `switchStmt`, `deferStmt`, `assertStmt`, `errdeferStmt`, `contextStmt`. Structs keep the C# record name (`BIf`, `BDefault`), so constructors are `add<Struct>` (`addIf`, `addThis`). Keyword field names: `struct` → `structId`, `enum` → `enumId`, `const` → `constId`, `else` → `elseBranch`, `never` → `isNever`, `property` → `propertyId`, C# `Syntax` → `TextSpan span`. Structs whose C# `Type` is computed from a symbol (`BLocal`, `BField`, `BStructLiteral`, `BWith`, `BMove`, `BErrorVariant`, `BEnumMember`, `BUnionNew`, `BStaticArray`, `BUnionField`, `BErrorField`) carry a trailing `Type type` the constructor fills; the constant-typed kinds (`symbolLiteral`, `errorExpr`, `jump`, `isExpr`, `interpolated`, …) have no field and `exprType` returns the C# constant. `UserIteration.Advance`/`Item` are `Symbol` witnesses, so they are `FuncId advance`/`item` plus `FieldId advanceField`/`itemField`; `StructRule` adds `List<FieldId> reads`. `BMethodGroup.TypeArgs` (`TypeSyntax[]`) is kept as `List<TextSpan> typeArgs`; T28 re-reads the syntax by span if a caller needs it. `BoundExpr.Constant` is not a field: it lives in `Ctx.constants` keyed by handle (`exprConstant`/`setConstant`). Jump targets are `i64` indexes into `Ctx.jumpTargets`. New.
536. **010 T4: `Constant` and `constantText`.** `ConstantKind` is `integer`, `real`, `flag`, `text`, `rune` (`float` and `bool`-as-case read badly; `float` is reserved). `constantText` matches `ConstantValue.ToString()` under the invariant culture: `bigText` for integers, `true`/`false`, the string in quotes without escaping, the rune as its character, and `realText` for doubles, which re-lays Bayan's shortest digits the .NET way (exponent form `1E+17`/`1E-05` when the decimal exponent is at least 17 or below -4, two-digit minimum exponent, `-0`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`, `NaN`). C#'s output is culture-dependent (`∞` under en-US ICU), so the test pins the invariant culture. New.
537. **010 T4: the syntax facts the binder reads from bound nodes.** Bound nodes hold a span, not syntax, so the four `Syntax is …` sites become flags in `Ctx.syntaxFlags` keyed by handle (`setSyntaxFlags`/`syntaxFlags`/`hasSyntax`): `syntaxLiteral` (BinderExpressions.cs:94, :1496 `LiteralExpr`), `syntaxUnary` (:1496 `UnaryExpr`), `syntaxUntypedLiteral` (:249 `IsUntypedLiteral`), `syntaxDiscard` (BinderCalls.cs:1590 `DiscardPattern`). BinderCalls.cs:120-122, Particles.cs:24 and Compilation.cs:674-677 read a parameter `LocalSymbol.Syntax`, not a bound node, so they need no flag. Lowering has no `Syntax is` test but reads `e.Syntax` at Lowerer.cs:1033, 1265, 1308, 1369 (`((CallExpr)call.Syntax).Callee is MemberExpr`), 1397 (`IsLiteral(e.Syntax)`), 1494, 1543, 1643; whoever ports lowering adds flags for those. New.
538. **010 T4: `for:` instead of `of:`, and where `StructChecks` lives.** `of` is not a particle (BYN5008), so the walk is `children(in Ctx c, for BNode n)`, `descendants(in c, for:)`, `exprType(in c, for:)`, `nodeSpan(in c, for:)`, `patternInput(in c, for:)`. `Compilation.Checks` (`Dictionary<StructSymbol, StructChecks>`, Compilation.cs:1120) is `Ctx.checks: List<StructChecks>` plus `Ctx.checksOf: Map<StructId, i64>` into it. `boundKind` of a `-1` handle is `.errorExpr` (`fromOrdinal` returns `BoundKind?`); callers test `-1` first. New.
539. **010 T4: the symbol fields that hold bound nodes.** Appended to `symbols.byn`: `FieldSymbol.defaultValue: BExpr`, `FunctionSymbol.body: BStmt` and `requirements: List<BExpr>` (`requires` is a keyword in a struct body, BYN1004), `LocalSymbol.constant: Constant?` and `defaultValue: BExpr` (C# `ParameterSymbol.Default`, parameters being locals here), `ConstSymbol.value: Constant?`, `bound: BExpr` and `elements: List<Constant>`, `EnumMemberSymbol.values: List<Constant?>`. Two follow C# rather than the plan: `ConstSymbol.Elements` is `ConstantValue[]`, not a list of bound expressions, and `EnumMemberSymbol.Values` is `ConstantValue?[]`. New.
540. **010 T5: Bayan has no `i128`, so `Big` stands in, and three C# cases have no direct spelling.** `ctx.byn` declares `struct Big { u64 lo; u64 hi }` (two's-complement, `hi`'s top bit is the sign) and `struct BigParse { Big value; bool ok; bool overflow }`; every `Int128` result the C# folds is a `Big` here. Unrepresentable or changed cases, all owned by `bigint.byn`: (a) C# `Int128` arithmetic is unchecked, so `a + b` wraps; Bayan's plain `+ - *` trap, so the file uses `+% -% *%` and a compare-before-subtract carry (`s < a ? 1 : 0`) everywhere. (b) C# `Int128.MinValue / -1` throws `OverflowException` and `% -1` throws too; *current choice:* `bigDiv(MIN, -1)` wraps to `MIN` and `bigRem(MIN, -1)` is 0 (two's-complement truncation), the test's oracle special-cases the two. (c) `ConstantFolding.Wrap` uses `1 << type.Bits`, which for a 128-bit type would be inexpressible, but the port only ever asks for widths 8/16/32/64 (`PrimitiveType.Range`); `bigWrap`, `bigFits`, `bigSaturate`, `bigMin` and `bigMax` therefore take a width and treat anything else as caller error. Bayan also rejects the plan's unlabeled signatures: BYN5004/BYN5006 require a particle on every required non-`bool` parameter after the object (Q431/Q441), so the second operand is labeled `as:` for comparison (`bigCmp`, `bigEq`), `by:` for arithmetic, bitwise and shift operations (`bigAdd`, `bigSub`, `bigMul`, `bigDiv`, `bigRem`, `bigAnd`, `bigOr`, `bigXor`, `bigShl`, `bigShr`), and `to:` for a width (`bigFits`, `bigWrap`, `bigSaturate`); `bigMin(i64 bits, bool signed)` and `bigMax` keep no particle because `bool` parameters are exempt (BYN2305 still names them at the call site). Later tasks call those labels. New.
541. **010 T5: `bigParse`'s three outcomes, and what `literalDecimalText` promises.** `bigParse` strips `_` anywhere (C# `ParseInteger`'s `Replace("_", "")`), reads an `0x`/`0X` or `0b`/`0B` prefix case-insensitively, validates each digit against the base (`0b102` is a bad digit, hex accepts `a`–`f`/`A`–`F`), and reports `ok=false` for an empty digit run, an empty string or a bad digit. Above 2^127-1 it reports `ok=true, overflow=true` and leaves `value` at the last in-range accumulator (the plan says "unspecified"); it detects the crossing by dividing `(2^127-1 - digit)` by the base before accumulating, so no wrapping product can hide it. C# `BigInteger.Parse("ZZ", …)` would throw `FormatException` (`0xZZ` cannot be spelled as a diagnostic value), so `ok=false` stands in; `literalDecimalText` is defined only for a well-formed literal, the out-of-range message path, and on a malformed one it returns the value of the digits it could read (`0xZZ` → `0`), which no caller reads because `ok` is false. New.
542. **010 T5: how division, decimal text, and the two float conversions work.** Unsigned 128/128 division is a bit-at-a-time long division from bit 127 down (128 rounds, subtract when the remainder compares `>=` the divisor); `bigDiv`/`bigRem` take magnitudes, divide, and reapply the sign (`bigDiv` truncates toward zero, `bigRem` takes the sign of `a`, so both match C# `Int128`). The remainder is `a - q*b` by wrapping `bigMul`, exact because `q*b <= a`. `bigText` and `bigParse`'s overflow limit use `bigUDivSmall`, which divides by 32-bit limbs (`r * 2^32 + limb` stays under 2^64 for `d < 2^32`) instead of the 128-round loop, one limb per decimal digit. `bigToF64` rounds to nearest-even from the top 53 bits plus the leftover bits, then scales the exact 53-bit integer by a power of two (C# `(double)Int128`); `bigFromF64` splits `|d|` at 2^64, converts each half with 32-bit `i64` conversions (an `i64(f64)` truncates toward zero), and negates the magnitude, so the caller's clamp is the only range check, as in `ConstantFolding.Cast`; the `d != d` NaN guard is defensive and unreachable from the test, because `Cast` maps NaN to zero before the conversion and the generated program has no NaN literal. The oracle skips `bigToF64` on 2^127-1, where C# `(Int128)(double)` overflows after rounding to 2^127. New.
543. **010 T5: the test's generated module and what it compares.** `SelfhostSemanticsT5Tests` writes a `main.byn` in memory at `selfhost/semantics/main.byn` (not just `main.byn`): a directory is a module, so the generated `main` must sit in the semantics module to see the module-private `Big` functions (Q521's per-file facts do not widen function visibility). It builds every other `selfhost/semantics/*.byn` plus that source once per class (`Lazy`, `Compilation.Create(…, packageRoot: selfhost/)`, `Toolchain.Build`) and compares the printed lines section by section: 47 boundary operands (0, ±1, the i8/i16/i32/i64 extremes and their neighbours, the unsigned maxima and their successors, 2^63, 2^64-1, 2^64, 2^100+1, 2^127-1, -2^127) each printing negate, not, `bigFromU64` of the low half, `bigToI64`/`bigFromI64` when the value fits, and `fits`/`wrap`/`sat`/`min`/`max` for 8/16/32/64 × signed/unsigned; then 84 pairs (one per operand against `(i*7+3)` mod the list, 24 from `new Random(510)`, and 13 fixed division and shift corners) printing `p`, add, sub, mul, div, rem, and, or, xor, cmp, eq, and `shl`/`shr` at 0, 1, 63, 64 and 127; then 21 literal cases and 18 float cases: 3,953 expected lines (the test asserts at least 1,500). The expected text is `Int128.ToString()` (or `BigInteger.ToString()` for the literals) and the first differing line is reported with its case number and output line. The first cut computed the operations section's length before emitting the pairs, so none of the pair lines were compared; break-test (a) below found it and the boundary moved after the pair loop. New.
544. **010 T5: break-tests performed and restored; the guard reverts an uncommitted file.** (a) `selfhost/semantics/bigint.byn:172` `hi: hi +% carry` → `hi: hi` (addition loses its carry): `OperationsMatchInt128` failed (this also exposed Q543's section-boundary bug), restored from `tmp/t5/bigint.good` (`cmp` clean) and the rerun passed. (b) `bigint.byn:374` `if c > 0 || (c == 0 && …)` → `if c > 1 || …` (drop the round-up branch): `FloatConversionsMatchCSharp` failed on the `bigToF64` of 2^64-1. (c) `bigint.byn:67` `bigCmp(acc, as: limit) > 0` → `> 1` (raise the overflow threshold): `LiteralsMatchBigInteger` failed on the 2^127 literal. (d) `bigint.byn:107` `… * base + carry` → `… * base + carry + 1` (decimal limb arithmetic): `LiteralsMatchBigInteger` failed on `42`. Every restore reran the filter to green. *Open:* `tmp/guard/guard.sh:60` restores a mutated file with `git checkout -- "$f"`, and `bigint.byn` was uncommitted, so running the guard after a green pass wiped the whole file to its one-line HEAD header; it was rebuilt from the recorded patches and backed up to `tmp/t5/bigint.good` before the next run. The dispatcher should commit (or copy aside) before running the guard. New.
545. **010 T6: the private helpers in `conversions.byn` and `fold.byn`.** All `t6`-prefixed. `conversions.byn`: `struct T6Unique { Type part; string why }` is `TypeFacts.Find`'s `(TypeSymbol Part, string Why)`; `t6Find(ref c, for: t, through: ref seen)` is `Find` (C#'s `HashSet<TypeSymbol> seen` is a `List<Type>` of the struct and union handles already walked); `t6Held(ref c, for: outer, by: inner)` is `Held`. `fold.byn`: `t6Integer`/`t6Real`/`t6Flag(flag:)` build a `Constant` of one kind (a `bool` argument must be named, BYN2305); `t6Wrap(n, as: type)` is `ConstantFolding.Wrap` over T5's `bigWrap`; `t6RealOrder(a, as: b)` is `double.CompareTo` (NaN below every number, equal to itself); `t6Compare(op, by: order, equal:)` is the shared comparison tail; `t6IntegerOp(op, from: a, by: b, as: type)` is the `Int128` arm of `Binary`. New.
546. **010 T6: null results and the `unique` modifier.** C#'s `TypeSymbol?` results are a `Type` with -1 for null (`common`, `uniquePart`), as everywhere in the selfhost. `implicitFunction` returns null for a target that is not a function type (C# takes a `FunctionType` parameter, so the case cannot arise there). `evaluate` takes `by in Map<FieldId, Constant> fields`; C#'s nullable `fields` is an empty map. `parser.modifierUnique` is a module constant and not visible outside `parser` (BYN2005), so `t6Find` tests `StructSymbol.modifiers & 64` with a comment naming it; T28 may want the parser to export the modifier bits. New.
547. **010 T6: `foldCast` to `f32` rounds twice.** C# converts `Int128` straight to `float`; `foldCast` does `f64(f32(bigToF64(n)))`, Int128 → double → float. The two can differ for an integer above 2^53 whose double rounding lands exactly halfway between two floats (by reasoning, for example 2^60 + 2^36 + 1, where the double drops the +1 and the float then rounds the tie to even, down to 2^60, while the direct conversion rounds up to 2^60 + 2^37; this case is not confirmed by a test). The test's seeded values do not hit such a case, so `CastFoldingMatchesCSharp` passes. Exact behaviour needs a `bigToF32` in `bigint.byn` (T5's file), which T6 does not own. Open.
548. **010 T6: test shape and break-tests.** `SelfhostSemanticsT6Tests` generates one `main.byn` that rebuilds the oracle's symbols by hand (6 structs incl. a `unique struct`, a self-referential struct and a conformer; 2 unions; 2 error sets; an interface, 2 type parameters; 9 functions) and 70 types, then prints 8 sections compared line for line with C#: `prims` (isWidening/implicit/explicit/common over the 17 primitives), `pairs` (implicit, implicit as argument, explicit, common over every type pair), `functions`, `unique`, `unary`, `binary`, `cast` and `evaluate` (36 hand-built trees). `ConstantFolding` is `internal`, so the oracle calls it by reflection. Break-tests, each failing its test then passing after `cp` restore: `conversions.byn:108` `ab < 64` → `ab <= 64` (PrimitiveConversionsMatchCSharp); `conversions.byn:93` `> 0` → `>= 0` (FunctionConversionsMatchCSharp); `conversions.byn:204` `!= 0` → `== 0` (UniquenessMatchesCSharp); `conversions.byn:70` `==` → `!=` (ConversionsMatchCSharp); `fold.byn:34` drop `bigNot` (UnaryFoldingMatchesCSharp); `fold.byn:117` `< 0` → `<= 0` (BinaryFoldingMatchesCSharp); `fold.byn:225` NaN → 1 (CastFoldingMatchesCSharp); `fold.byn:144` `!= .thisRef` → `== .thisRef` (EvaluateMatchesCSharp). New.
550. **010 T7: casing is ASCII-only.** C# `Naming` uses `char.IsUpper`/`IsLower`/`ToUpperInvariant`/`ToLowerInvariant`, which case any Unicode letter. `naming.byn` works on bytes: `isUpperAscii` (`A`–`Z`), `isLowerAscii` (`a`–`z`), `isDigitAscii`, `lowerAscii`/`upperAscii`/`capitalize` touch only those bytes, and every other byte (including each byte of a multi-byte letter) is uncased and stays with the word it follows in `wordSpans`. Identifiers that differ only in non-ASCII casing (`Éclair` as a type name, `éclair` as a value) can therefore get a different BYN2008/BYN2009 verdict and suggestion from C#; the test's `type-uncased` case (`café_shop`) agrees because the non-ASCII letter sits mid-word. Byte offsets equal C#'s `char` offsets only for ASCII names. *Current choice:* ASCII; a Unicode case table belongs to a later spec. Open.
551. **010 T7: where the manifest grammar comes from, and its dependence on T10.** `checkMembers` calls `grammarOf(ref c)`, which finds the `c.files` entry whose `displayPath` is `package.byn`, parses it with `manifestParse` (T10, still a stub returning an empty manifest) and lowercases its words with `lowerGrammar`; it is re-read on every `checkMembers` call (the plan's "merged per lookup"), not cached. C# reads `DisplayRoot/package.byn` from disk; if T28's driver does not add `package.byn` to `c.files`, the grammar is empty and only the built-in lexicon applies. C# `HashSet<string>` sets are `List<string>` here (duplicates harmless, lookup is linear). Because `manifestParse` is a stub, the test covers the file lookup through `packageFileIndex` and the grammar through `checkMembersWith(…, by: lowerGrammar(raw))` with a `Grammar` built from C# `Manifest.Read`, not through `grammarOf`. Open.
552. **010 T7: `checkParticles` is a new entry point with no API-index line.** `void checkParticles(ref Ctx c, from FileId f, for FuncId fn)` ports `Particles.Check` (BYN5004, BYN5006, BYN5013). It reads parameter syntax (particle span, name span, default, `rest`) from the tree through the function's `declIndex`/`memberIndex` rather than from `LocalSymbol`s, which carry no spans; for a constructor it reports at `nameSpan` (C# uses the constructor's `Location`) and uses the owner struct's name. It returns at once for templates (`template >= 0`) and `extern` functions (modifier bit 128). The caller (C# calls it from `DeclareParameters`, owned by the declare task) must call it after the parameters are declared; T28 should add it to `010-api.md`. Constructors are not exercised by the test. Open.
553. **010 T7: private helper names and the lexicon call.** `naming.byn` adds unprefixed module-level helpers (`toPascal`, `toCamel`, `capitalize`, `wordSpans`, `WordSpan`, `lowerAscii`, `upperAscii`, `isUpperAscii`, `isLowerAscii`, `isDigitAscii`, `trimDigits`, `bases`, `isVowel`, `typeSyntaxSpan`, `paramFacts`, `ParamFacts`, …); none clashes with another semantics file today, but a sibling landing the same name would collide at T28. Every string read from `c` (`getText` of a span, a symbol's `name`) is copied with `$"{…}"` before a `report(ref c, …)` call (BYN3004/BYN3005, as in Q455/Q475). `buildLexicon` is idempotent (it returns when `lexiconVerbs` is non-empty) and `checkMembersWith` calls it itself, so no driver ordering is needed. New.
554. **010 T7: what the test compares, and break-tests.** `SelfhostSemanticsT7Tests` generates one main: 11 BYN50xx/51xx goldens from `tests/cases/diag/`, an `extra` source (participle stems, `to`/`as` conversions, `try`/`fails`, bool states, particles), `grammar-dictionary` with its `package.byn`, and 23 casing names over type, interface and value declarations. The C# side runs a full `Compilation` and filters `main.byn` diagnostics by code; the Bayan side rebuilds the structs, methods, properties and parameters from the C# symbols and calls `checkMembersWith`/`checkParticles`/`checkType`/`checkInterface`/`checkValue`. Lines are `code start+length message | label | help | fix` with byte offsets, both sides sorted, each section ending in `end` so a clean case still compares. `LexiconIsBuiltOnce` compares counts and sampled entries with `Lexicon`. `PackageFileIsFound` checks `packageFileIndex` (-1 without a `package.byn`, its index with one). Break-tests (line numbers as committed; each restored from `tmp/naming.byn.bak`, `cmp` clean, filter green after): `naming.byn:500` `b <= 0x5A` → `0x59` survived the first suite, so `type-z` (`ZZTop`) and `value-z` were added, after which `CasingMatchesCSharp(type-z)` failed; `:206` negated `isThingNoun` → `noun-on-mutator`, `extra` failed; `:601` `a1: text` → `a1: fnName` → `repeated-particle`, `extra` failed. The guard's first run left three survivors, each now covered: the `package.byn` test in `grammarOf` (moved into `packageFileIndex`, `:353` `==` → `!=` → `PackageFileIsFound` failed), `:401` the three-letter-stem `w` exclusion (`hoped`/`towed` added, `extra` failed), `:531` `isAllLowerLetters` (`md5sum` added, `extra` failed); the second run's survivor, `:343` `if i < 0` → `if i >= 0` in `grammarOf`, is now caught by `PackageFileIsFound` calling `grammarOf` without a `package.byn` (the mutant indexes `files[-1]` and the generated main traps, failing every section). New.
555. **010 T8: an alias is a `Type` of kind word 25.** `TypeKind` has no alias case (ordinals 0–24, `kindOf` maps ≥ 24 to `.errorSet`), so the C# `AliasPlaceholder` in `Mod.types` is encoded as `t8AliasType(a) = (25 << 32) | a` and tested with `t8IsAlias`; `expand` is the only reader and returns the alias's `target`, resolving it once (BYN2011 at the alias name on a cycle). T11's `addType` must store aliases and `union error` compositions with `t8AliasType`, and nothing may call `kindOf` on an unexpanded alias. New.
556. **010 T8: the `CheckKey` closure is a `.keyCheck` work item, and members are never "declared" here.** C# `ResolveNamed` defers the map-key check of a struct or tuple key until `MembersDeclared` via a closure. Bayan has no closures, so `resolveMap` hands `afterMembersDeclared` a `Work { kind: .keyCheck, subject: key, file, span: <first type argument> }`, and T11's `runWork` should call `t8CheckKey(ref c, for: subject, from: file, at: span)` (`keyPartNotHashable` or `invalidMapKey`, the C# texts). `Ctx` has no `MembersDeclared` flag, so `t8MembersDeclared` is always false and every struct/tuple key is deferred; T11 should add the flag (or say a later resolution is always after members) and replace it. Until then the tests do not compare a struct or tuple key that is not a valid key. New.
557. **010 T8: `IoError`, `Utf8Error`, `ParseError` and `Rule` are found by name in a `<builtin>` file.** T9 exposes no entry point for the C# `Builtins.IoError`/`Utf8Error`/`ParseError`/`Rule`, so `t8BuiltinSet`/`t8BuiltinUnion` search `c.errorSets`/`c.unions` for that name declared in a file whose path is `<builtin>` (or with no file). T9 or T28 should replace them with T9's own lookups. Untested until T9 lands. New.
558. **010 T8: case handling is ASCII-only.** `char.IsLower` (the state-segment test in `Order.paid`) is `a`–`z`; `ToLowerInvariant` and `OrdinalIgnoreCase` in `suggestType` are `t8Lower` (A–Z only). `suggestType` walks `Mod.types` in Bayan `Map` order, which may differ from C# `Dictionary` key order when two module types differ only in case; the first match wins on both sides. New.
559. **010 T8: the other port cuts, and the break-tests.** C#'s `Binder` built for array sizes carries the resolver's type arguments, but the Bayan `Binder` has no such field, so `t8Binder` drops them. `goto case "Map"` is the helper `resolveMap`. `n with { Path = [n.Path[0]] }` (a state path's owner) is `construct(…, at: n.path[0])`: `construct` and `noTypeArgs` take the segment their diagnostics name. Passing `ref c` with an `in` borrow of a declaration in the same call is BYN3005, so `expand` and the test's `Probe` walk swap the `parser.Decl` out with `t8TakeDecl` and swap it back after. C# `AssociatedType` is `resolveAssociated` (T11 owns `associatedType`), and `Suggest` is `suggestType` (`suggest` exists in `express.byn`). Not compared, because the sibling stubs return defaults (statesOf, validationErrorOf, associatedType/associatedBinding, instantiateType, findInterface, bindArraySize, reportUnknown, functionTypeNotHere): state and refined types, `T.Field`, `ValidationError`/`Violation`, associated types, generic instantiation, array sizes, an unknown written effect, and the visibility of an alias (`accessOf` is a stub). Imported error sets, `checkVisible` on a set, and the `dyn` checks are compared (the `dyn` and `imports` fixtures register interfaces and a second module by hand; the C# side writes `geo/geo.byn` to a temp directory, because imports are read from disk). The oracle drops BYN2822/BYN3001 (struct field pass) and BYN6003 (effect analysis). Break-tests, each restored from `tmp/t8/typeresolve.orig` and rerun to green: `selfhost/semantics/typeresolve.byn:131` `== .optional` → `!= .optional`: `Named` and `Errors` failed; `:603` `!= set ||` → `== set ||` (composition exclusion): `Compose` failed; `:708` `if !listContainsString` → `if listContainsString` (effect dedup): `Named` and `Compose` failed; `:774` `"bool"` → `"boo"` (suggestion): `Compose` failed. New.
560. **010 T9: the builtins live in a lazily created `builtin` module, not a `Ctx` field.** ctx.byn (frozen after T4) has no `Builtins` field, so the first call to any builtins.byn entry point appends a module named `builtin` (cName `builtin`, directory `""`, no files) to `c.modules` (`t9Module`). Types sit in `mod.types` by their C# name (`Stream`, `Radix`, `Edge`, `Align`, `Comparison`, `LogLevel`, `IoError`, `Utf8Error`, `ValidationError`, `Rule`, `ParseError`, `Utf8Invalid`, `IEnumerator`, `IIndexable`) and functions in `mod.functions` by key: the plain name for `print`/`log`/`panic`/`todo`/`Owned`/`Untrusted`/`trust`/`Arena`, `Io.<name>`, `Utf8.decode`, `Utf8.tryDecode`, `Utf8.decode(invalid)`, `Hex.encode`, `Hex.decode`, `Symbol.intern`, `string.invalidUtf8At`, `StrBuf`, `StrBuf(buffer)`, `StrBuf.over` and `parse.<primitive>` (made and cached by `intParse`). Each parsed `"<builtin>"` source is a `SourceFile` whose `module` is the builtin module. Nothing is added to `allFunctions`, `enums` or the module's `files`, and symbol `modifiers` stay 0. As in C# Compilation, the declare pass still adds the error-set variants, the `Rule` variants and the interface members. T28 may move this into a `Ctx` field. New.
561. **010 T9: `names` takes the `Ctx` and filters as C# does.** The plan's `Ctx`-free `names(Type t)` could not see a list's element or an optional's inner type, so it over-approximated `joined`, `replace`, `sort` and `take`. *Resolved (dispatcher):* the signature is `List<string> names(ref Ctx c, for Type t)` (010-api.md updated), and a name is listed iff `builtinProperty` or `method` resolves it for `t`, as in `BuiltinMembers.Names`. T6's `isUnique` is a stub on this branch, so `method` uses a local `t9IsUnique`: `List`, `Map`, `Owned` and `StrBuf` are unique; `Untrusted`, optional, `Result` value and array element recurse; everything else is not unique. That means structs, unions, tuples, states and type parameters are wrong for now. T28 should replace `t9IsUnique` with T6's `isUnique`. The test compares `names` for 26 types, including `List<i64>`, `List<string>`, `List<List<i64>>`, `List<StrBuf>`, `ReadOnlySpan<u8>`, `i64?`, `StrBuf?` and `List<i64>?`. No unique-struct row: the C# oracle needs a `StructSymbol` with a parsed declaration. Resolved.
562. **010 T9: `isUnique` is T6's stub (always false).** So `List<T>.replace` is offered and `T?.take` withheld for every element type until T6 lands. The T9 tests use only non-unique element types; T28 should add a unique-element row (e.g. `List<StrBuf>`) once `isUnique` is real. Open.
563. **010 T9: what siblings call in place of `Builtins.X`.** `t9Type(ref c, for: "Rule")` returns the type (or -1) and `t9Function(ref c, for: key)` returns the function (or -1), using the keys in Q560. Both force the module into being. `Violation` is declaration 1 of the `Rule` union's file (`c.files[unionDecl.file]`). The C# `Builtins` properties with no entry point (`ArenaNew`, `StrBufNew`, `StrBufGrow`, `StrBufOver`, `HexEncode`, `HexDecode`, `SymbolIntern`, `Utf8DecodeReplace`) are reached this way; the `Io*` properties go through `findIo`. New.
564. **010 T9: break-tests performed and restored.** `selfhost/semantics/builtins.byn`: :418 `startsWith` returns `string` → `MemberTablesMatchTheCSharp` failed; :495 `removeLast` not mutating → `MemberTablesMatchTheCSharp` failed; :619 `formatSpec` names drop `radix` → `NamesMatchTheCSharp` failed; :280 `invalidUtf8At` key changed → `FunctionsMatchTheCSharpBuiltins` failed.; after Q561, the `names` filter without its `builtinProperty` half → `NamesMatchTheCSharp` failed; `t9IsUnique` without `.list` → `MemberTablesMatchTheCSharp` and `NamesMatchTheCSharp` failed. Each passed again once restored. New.
565. **010 T10: manifestRead unreadable file behavior.** In C#, `Manifest.Read` throws IO exceptions if the file cannot be read. In Bayan, `Io.readFile` returns an error, caught to parse an empty `package.byn` source text, which reports BYN3100 (`package.byn is data only: expected Package { … }`). Matches test expectation for unreadable manifests. New.
566. **010 T10: ASCII casing in camelOf/kebabOf and manifest validation.** Following Q442, Bayan has no Unicode casing table, so `camelOf`, `kebabOf`, `t10IsKebabName`, and `t10IsAsciiLetterOrDigit` operate on ASCII `A`-`Z` / `a`-`z` / `0`-`9`. New.
567. **010 T10: string decoding and StrBuf.** `t10DecodeString` and `t10TextOf` unescape ASCII and `\u{...}` hex scalars into bytes, then copy into a `StrBuf` and return `$"{sb.finish()}"` to avoid returning borrowed references to the token/reader buffers (avoiding BYN3003/BYN3004/BYN3005). New.
568. **010 T10: break-tests performed and restored.** `selfhost/semantics/manifest.byn`: :86 change `n += 1` -> `n += 0` → `ManifestMatchesCSharp` failed; :460 change `buf.append(0x2D)` -> `buf.append(0x5F)` → `KebabOfMatches` failed; :511 change `if slash < 0 { return false }` -> `if slash < 0 { return true }` → `PackageNamesMatch` failed. Each passed again once restored. New.
570. **010 T11: the C# closures are `Work` records; `runWork` runs each one's body.** C#'s `List<Action>` fields became `List<Work>`: `wheres` in ctx.byn's `// ── T11 state`, T3's `pendingKeys`, and T13's `pendingInterfaces` (kind `.interfaceMembers`). Encodings: `.where` is `file` + `declIndex` of the generic declaration, with `subject` its type (struct, enum, union, interface) or `instance` its function; `t11RunWhere` re-reads the declaration's `where` clauses and calls `declareWhere` with the symbol's type parameters and its type map, or `null` when it has none, as the C# `TypeMap` is. `.keyCheck` (from T8's `resolveMap`) runs T8's `t8CheckKey`, the closure body (compile.byn:1162 `let _ = t8CheckKey`). `.interfaceMembers` is `declareInterfaceMembers(subject)`; the caller wraps it in `instantiatingBegin`/`instantiatingEnd` as Compilation.cs:204 does. `.constraint` is the `Check` closure of `CheckConstraintsAt`, which T13 ports as `t13RunConstraint` (compile.byn:1164 `t13RunConstraint(ref c, for: in work)`). `.members`, `.unionVariants` and `.conform` call nothing: each panics, because C# runs them at once inside `Instantiating` and never queues them (compile.byn:1170 `panic("internal error: C# runs DeclareMembers`; Q720). `.fieldDefault` (`memberIndex` is the field) and `.bindFunction` (`instance`) call those entry points unwrapped (compile.byn:1178 `let _ = fieldDefault(`, :1182 `bindFunction(ref c, for: work.instance)`); no list that `runWork` drains holds these two kinds today (Q720). A `.keyCheck` queued at an instantiation site carries it in `atSite`/`siteFile`/`siteSpan` (Q716), and `declare` runs it inside `instantiatingBegin`/`instantiatingEnd`. `declare` copies each item (`t11CopyWork`) before running it, because `runWork` takes `c` by `ref`. The other C# fields with no home in `Ctx` are in the T11 section: `packageRoot`, `displayRoot`, `moduleOrder` (the C# `Modules`; `c.modules` also holds T9's builtin module, so `declare` walks `moduleOrder`), `entryModule`, `modulesByDir`, `loading`, `parseTime`/`checkTime`, `aliasOrder` (the C# `_aliases`: only aliases `addType` accepted), `testCases`, `associatedTypes`, `membersDeclared` and `onPanic` (the C# `OnPanic`, -1 for null; T11 never writes it: T36's `bindOnPanic` sets it, as Binder.cs:1393 `_c.OnPanic = handler` does, and the backend reads it). Shared fields (Q714): `includeTests` (compile.byn:944 `if !c.includeTests`), `skipOwnershipCheck`, `mainStatementsFn`/`mainStatements` (the C# `_mainStatements`), `testBodies`. Resolved.
571. **010 T11: path and loading parity.** `fromPath`, `fromProject` and `create` port Compilation.cs:69, :87 and :100, where they are `public static`; here they are module-level declarations without `public`, which the generated test main calls directly. They return the `Ctx` and take a `CompilationOptions` struct (compile.byn). `fromPath` normalizes its path with `t11FullPath` (compile.byn:35 `let full = t11FullPath(path)`), a port of what `Path.GetFullPath` does to an absolute path (.NET `PathInternal.RemoveRelativeSegments`, root length 1: `//`, `/./` and `/../` segments go, `..` never climbs past the root). Bayan has no current directory, so a relative path is returned as given and callers pass absolute paths. One branch is folded: .NET keeps the root `/` for a final `..` (`s + 1`), which the trailing root fix (compile.byn:1355 `if acc.length < 1 { acc = "/" }`) already does at root length 1. `unit fullpath` compares it with `Path.GetFullPath` on twelve inputs, `path dotted` loads `clean/./util/..//lib.byn`. `Directory.Exists` is "`Io.listDir` succeeds" (compile.byn:1289 `let _ = Io.listDir(path) catch return false`). `ModuleFiles` filters `Io.listDir`'s names by `.byn`, skips the ones that are directories, as `Directory.EnumerateFiles` lists files only (compile.byn:128 `if t11DirectoryExists(f) { continue }`), and sorts them with `pathLess`; `fromProject`'s `tests/` scan skips them too (compile.byn:64 `!t11DirectoryExists(f)`). `project dirs` and `path dirs` have directories `x.byn`, `y.test.byn` and `tests/x.test.byn`. `Path.Combine` and `Path.GetRelativePath` handle `/` paths only, and a path outside the root is returned whole instead of as `../…` (compile.byn:1370 `if path.startsWith(prefix)`); no C# caller asks for one. `File.ReadAllBytes` failing throws out of the C# compiler; here it panics (compile.byn:1283 `let bytes = Io.readFile(path) catch panic`). `CNameOf` writes one `_` per UTF-16 unit, as C# does, by byte arithmetic: a UTF-8 lead byte writes one, a 4-byte lead writes two (compile.byn:274 `sb.append("__")`), a continuation byte none; `unit cname` compares it with the C# `CNameOf` on `café`, `𝑥y` (astral, accepted by both lexers), `a.b-c` and `日本`. `create` sets `isEntry` on the entry module's files (compile.byn:95 `c.files[f].isEntry = true`), as `EntryModule` marks them; `declareFile` itself compares `module == c.entryModule`. Every lexer and parser diagnostic is an error (DiagnosticCodes.cs has no BYN0xxx/BYN1xxx warning), so `loadModule` copies them with `isWarning: false` (compile.byn:167 `isWarning: false,`). It skips a report the parser withdrew (`unreport` leaves code `""`, Q440), which the C# removes from its bag (Parser.cs:2627), and does not count it as an error (compile.byn:159 `if d.code == "" { continue }`). `create` calls T7's `buildLexicon` before `declare` (the C# `Lexicon` is static). `pathLess` (T2's, diag.byn:259) compares UTF-8 bytes while C# `StringComparer.Ordinal` compares UTF-16 units, so the module and `tests/` file orders differ only between a name with an astral character and one with a character in U+E000–U+FFFF; T28 is the place to change `pathLess`. `Compilation.IsEquatable` (Compilation.cs:63) only forwards to `Binder.IsEquatable`; Bayan has no class scope, so callers call express3.byn's `isEquatable` directly and compile.byn makes no second function of that name. `packageName` is not T11's field (ctx.byn's options section, `string`): `create` stores `options.packageName ?? ""`, so `""` stands for the C# null `PackageName`, and a reader rendering it (EffectAnalysis.cs:101 `?? "main"` for BYN6004) must read `""` as null. Resolved.
572. **010 T11: what `declareFile` leaves for the declare pass.** A symbol's `span` is the C# `Location` (the name for a type, function or constant; the whole test for a test; the first statement for a synthesized `main`). J23's `T_Field` enum is an `EnumSymbol` with the struct's `declIndex` and `fieldsOf` set (compile.byn:763 `fieldsOf: sym,`): T12's `declareEnumMembers` must take its members from the struct's fields, as the C# `EnumDecl` built from them does. A `type distinct` struct's `declIndex` is the alias declaration (compile.byn:877 `c.distinct[sym] = 1`), so T12's `declareMembers` builds its one `value` field, carrying the alias's `requires` (ported, declare.byn:187). `@positional` marks the declaration, as the C# `HashSet<StructDecl>` does: `c.positional` is keyed by `declKey(file, declIndex)` (compile.byn:575 `c.positional[declKey(file, at: declIndex)] = 1`), so express.byn's `c.positional.contains(s)` with a `StructId` (express.byn:998 `if c.positional.contains(s)`) must look the struct's declaration up instead (T17). `_testCases` keeps, per test, the index of its first `@cases` attribute and of each argument that is a case; `_testBodies` maps each test function to that attribute and argument, -1 for a test without parameters (compile.byn:694 `c.testBodies[fn] = TestBody`). `_nextErrorCode` is `errorVariants.length + 1`, as in T12's `declareVariants`: every `ErrorVariantSymbol` takes the next code (compile.byn:443 `code: c.errorVariants.length + 1,`). `CheckAttributes` reads its declaration taken out of the file with T8's `t8TakeDecl` and put back (compile.byn:723 `let decl = t8TakeDecl`), because passing `c` by `ref` and a declaration inside it is BYN3005. Resolved.
573. **010 T11: tests, break-tests and what they cannot reach.** `SelfhostSemanticsT11Tests` (35 cases) writes fixture trees to `tmp/t11-cases/` and compares each section line by line with the C#: `Compilation.FromPath`/`FromProject` for loading (module order, `CName`, files, imports, diagnostics as `code path line:col message | label | help`, including `unless (a && b)`, whose withdrawn BYN1017 must not show), the private `LoadModule` + `DeclareFile` and `Declare` by reflection for declaration (types, functions, constants, symbol lists, tests and case titles, `main`, `_aliases`, `Distinct`, `Positional`, `_wheres`, `_testCases`, `_mainStatements`, constraints, builtin error variants and codes, `Rule`'s variants), `Compilation.Create` filtered to BYN2771 for `main`'s signature (the signature is built by hand on the Bayan side, as T38's `declareSignature` would; `Missing main() { }` and `void main(Missing args) { }` give error types, which the check accepts), `AssociatedType`/`ReportInto` by reflection, `FunctionSymbol.IsInstance` on hand-built symbols for T5's `functionIsInstance` (the instance method is FuncId 0, the enclosing function of a lambda), a tuple `Map` key resolved by the C# `TypeResolver` with `_instantiationSite` set and then `Declare` (`unit keysite`: BYN2831 at the site with `InstantiationLabel`), and `Box<P>` resolved after `Declare` with each `_pendingConstraints` entry run (`unit constraint`: `runWork`'s `.constraint` arm, BYN2807). Break-tests, each run and restored from a copy: compile.byn:546 `if name == "cases" && isTest` changed to `!isTest` failed `declfile decls` and `declfile decls-tests`; compile.byn:236 `chain.append(" → ")` changed to `" -> "` failed the six `path imports-*` cases; removing the `continue` after BYN2013 at compile.byn:914 `continue` failed `declfile decls` and `declfile decls-tests`; compile.byn:159 `if d.code == "" { continue }` with `"x"` failed `path unless`; compile.byn:1138 `w.atSite = true` to `false`, compile.byn:390 `if work.atSite {` to `if false {` and compile.byn:1140 `w.siteSpan = c.instantiationSiteSpan` to another span each failed `unit keysite`; compile.byn:1164 `t13RunConstraint(ref c, for: in work)` replaced by `let _ = work.kind` failed `unit constraint`; compile.byn:934 `isConst = false` (the arm for a statement that is not a `let`/`var`/`const`, reached by `print("a")` in `stmts/a.byn`) to `true` failed `declfile stmts`; dropping `isError(returns)` from compile.byn:479 `let returnOk` failed `mainsig main-missing`, and compile.byn:485 `if isError(type) {` changed to `if false {` failed `mainsig main-missing-param`; compile.byn:405 `if main >= 0 && c.functions[main].kind == .function` with `!=` failed `declare main-string`; compile.byn:274 `sb.append("__")` with `"_"` and compile.byn:275 `} else if b < 0x80 || b >= 0xC0 {` with `} else {` each failed `unit cname`; removing compile.byn:128 `if t11DirectoryExists(f) { continue }` failed every case (the run panics reading the directory `x.byn`), and dropping `&& !t11DirectoryExists(f)` from compile.byn:64 failed every case (the run panics reading the directory `tests/x.test.byn`); compile.byn:35 `let full = t11FullPath(path)` with `path` failed `path dotted`. `create`'s `removeRepeats` condition is untested and marked (compile.byn:105 `// (blocked: Q573)`): no current path produces a repeated diagnostic to observe. A repeat comes only from binding one `@cases` body once per case, each case its own test function (Compilation.cs:367, T13's `t13BindTest`). With `includeTests` off, `t11CheckAttributes` still fills `testCases` but no test function is declared (compile.byn:944 `if !c.includeTests`), so `create` reaches the `removeRepeats` line with nothing repeated; with it on, `create` stopped earlier in T12's `checkOverloads` (below; it now skips them, declare.byn:576 `c.functions[f].kind == .function`). T12's landing (`checkOverloads` skipping test functions) makes a repeat reachable: then add a `path` case with includeTests and a `@cases` test whose body has an error. The fixtures avoid two sibling bugs found here: T12's `t12LocationOf` checks the kind before `t8IsAlias`, and `kindOf` of an alias handle is `.errorSet`, so a name declared after an alias reported "already declared on <builtin>:1" (fixed: the alias test now comes first, declare.byn:740 `if t8IsAlias(t) { return loc(c.aliases[i].file`); T12's `checkOverloads` indexes `functions[name]` for every function in `allFunctions`, so a synthesized `main` or a test function panicked (fixed: keys come from `.function` symbols only, declare.byn:576, and each is indexed at declare.byn:579 `var overloads = copyIds(in c.modules[module].functions[key])`), which is why `keysite` and `constraint` write their types in a function body rather than at top level. Open (blocked on T12).

580. **010 T13: `Instantiating` (Q704) as `instantiatingBegin`/`instantiatingEnd`, its state, and what it forwards.** The C# fields live in ctx.byn's `// ── T13 state` section (Q710): `instantiating` (`_instantiating`), `hasInstantiationSite`/`instantiationSiteFile`/`instantiationSiteSpan` (`_instantiationSite`; set only when unset, so it is the outermost use), `instantiationErrors` (`_instantiationErrors`). `instantiatingBegin` saves the sink (`_scratch`) and the site into `InstantiatingScope` and pushes a fresh bag; `instantiatingEnd` restores both, decrements the depth and walks the bag's errors as C# `:1483-1497` does: BYN2760, BYN2831, BYN2208, BYN2225 and BYN2807 always go to the use (generics.byn:295 `let always = code == codeText(.invalidMapKey)`), BYN2822, BYN2022 and BYN2780 only when `t13Reported` finds no diagnostic with the same code, file and span in the target or in `c.diagnostics` (generics.byn:271 `bool t13Reported`), BYN7012 only with an instance and not reported, with C#'s help and a `Related` span when the error is in the use's file (generics.byn:303 `} else if code == codeText(.assignmentChangesState)`); every other error is held in `instantiationErrors` (generics.byn:316 `c.instantiationErrors.append(move d)`), warnings are dropped. Forwarded diagnostics and what `reportHeld` releases go straight into the sink through `t13Add`, which is diag.byn's `addDiag` without its `if c.quiet { return }` (generics.byn:66), since C# `target.Add`/`AddRange` (Compilation.cs:1488, :1490, :1919) has no such gate. C# has no `_quiet` at all, so there is no reachable C# equivalent to set: the `instantiating` and `reportHeld` sections set Bayan's `c.quiet = true` around `instantiatingEnd`/`reportHeld` and compare with the lines of the same C# run without it. 581. **010 T13: instance keys, `Decl`, and the deferred-work encodings.** C# `_instances` is ctx `instanceKeys`, keyed by `t13Key` (`f` + template `FuncId` or `t` + template `Type`, then each argument handle; handles are canonical, so this is C#'s reference-and-sequence equality) (generics.byn:391 `let key = t13Key("f"`). Instances are not added to `Mod.structs`/`unions`/`interfaces`; a function instance goes to `allFunctions`, as in C#. A C# `Decl` is the symbol's `(file, declIndex, memberIndex)`: `t13DeclareInstance`, `t13BindBody`, `t13SyntaxDefault` and `templateOf` (its twin lookup compares the triple) read the tree through it. `modifiers` is copied because it is the `Decl`'s modifiers (compile.byn:901 `modifiers: i64(f.value.modifiers),` for a top-level function), so the review's item 19 is wrong on that field; `iface` and `isAbstract` are no longer copied. Work items: `.bindFunction` carries the function to bind in `instance` and C#'s `Instance` in `memberIndex` (-1 for null), so T14's `conform` queueing `instance: fn` with no `memberIndex` (conformance.byn:330 `instance: fn,`) is C#'s null of Conformance.cs:184 (Q721; generics.byn:427 `memberIndex: fn })`). `.fieldDefault` carries the instance in `subject` and the field in `memberIndex`. A deferred constraint check (`_pendingConstraints`) is `Work { kind: .constraint, subject: instance }` in `c.pendingConstraints` (generics.byn:559 `c.pendingConstraints.append(move work)`), run by `t13RunConstraint` (generics.byn:480 `void t13RunConstraint`), which compile.byn's `runWork` calls from its `.constraint` arm (compile.byn:1163-1164) when conformance.byn's `checkConformances` drains `c.pendingConstraints` (conformance.byn:467-485, Compilation.cs:1592-1593). `_interfaceMembersDeclared` and `_pendingInterfaces` are ctx `interfaceMembersDeclared`/`pendingInterfaces` (`Work { kind: .interfaceMembers }`, generics.byn:720 `c.pendingInterfaces.append`); compile.byn's `declare` sets the flag and drains the list inside `instantiatingBegin`/`instantiatingEnd` (compile.byn:305-311, Compilation.cs:202-204). C#'s `_interfaceGetters[fn]` and `_constructorBodies[fn]` (Compilation.cs:1777, :1786) are the function's own `declIndex`/`memberIndex`: `t13BindBody` reads an interface getter (one with `iface` set) and a constructor through them unchanged (generics.byn:885 `if (t13Handle(c.functions[fn].iface) is { } _) {` keeps `d`/`m`; :900-902 for a constructor), and binds the member they name (generics.byn:939-947 for an interface, :928-938 for a struct). declare.byn sets them for struct members (declare.byn:99-100 for a getter, :216-217 for a constructor); T38's `declareInterfaceMembers` (declare2.byn:12, a stub) must set them on each interface getter it creates, whose C# `Decl` is null and whose declaration lives only in `_interfaceGetters` (Compilation.cs:1160-1164). Not compared (Q584). Resolved.
582. **010 T13: `CheckMutation` is blocked; `RequiresCheck`, seeds and the parameter-default binder.** C# `MutationCheck(Binder, Callee, Receiver)` and `ThisWrites` hold the binder object that saw the call, and `CheckMutation` calls `CheckWritable`/`CheckGuardWrite`/`ReportMutatesWithoutRefThis` on it after every body is bound. A Bayan `Binder` is a value the binding function owns, so there is no binder to hold; a copy taken at the call would not be the binder's final state. `checkMutation` stays a stub (generics.byn:1017 `void checkMutation(ref Ctx c) {}`) and `bindFunction` does not roll `MutationChecks` back (generics.byn:802 `MutationChecks` has no home), until T28 decides how a check reaches its binder (a binder arena, or the check carrying what `CheckWritable` reads). *Dispatcher decision (2026-10-31):* C# `ChangedFields` (Compilation.cs:1841) is RegionAnalysis's per-function memo (only RegionAnalysis.cs:724-769 reads or writes it); T13's range only declares it. The RegionAnalysis port (T25, region.byn) adds it to ctx.byn's T25 section when it ports `ChangedFields`; T13 has no code for it. Resolved. `RequiresChecks` is ctx `requiresChecks`: `RequiresCheck { source, callSpan, callArgs, callee, arguments, argumentFiles }`, where `callArgs` is a `Location` (file and span) per argument value written in the call and `argumentFiles` is the file of each bound argument's syntax (the caller's for a written one, the callee's for a default, which `parameterDefault` binds in `fn.File`, Compilation.cs:1904). *Dispatcher decision (2026-10-31):* C#'s `ReferenceEquals(a.Value, check.Arguments[p.Ordinal].Syntax)` is file-and-span equality (generics.byn:1050 `if a.file == writtenFile && a.span == written { inCall = true }`): within one file no two argument expressions share a span. `Location` is declare.byn's (T12). T20 must append these, with both lists, when it binds a call to a function with `expects`. `release` returning an empty list is C#'s null seeds (generics.byn:954 `if next.length > 0 { return next }`). `Binder` now has `typeArgs` (from T15), so `parameterDefault` sets `b.typeArgs` to `c.functions[f].typeMap` as C# passes `fn.TypeMap` (generics.byn:1128 `var b = t13NewBinder(c.functions[f].file`). *Resolved (dispatcher):* checkMutation blocked until T28 designs a binder-free MutationCheck record.
583. **010 T13: exit codes, main statements and test bodies.** `_exitCodes`, `_mainStatements` and `_testBodies` are shared fields in `ctx.byn` (Q714: `c.exitCodes`, `c.mainStatementsFn`/`c.mainStatements`, `c.testBodies`). `ExitCodeRef` has no separate file: C#'s tuple `file` is the file the attribute is in, which is `attribute.file`, so `bindAll` binds each exit code with that file (generics.byn:138 `let f = entry.attribute.file`) and panics on an entry that is not on an error variant (generics.byn:148). `t13BindBody` calls T15's entry points with the signatures of Q718: the `.main` arm passes a copy of `c.mainStatements` to `bindMain` (generics.byn:921 `bindMain(ref b, through: ref c, for: in statements)`), since `c.mainStatements` cannot be lent while `c` is passed by `ref`, and a `.testKeyword` function passes `c.testBodies[fn]` to `bindTest` (generics.byn:923 `bindTest(ref b, through: ref c, for: c.testBodies[fn])`), indexing the map directly so a missing entry traps as C#'s `_testBodies[fn]` throws (Compilation.cs:1792); `bindTest` itself panics on a ref that is not a test and reads `hasValues`/`values` for a `@cases` case. `bindMain` sets `firstStatementFile`/`firstStatementSpan` (Q719), so T13 writes no first statement; ctx.byn's older `i64 firstStatement` (outside T13's section) is no longer written by anyone and can go at T28. `_thisType` needs no T13 call: every T15 entry point calls `t15CaptureTypes` first (Q719), so `t13NewBinder` stays a plain literal. `EntryModule` is T11's `c.entryModule` (ctx.byn:469, set by `fromProject` at compile.byn:94): `bindAll`'s BYN2014 check (generics.byn:229 `if c.modules[c.entryModule].main == -1`) and `invokeSymbol`'s module (generics.byn:1083 `module: c.entryModule,`) read it directly, as C# reads `EntryModule` (Compilation.cs:1422, :1893), with no guard on it. 584. **010 T13 redo: tests, break-tests, and review items judged.** `SelfhostSemanticsT13Tests` has 17 sections in `All` plus one fact. Each section compiles its source with `Compilation.Create`, drives the C# method through reflection (`Instantiating`, `CheckConstraints`, `InstantiateFunction` with `_instantiating`/`_firstPass` set, `InstantiateType` with `_conformancesChecked` false and `_interfaceMembersDeclared` toggled, then `_conformancesChecked` true for `Box<Circle>` and `Maybe<Both>` (the constraint runs at once: no pending check, `checkedBad` reports BYN2807 at the use), the `_pendingConstraints` actions, `TemplateOf`, `InvokeSymbol`, `ErrorSetsOf` after inference, `BindConstant` with `State` set, `ReportHeld`/`ReportInto`, `FieldDefault`, `ParameterDefault`, `BindFunction` on a method, a getter, two functions and an invoke symbol, with the locals each declares, the BYN2002 a first pass held and released, and the change in `_instantiationErrors`, `BindFunction` on the synthesized main (two top-level blocks, the second a BYN2202) and on both cases of a `@cases` test (the second a BYN2202), the `RequiresChecks` the C# binder recorded in a one-file and a two-file compilation, BYN2014 from four compilations, `BindAll` draining an exit code and a test body, and the drain of the methods an `InstantiateType` queued, each run as `Instantiating(work.Site, work.Span, work.Bind, work.Instance)`), and emits Bayan code that builds the same symbols from the C# ones; diagnostics compare as `code line:col message | label | help`. The old `Map<i64, i64> conformancesChecked` arena (ctx.byn:356) is dead; it stays until T28 because guard check C lets ctx.byn sections only grow (Q723). Compared in `checkConformances` (`checked yes`). New.
586. **010 T14: `Quietly` is `quietlyBegin`/`quietlyEnd`.** C# `Quietly(Action)` (Conformance.cs:188) swaps in a throwaway bag around the action; the port opens a bag with `pushBag` (conformance.byn:357) and drops it with `popBag` (conformance.byn:362), around `associatedBinding`'s resolve (conformance.byn:38-41), `t14Expected`'s declaration (conformance.byn:258, :277) and `t14CloneDefault`'s signature (conformance.byn:318-320, :323-326). Compared in `quietly` (a report inside is dropped, one after reaches the diagnostics), `associatedBinding` and `expected` (`diags +0` with an unresolvable `Nope`). New.
587. **010 T14: what `conform` reads and writes.** Per base, in `Bases` order: the base's span from the shared `c.baseSpans` or the struct's name span (conformance.byn:115), each associated type from `c.associatedBindings` or BYN2803 (conformance.byn:122-129), then members ordered by start (conformance.byn:133, a stable insertion sort at :218). A field stands for a getter only (conformance.byn:139): a type mismatch is BYN2802 (conformance.byn:143), else a field witness, with BYN2780 when the field is unique other than through a type parameter (conformance.byn:156). Without a witness: a field for a method (conformance.byn:172), a later base's default (conformance.byn:175), a missing abstract member with `t14InsertMember`'s fix (conformance.byn:180-183), or a cloned default (conformance.byn:185). A witness that is an earlier base's clone is BYN2802 (conformance.byn:194), a shape mismatch BYN2802 (conformance.byn:202), a `ref this` mismatch BYN2814 with `t14RefThisFix` (conformance.byn:206-209). `t14CloneDefault` appends to `allFunctions` and, for a non-generic owner, a `.bindFunction` Work at the base's span (conformance.byn:348-350). `checkConformances` adds the interfaces' defaults to `allFunctions` (conformance.byn:62, :66), conforms every struct, then the instances in `c.instanceKeys` inside `instantiatingBegin` (conformance.byn:81-85), and drains `c.pendingConstraints` by copying each Work (conformance.byn:88-101) before clearing it (conformance.byn:103), as C# runs `_pendingConstraints` then clears it (Conformance.cs:51-52). Compared in `checkConformances`, `baseSpanFallback` and `associatedBinding`. New.

589. **010 T14: copies instead of aliases.** BYN3005 rejects `ref c` beside an argument read from `c`, so `conform` reads a field's name into `fieldName` before `findField` (conformance.byn:152-153), `checkConformances` copies each pending `Work` field by field (conformance.byn:88-100) rather than passing `in c.pendingConstraints[k]`, and the id lists it walks while appending are `copyIds` copies (conformance.byn:58, :78, :111). Bayan's `List` has no `contains`, so `t14SetEquals` (C#'s `ToHashSet().SetEquals`) uses `t14Has` (conformance.byn:412). New.
590. **010 T15: `hold`, `report` and `release`.** `Binder.held` is the held bag's `Ctx.bags` index plus one, 0 for none (`Ctx.sink` already uses -1 for the root list). `hold` appends a bag (C#'s standalone `_held`) and sets `held`; `report`, `checkValueName` and `resolveType` point `c.sink` at it while held and restore it after (the C# `Report` and `Holding`). `release` (binder.byn:144) groups the constraints by `findPeer` as Binder.cs:71-92 does and returns the seeds keyed by `LocalDecl` span start, the key `Binder.pending`, `constraints`, `peers` and `seeds` use (Q708): the first item of the signature's `(LocalId, Type)` is that key, not a `LocalId`. C#'s null ("the pass stands") is an empty list. Held diagnostics are copied (`Diag` is unique) and filtered by the text of `Compilation.InstantiationLabel` (binder.byn:184), which has no Bayan constant (generics.byn writes the same text). `t15CloneDiag` (binder.byn:13) repeats generics.byn's `t13CloneDiag`, and `reportHeld` clones the copies again; T28 merges the duplicate. Tested by `HoldAndReleaseMatch` (7 cases against the C# `Hold`/`Report`/`Release` with `_pending`, `_constraints` and `_peers` filled by reflection). New.
591. **010 T15: scopes and locals.** C# starts every binder with a root scope (`_scope = new(null)`); a Bayan `Binder` literal has `scopes: []`, so `t15Scope` (binder.byn:113) opens the root on first use, and `pushScope` opens it before the child. Each scope takes `nextScopeId` into `scopeIds`, parallel to `scopes` (Q715); `popScope` removes the innermost scope and its id. `addLocal` (binder.byn:283) follows Binder.cs:143-162: BYN2028 (`sameTypeShadowing`) for a `let` over a same-scope local of the same non-error type, else BYN2007 (`shadowing`) when the lookup, which includes the current scope, finds the name; labels and help are the C# texts. Bayan `LocalSymbol` has no null location, so the C# "already declared here" (a local with no `Location`) never occurs; every label names a line. C#'s private `DeclareParameters` is `t15DeclareParameters`. Tested by `ScopesAndLocalsMatch` (same-scope, outer-scope, `_`, naming, `temp`, held, `outer-first` (the shadowed local is `c.locals[0]`), and `identity`, which numbers the C# `_scope` object by first appearance against `scopeIds`). New.
592. **010 T15: type maps and parameter syntax.** The C# constructor builds `_types` once, with `typeArgs ?? fn.TypeMap ?? container.TypeMap` (Binder.cs:55). `t15CaptureTypes` (binder.byn:214) takes that map into `Binder.types` (T15 state, with `typesCaptured`) on the first call of any entry point or of `resolveType` (binder.byn:242), so a lambda body, which moves `b.fn` to the lifted lambda, keeps the enclosing map (case `lambda-keeps-map`). The C# constructor's `typeArgs` is `Binder.typeArgs` (null by default), and an empty Bayan `typeMap` stands for C#'s null. `bindParameterDefault` needs C#'s `p.Syntax!.Default!`, which `LocalSymbol` does not keep: `t15ParameterOwner` (binder.byn:449) finds the function whose `parameters` hold `p`, and the default is `params[ordinal].defaultKeyword` of its declaration (a top-level function, a struct method or constructor, an interface or extension method). Q713 accepts the scan until T38 records the syntax and T28 switches to it. The same constructor sets `_thisType` to the container, else `fn.Interface.Self` (Binder.cs:54): `t15CaptureTypes` sets `b.thisType` to `structTypeOf(b.owner)` (binder.byn:217 `if b.owner >= 0 {`), else, for a function whose `iface` is set, to `t15InterfaceSelf` (binder.byn:232), which ports `InterfaceSymbol.Self` (Symbols.cs:294) and makes the `Self` type parameter on first use (binder.byn:233 `if c.interfaces[i].self == -1 {`); the test no longer sets `thisType` by hand (Q719). T13's `parameterDefault` (generics.byn:1126) binds only a parameter whose syntax has a default (`t13SyntaxDefault`, generics.byn:1095, called at generics.byn:1127 `if c.locals[p].defaultValue == -1 && t13SyntaxDefault(in c, for: f, by: p) {`, as Compilation.cs:1901-1904), so a parameter with no default is skipped on both sides and the test sources need no default on every parameter (an earlier text said otherwise; `defaults` keeps a non-constant `zz` on purpose). Tested by `ResolveTypeMatches` (7 cases) and `DefaultsMatch`. New.
593. **010 T15: binder state and syntax shapes.** ctx.byn's Binder `// ── T15 state` holds `typeArgs`, `types`/`typesCaptured` (Q592), `itField` (C#'s `_it`, which T17's `it` and `bindChecks` read) and `thisFacts` (C#'s `_thisFacts`, a `let` named `this` of the error type; `t15ThisFacts` (binder.byn:323) makes it on first use, and T22's state functions should key on the same field). `firstStatementFile`/`firstStatementSpan` hold C#'s `_firstStatement` as the statement's file and full span, `firstStatementFile` -1 for none (Q719; binder.byn:342 `b.firstStatementFile = any ? b.file : -1` in `bindFunctionBody`, :550-551 in `bindMain`); ctx.byn's older `i64 firstStatement` (outside the T15 section) is written by nobody since T13 calls `bindMain` (generics.byn:921 `bindMain(ref b, through: ref c, for: in statements)`), and can go (Q583). `bindTest` (binder.byn:566) takes C#'s null `values` (no `@cases`) as `hasValues` false (Q718). C# never passes a non-null empty array: Compilation.cs:334-335 makes `values` the tuple's elements or `[arg.Value]` and drops a case whose count differs from the parameters, and a probe of `@cases(())` stops in the parser (BYN1002, "a tuple has at least two elements"), so a case always has at least one value and `hasValues` true always names one. The panic check calls `t9Function(ref c, for: "panic")`, the builtin C# reads as `_c.Builtins.Panic`. C#'s `BlockStmt` bodies are a parser `Stmt` here, so `bindGetter`, `bindConstructor` (binder.byn:528) and `bindTest` switch on `.blockStmt`; the parser builds no other variant there. Tested by `FunctionBodyMatches`, `MissingBodyMatches`, `GetterAndConstructorMatch` (with `copy`, a method returning `this`), `InterfaceSelfMatches` (`IShape.touch`), `GuardedFirstStatementMatches` (`return if d`, whose span is larger than its child's), `MainMatches`, `TestBodyMatches`, `ModuleConstantMatches` and `ArraySizesMatch`; failure paths: getter `wrong` (BYN2202), constructor `Point` with default `zz` (BYN2001; the oracle clears `p.Default`, which `Compilation.Create` already filled, so both sides bind it on first use), main over the source's two top-level blocks, passed as `SyntaxRef`s (Q718): `let q: bool = 3` gives BYN2202, and the block span is the first statement's, tests `plain` (no `@cases`), `cased`, `dup` (two `n` parameters: C# reports BYN2028, not BYN2007, since both are `let i32` in one scope), `mism` (BYN2202 twice) and `lone` (`@cases(5)`, a value that is not a tuple: BYN2202), passed as `TestBody` refs (Q718), field `bad` (BYN2202). New.

Bayan `List` has no insert, so C#'s `statements.Insert(0, …)` for each `broken_` flag becomes a separate list of flag declarations put in front when the block is built. 595. **010 T16: integer literal fallback in `bindExitCode`.** While `bindExpr` is a stub in `express.byn` (T17), `bindExitCode` falls back to `bigParse(lit.value.text)` when encountering an integer literal syntax node directly. This enables exit codes on error variants (BYN2772 checks) to resolve values during T16 testing ahead of expression binding completion. New.
596. **010 T16: diagnostic code mappings for statements B.** Verified diagnostic codes in `codes.byn`: `checkUniqueConst` emits `uniqueConst` (BYN3209, not BYN2803); `bindLabeled` duplicate label emits `duplicateDeclaration` (BYN2006); `bindLabeled` label on non-loop emits `labelNotOnLoop` (BYN2408); missing initializer emits `missingInitializer` (BYN2101); `assert` condition not bool emits `assertNotBool` (BYN2775); `using` on non-disposable emits `notDisposable` (BYN2226); `invalidExitCode` is BYN2772. New.
597. **010 T16: borrow-checker workarounds in AST traversals and assertions.** In `bindLabeled`, checking duplicate labels iterates over `b.targets`; reporting inside the loop triggered BYN3004 on `b`. A boolean flag is now set in the loop and reported after the loop terminates. In `isBorrowedPlace` (within `binder2.byn`), checking switch arm values or with updates iterates over lists on `c`; to avoid BYN3004, target IDs are extracted to a local list before calling methods borrowing `c`. In `bindAssertFails`, accessing `a.failsKeyword` by reference directly avoided BYN2780 (moving unique AST expression variant). New.
598. **010 T16: break-tests performed and restored.** `selfhost/semantics/binder2.byn`: (a) :488 inverted exit code range check `code < 1 || code > 255` → `SelfhostSemanticsT16Tests.BindExitCodeMatches` failed; (b) :273 commented out local declaration in `bindFor` → `SelfhostSemanticsT16Tests.BindStatementsMatches` failed; (c) :556 changed `narrowedBegin` learned state insertion → `SelfhostSemanticsT16Tests.IsNonNullAndNarrowingMatches` failed. Each test failed as expected and passed again once restored. New.
595. **010 T16: the port's shapes: jump targets, scope keys, `Narrowed` split, exit codes.** C#'s `labelTarget ?? new JumpTarget(null, isLoop)` is `t16Target` (binder2.byn:16 `JumpTarget t16Target(ref Ctx c, to JumpTarget? labelTarget, bool isLoop) {`), and `new JumpTarget(label, isLoop)` is `t16NewTarget` (binder2.byn:24 `JumpTarget t16NewTarget(ref Ctx c, for string? label, bool isLoop) {`), which appends to `c.jumpTargets` and takes the next id, so a bound loop stores `target.id`. Facts are keyed by the current scope's identity (Q715) through `t16ScopeId` (binder2.byn:35 `i64 t16ScopeId(ref Binder b) => b.scopeIds[t15Scope(ref b)]`). The C# `Narrowed<T>(cond, whenTrue, Func<T> bind)` cannot take a stored lambda, so it is `narrowedBegin`, the caller's bind, then `narrowedEnd`, with what C# keeps in locals (`mark`, the state facts `before`, `learned`) carried in `NarrowedScope` (binder2.byn:9 `struct NarrowedScope {`). `bindExitCode` reads C#'s `Int128 n` from `Constant.integer`, so `n < 1 || n > 255` is binder2.byn:53 `if k.integer.hi != 0 || k.integer.lo < 1 || k.integer.lo > 255 {`. `bindStatement` matches C#'s `Panic.handler`/`onPanic` property pattern with nested `switch`es and `t15Text` (binder2.byn:104 `if t15Text(in c, from: b.file, at: n.value.name) == "Panic" {`); a null `Else` is `elseBranch` -1 (binder2.byn:131 `var elseBranch: BStmt = -1`),. `bindLabeled` makes the label's target (binder2.byn:501 `let target = t16NewTarget(ref c, for: text, isLoop: !isSwitch)`) and passes it on (binder2.byn:506 `return bindStatement(ref b, through: ref c, for: in l.statement, labelTarget: target)`). Resolved.
596. **010 T16: null narrowing.** `isNonNull` walks the open scopes' identities instead of C#'s `_scope.Parent` chain (binder2.byn:366 `for s in b.scopeIds {`, then binder2.byn:367 `if s == pair.item1 { return true }`); `scopeIds` holds exactly the open scopes, innermost last (Q715), so the two agree. `narrowedBegin` and `narrowAfter` key new facts by `t16ScopeId` (binder2.byn:376 `let scope = t16ScopeId(ref b)`). C#'s `_stateFacts.RemoveAll(f => !before.Contains(f))` keeps a fact when an equal tuple was there before, so `narrowedEnd` compares all three fields (binder2.byn:399 `if bf.item1 == f.item1 && bf.item2 == f.item2 && bf.item3 == f.item3 {`). C#'s `BoundIf { Else: { } e }` arm of `Exits` needs an else, so binder2.byn:435 `return node.elseBranch != -1 && exits(in c, for: node.then) && exits(in c, for: node.elseBranch)`. `NonNullWhen`'s local function `Collect` is `nonNullCollect`, appending to the caller's list. `learnStates`, `unlearnStates` and `forgetChangingStates` are T22 stubs (Q599). Resolved.
597. **010 T16: `_handled` and `assert … fails`.** C# `_handled` is a Binder field (BinderCalls.cs:11 `private Expr? _handled;`), so it is `Binder.handled` in ctx.byn's Binder `// ── T16 state`, a `TextSpan?` holding the handled call's span (Q703). C# binds `StripParens(a.Condition)` with `_handled` set to it when it is a `CallExpr`, and otherwise binds the whole condition with `_handled` left as it was (Binder.cs:690-700). `t16BindAssertOperand` does the same without T20's `stripParens` stub: it walks the `parenExpr` chain in place (binder2.byn:287 `case .parenExpr(let p):`), binds a call itself with `handled` set to the call's span (binder2.byn:291 `b.handled = call.value.span`) and restores it after (binder2.byn:293 `b.handled = saved`), and binds anything else as the whole condition (binder2.byn:296 `return bindExpr(ref b, through: ref c, for: in condition)`). The non-call path is compared in `misc` (`assert 3 fails E`, `assert zz fails E`, `assert (p) fails E.bad`; every body section prints `handled` after binding). Binding the inner `p` of `(p)` instead of the whole condition passes every case: the bound tree and the report span are the same. The call path and what `handled` changes (BinderCalls.cs:166 and :231 skip the BYN2602 report for the handled call; BinderCalls.cs:965 `Checked` compares it with struct-literal and `with` syntax) need T20 (Q599). `setSpan` starts as `a.span` (binder2.byn:313 `var setSpan = a.span`) only to have a value; both arms of the following `switch` overwrite it. Resolved.
