710. **010 dispatcher: per-task state sections in ctx.byn.** ctx.byn was frozen after T4, but `Ctx` and `Binder` do not hold every field the C# keeps (`_instantiating`, `_exitCodes`, `_associatedBindings`, `_baseSpans`, `MutationChecks`, `RequiresChecks`, `_loading`, `_caught`, `_handled`, `_it`, …). With nowhere to put them, T11–T17 approximated or dropped them (Q711). From 2026-10-28 ctx.byn carries one `// ── T<n> state` marker per task, at the end of `Ctx` (T10–T39) and of `Binder` (T15–T25, T34–T39). A task adds the fields it needs, each with a default, only under its own marker; the guard rejects any other ctx.byn change. T28 may regroup them. Resolved.
711. **010 dispatcher: T11–T17 are reopened.** An independent review on 2026-10-28 found that T11–T17, landed 2026-10-27/28 after the dropoff, are not method-for-method ports: their tests type the expected lines by hand instead of running the C# (the brief requires the C# oracle), several functions invent logic or carry fallbacks for unported siblings (T15 `bindConstructor`, T16 `bindExitCode`/`bindAssert*`, T17 `bindName`/`bindConverted`, T13 `bindFunction`'s `body = 0`), some are empty (T13 `checkMutation`, `checkRequires`), Q704 was skipped, and Questions 565, 571–574, 587, 592 and 603 make claims the code contradicts. Concrete crashes: T12 `checkOverloads` indexes `functions[name]` for method names (panics on any struct with a method); T14 tests the private bit as the static bit. T10 passed review and stays landed. The tasks are unticked and redone on the same files, starting from the landed code, under the tightened gate (Q712). Resolved.
712. **010 dispatcher: the landing gate.** The guard passed T11–T17 because it checks only that the task's own tests pass and kill mutants, and hand-typed expectations satisfy both. From 2026-10-28: (1) `scripts/selfhost/guard.sh` also runs `guard-checks.py`: the test class must run the C# implementation and may not type expected lines (2 exemptions, each naming a Question); no `// stub: <task>` marker or empty body may remain unless marked `(blocked: Qnnn)`; ctx.byn changes only in the task's section; no Open Question gating the task; a Progress log entry; Question line citations must hold. Mutants that do not compile no longer count as killed. (2) An independent reviewer that did not write the code compares the port with the C# (`scripts/selfhost/review-brief.py` writes its brief) and records `reviews/<T>.md`. (3) Only `scripts/selfhost/land.sh <T> <branch>` merges, and only after the guard passes and the review says `Verdict: PASS` with no open HIGH row on the branch head; it ticks the task. Writers no longer tick. Resolved.
713. **010 dispatcher: a parameter's default syntax.** C# `ParameterSymbol.Syntax` (set by `DeclareSignature`, Compilation.cs:1281) has no field in `LocalSymbol` (symbols.byn, T3). Until the task that ports `DeclareSignature` (T38) records it, T15 `bindParameterDefault` finds the declaration by scanning functions' `parameters` (`t15ParameterOwner`); it gives the C# result for every declaration shape. *Resolved (dispatcher, 2026-10-28):* accepted for now; T38 adds `Map<LocalId, …>` for the syntax in its `// ── T38 state` section and T28 switches T15 to it and deletes the scan. Resolved.
714. **010 dispatcher: shared state.** Some C# state is written by one task and read by another (`_exitCodes`: T12 → T13; `_mainStatements`, `_testBodies`: T11 → T13; `Options.IncludeTests`/`SkipOwnershipCheck`: T11 → T13), so neither task's own section can hold it without the other failing to compile. ctx.byn now has a dispatcher-owned `// ── Shared state (Q714)` section with those fields, plus `SyntaxRef` (file, declaration, member, item and sub-item indexes into the parsed units) for state the C# keeps as syntax objects; the owning task documents which indexes it uses in a Question. Tasks may not add to the shared section; a task that needs another shared field asks the dispatcher. T13's own `includeTests`/`skipOwnershipCheck` move here. Resolved.
715. **010 dispatcher: a scope's identity.** *Decided (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* C# keys `_nonNull` and `_stateFacts` by the `Scope` object (Binder.cs:22, :98-110), and a fact dies with its scope even when a sibling scope later opens at the same depth, so a depth is not a scope. ctx.byn's Binder `// ── T15 state` holds `scopeIds` (parallel to `scopes`, innermost last) and `nextScopeId`: `t15Scope` gives the root its id (binder.byn:116 `b.scopeIds.append(b.nextScopeId)`), `pushScope` takes the next id (binder.byn:259 `b.scopeIds.append(b.nextScopeId)`) and `popScope` drops the innermost (binder.byn:265 `b.scopeIds.remove(at: b.scopeIds.length - 1)`). T16 must key `nonNull`/`stateFacts` by `b.scopeIds[b.scopeIds.length - 1]` instead of `b.scopes.length - 1` and treat a fact as live only when its id is still in `scopeIds` (C# `IsNonNull` walking `_scope`→`Parent`); binder2.byn is unchanged until T16's redo. Tested by `ScopesAndLocalsMatch(identity)`: push, pop, push gives a new number on both sides. Open until T16 switches.
716. **010 dispatcher: a deferred check's instantiation site.** C# `AfterMembersDeclared` queues `() => Instantiating(site, span, check)` when `_instantiationSite` is set (Compilation.cs:1549-1550), so the check runs later inside `Instantiating` at that site: forwarded with the instantiation label, held errors kept, depth counted. A `Work` has one `file`/`span`, its own location, so overwriting them with the site (as T11's first redo did) loses the check's location and the wrapper. *Resolved (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* `Work` gains `atSite`, `siteFile` and `siteSpan` (ctx.byn, beside `memberIndex`); `afterMembersDeclared` sets them and leaves `file`/`span` alone; whoever drains `pendingKeys` (T11 `declare`) wraps an `atSite` item in `instantiatingBegin(siteFile, siteSpan)`/`instantiatingEnd` around `runWork`. Resolved.
717. **010 dispatcher: T11, T13 and T15 re-reviewed and reopened (2026-10-31).** Their 2026-10-28 `Verdict: PASS` files were not independent reviews: T15's and T13's were review 1 with the writer's rows changed to `fixed`, and T11's was written by the agent that wrote the fix. Fresh reviewers (no access to earlier reviews, handoffs or commit messages) found T15 1 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM (scope depth for scope identity), T13 2 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM (copies of T15's `bindMain`/`bindTest`; span equality for argument identity) and T11 3 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM (`afterMembersDeclared`, withdrawn parser diagnostics, a re-implemented `functionIsInstance`); two of the three `mutation-exempt` lines broke the exemption rule. The three tasks are unticked and redone on `feat/010-t{11,13,15}-redo2`, reviews in `reviews/T{11,13,15}.md`. The same day the guard was found to count a mutant the Bayan compiler rejects as killed: its per-mutant `dotnet build` never compiles `.byn`, so Q712's "mutants that do not compile no longer count" was false until `scripts/selfhost/mutant-outcome.sh` (tested by `mutant-outcome.test.sh`) replaced it. Resolved.
718. **010 dispatcher: `bindMain`/`bindTest` take the shared refs (Q583, Q714).** *Decided (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* T13 cannot build the old arguments from `c.mainStatements`/`c.testBodies` (a `List<parser.GlobalStatement>` or `List<parser.Expr>` built from the tree is BYN2780), so the entry points take what T13 holds and resolve the nodes against `c.files[f].unit.members`. Landed: `void bindMain(ref Binder b, through ref Ctx c, for in List<SyntaxRef> statements)` (binder.byn:541): each ref's `file`/`declIndex` must be a `.globalStatement`, else it panics (`internal error: a main statement ref is not a top-level statement`); the first gives `firstStatementFile`/`firstStatementSpan` (Q719) and the block span, as C#'s `statements[0]` does (BindMain, Binder.cs:387-394). The caller passes a copy of `c.mainStatements` (it cannot lend `c.mainStatements` while passing `c` by `ref`). Tested by `MainMatches`. Landed: `void bindTest(ref Binder b, through ref Ctx c, for TestBody body)` (binder.byn:566): `body.decl` must be a `.testDecl`, else it panics (`internal error: a test body ref is not a test`); `hasValues` false is C#'s null `values`, and when true `body.values` names an argument of that test's own `@cases` (`memberIndex` the attribute, `itemIndex` the argument), which `t15BindCaseValue` (binder.byn:595) turns into C#'s `values[i]`: a tuple's element `i`, or the value alone (Compilation.cs:334). T13's `t13BindBody` makes both calls: `bindMain` with a copy of `c.mainStatements` (generics.byn:921 `bindMain(ref b, through: ref c, for: in statements)`) and `bindTest` with the map's own entry (generics.byn:923 `bindTest(ref b, through: ref c, for: c.testBodies[fn])`), which traps when absent as C#'s `_testBodies[fn]` throws (Q583). Tested by `TestBodyMatches` (`plain` without values; `cased`, `dup`, `mism` with a tuple; `lone` with a lone value). 010-api.md (not T15's file) still lists the old signatures; the dispatcher updates it. Resolved.
719. **010 T15: the first statement is a file and a span; `thisType` from the constructor.** C# keeps `_firstStatement` as the `Stmt` object and T2x's `Panic.handler` check (Binder.cs:1384) asks whether the `assert` is that object. A Bayan statement cannot be referenced out of the `Owned` tree, so Binder's T15 state holds `firstStatementFile` (-1 for none) and `firstStatementSpan`, set by `bindFunctionBody` (binder.byn:342 `b.firstStatementFile = any ? b.file : -1`, :343) and `bindMain` (binder.byn:550-551) from `t15StmtSpan` (binder.byn:80), the full span, not its start. A span stands for the object only if no statement that wraps another has its child's span. Checked in Parser.cs and selfhost/parser: `BlockStmt` (Parser.cs:2133, stmts.byn line 38), `WhileStmt` (:2167, stmts.byn line 71), `DoWhileStmt` (:2177, stmts.byn line 80), `IfStmt` (:2589, stmts.byn line 525), `UnlessStmt` (:2664, stmts.byn line 623), the three `ForStmt` forms (:2716, :2743, :2759; stmts.byn lines 670, 705, 729), `SwitchStmt` (:2812, stmts2.byn line 69) and `ContextStmt` (:2925, stmts2.byn line 180) start at their keyword or `{`, before the child; `WhileLetStmt` (:2162, stmts.byn line 65), `LabeledStmt` (:2220, stmts.byn line 117) and `DeferStmt` (:2886, stmts2.byn line 137) take their span before parsing the child, so it ends before the child starts; `GuardedStmt` (:3111, stmts2.byn line 365) runs to the end of its condition, strictly larger than its child. No wrapper's span equals its child's, so (file, start, length) names one statement. T2x must compare `b.firstStatementFile == b.file && b.firstStatementSpan == a.span` (start and length both) where C# compares `ReferenceEquals(_firstStatement, a)`. The lambda task must save both fields, reset `firstStatementFile` to -1 for the lambda body and restore both after it, as C# does with `_firstStatement` (BinderExpressions.cs:1919-1934). `_thisType` (Binder.cs:54, the container, else `fn.Interface.Self`) is set by `t15CaptureTypes` (Q592), which every entry point calls first, so T13 needs no new call for it; `FunctionSymbol.iface` is set only by T38's `declareInterfaceMembers` (a stub, declare2.byn:11), so `InterfaceSelfMatches` builds the interface and its method by hand. T13 calls the entry points and writes no first statement: `t13BindBody` passes a copy of `c.mainStatements` to `bindMain` (generics.byn:921 `bindMain(ref b, through: ref c, for: in statements)`) and `c.testBodies[fn]` to `bindTest` (generics.byn:923 `bindTest(ref b, through: ref c, for: c.testBodies[fn])`), so ctx.byn's old `i64 firstStatement` is written by nobody and can go (Q583). Tested by `GuardedFirstStatementMatches` (`return if d`), `FunctionBodyMatches`, `MainMatches`, `GetterAndConstructorMatch(copy)` and `InterfaceSelfMatches`. Break-tests, each restored by copying the file back: binder.byn:218 (the `structTypeOf(b.owner)` line) deleted failed `GetterAndConstructorMatch`; binder.byn:220 (the `t15InterfaceSelf` call) deleted failed `InterfaceSelfMatches`; binder.byn:233 `== -1` with `!= -1` failed `InterfaceSelfMatches`; the span length set to 0 failed `GuardedFirstStatementMatches`; binder.byn:550 and :551 each deleted failed `MainMatches`; binder.byn:342 `any ? b.file : -1` with `any ? b.file : b.file` failed `FunctionBodyMatches(flagged, two, empty)` and `GetterAndConstructorMatch(m2)`; binder.byn:341 `let any = body.value.statements.length > 0` with `let any = true` failed `ScopesAndLocalsMatch(outer-first, identity, discard-and-names, same-scope)` among others (the empty body indexes `statements[0]`). Open until T2x and the lambda task use the fields and T13 switches.
720. **010 T11: `runWork` arms no caller reaches yet.** `runWork` runs the lists `declare` drains (`wheres`: `.where`; `pendingInterfaces`: `.interfaceMembers`; `pendingKeys`: `.keyCheck`) and T14's `pendingConstraints` drain (conformance.byn:101 `runWork(ref c, for: in work)`: `.constraint`). Accepted by the dispatcher (2026-10-31) as long as each arm names what makes it reachable. Per arm: `.interfaceMembers` and `declare`'s `pendingInterfaces` drain already run in `declare wheres` (`IOrder<T>` in a `where`), but their only effect is T38's `declareInterfaceMembers` (declare2.byn:12, a stub), so they become observable when T38 lands. `.members`, `.unionVariants` and `.conform`: no C# list holds these; C# runs them at once inside `Instantiating` (Compilation.cs:1630, :1631, :1648), and T13 does the same (generics.byn:644 `declareMembers(ref c, for: id)`, 648 `conform(ref c, for: id)`, :690 `declareUnionVariants(ref c, for: id)`), so nothing will reach these arms and each panics saying so (compile.byn:1170 `panic("internal error: C# runs DeclareMembers`). `.fieldDefault` and `.bindFunction`: C# queues them in `_instantiationWork` (Compilation.cs:1634, :1637), which T13 drains with its own switch (generics.byn:174 `while c.instantiationWork.length > 0 {`), because C# drains with `Instantiating(work.Site, work.Span, work.Bind, work.Instance)` (Compilation.cs:1391-1392), a closure call, not `RunWork`, and the switch ports that closure; they become reachable if T13 drains it through `runWork`. A `.bindFunction` item carries the function in `instance` (dispatcher, 2026-10-31; ctx.byn, conformance.byn:350 `kind: .bindFunction,`), so the arm reads `work.instance`; T13 sets `instance: fn` where `instantiateType` queues it (generics.byn:664 `kind: .bindFunction, args: List<Type>(), instance: fn,`) and where `instantiateFunction` does (generics.byn:427). The reachable arms say so in a comment (compile.byn:1167 `// Its only effect is T38's`). T28: test each arm once its caller or target lands. compile.byn has no mutation-exempt line. `declare`'s `main` check is marked `(blocked: Q720)` (compile.byn:404 `// (blocked: Q720)`): T38's `declareSignature` is a stub, so a user `main` keeps `returnType = -1`, whose `kindOf` is `.errorSet`, and through `declare` the check reports BYN2771 for every `main` of kind `.function`, a valid `void main() { }` included, where C# reports nothing. `declare main-string` (`string main() => ""`) already agrees with C#, which also reports BYN2771 there with the same message, and kills the line's mutant. T38 unblocks the rest: once `declareSignature` sets `returnType`, add a `declare` case with `void main() { }` (nothing). The check itself is compared in the `mainsig` cases, with the types built by hand. Also noticed: T8's `t8MembersDeclared` still returns `false` (typeresolve.byn:86 `bool t8MembersDeclared(in Ctx c) => false`), so any struct or tuple key resolved after `declare` is queued into `pendingKeys` and never run. Open.
721. **010 T13: a `bindFunction` Work's function and C#'s `work.Instance`.** C# queues `(site, span, () => BindFunction(fn), instance)` with `instance` set only by `InstantiateFunction` (Compilation.cs:1532); the struct-instance methods (Compilation.cs:1637) and conformance's cloned defaults (Conformance.cs:184) queue `null`. *Dispatcher decision (2026-10-31):* a `.bindFunction` Work carries the function to bind in `instance` (ctx.byn:146, conformance.byn:350, compile.byn:1179-1182, `runWork`'s `.bindFunction` arm), so generics.byn:427 and :664 set `instance: fn` and the drain binds it (generics.byn:188 `bindFunction(ref c, for: instance)`). The encoding of C#'s `work.Instance` (accepted for now by the dispatcher, 2026-10-31): for a `.bindFunction` Work it is `memberIndex`, set to the instance only by `instantiateFunction` (generics.byn:427 `memberIndex: fn`) and left at its default -1, C#'s null, by the struct-instance methods (generics.byn:664) and conformance's cloned defaults (conformance.byn:350); for a `.fieldDefault` Work `memberIndex` is the field and C#'s `Instance` is always null (Compilation.cs:1634), so the drain reads it as -1; no other kind is queued in `c.instantiationWork`. So: the drain passes it to `instantiatingEnd` (generics.byn:182 `let workInstance = kind == .bindFunction ? target : -1`), and the first-pass rollback keeps a Work unless it is a `bindFunction` whose `memberIndex` is a rolled-back instance (generics.byn:840 `if w.kind != .bindFunction || !t13Contains(in instances, for: w.memberIndex) {`), as C#'s `w.Instance is null || !pass.Instances.Contains(w.Instance)`. A `fieldDefault`'s `memberIndex` is its field, so the kind test keeps a field id from being read as a function. `workInstance` reaches only `instantiatingEnd`'s BYN7012 branch (generics.byn:303), and BYN7012 is reported only by the call binders (BinderCalls.cs:516, T20; BinderCalls.cs:1739, T39), both stubs, so generics.byn:182 carries the file's one `// mutation-exempt: Q721`; add a `drainInstanceMethods` case with a state-changing assignment in a queued body when T20 or T39 lands. Tested by `drainInstanceMethods` (C# drains `_instantiationWork` itself after `InstantiateType(Box, [Tri])`, printing each Work's `Instance`; Bayan runs `bindAll`, printing `memberIndex`) and break-tests (i), (j) of Q584. The first-pass rollback copies every field of a kept Work, including `atSite`/`siteFile`/`siteSpan` (generics.byn:841), as C# keeps the same tuples; no current path observes them there, since C#'s `AfterMembersDeclared` queues its site-wrapped checks in `_pendingKeys` (Compilation.cs:1549-1550), never in `_instantiationWork`, so every Work in `c.instantiationWork` has `atSite` false and no test can tell the copy from one that drops them. New.
722. **010 T14: dispatcher decision: append + truncate stands in for the C# throwaway FunctionSymbol.** C# `Expected` builds a `FunctionSymbol` no collection holds (Conformance.cs:144). *Decided (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* `t14Expected` appends it with `newFunction` (conformance.byn:247), declares it, and returns `t14Drop(ref c, at: fn)` (conformance.byn:279): `t14Drop` takes the symbol as a `t14View` value and removes it only while it is still the arena's last entry (conformance.byn:508). *Review 2 (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* the resolve at :267/:270 (and T38's `declareSignature` at :264) can reach `instantiateType`, whose `declareMembers` and `t14CloneDefault` append functions after the throwaway, so a bare `removeLast` would pop an instance's method; in that case the throwaway stays as an entry no module, `allFunctions` or work item registers (C#'s detached object, unreachable), and binder.byn:450's parameter-owner scan cannot match it because its parameter locals are its own. Normally `c.functions` has its old length when it returns and `conform` holds the symbol as a value (`expected.kind`, `expected.returnType`, `expected.isMutating`). `t14SameShape`, `t14SignatureText` and `t14InsertMember` take a `FunctionSymbol` value (conformance.byn:372, :423, :460); an arena witness is projected with `t14View` (conformance.byn:387). Parameter locals that T38's `declareSignature` will add for a method member stay in `c.locals`, as nothing indexes them but the returned value. Compared in `expected` (`functions +0` against C#'s unchanged `AllFunctions`); break-test :279 of Q588. New.
723. **010 T14: shared fields, kept arena, and what is not compared.** *Shared fields (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* `associatedBindings` and `baseSpans` are in ctx.byn's shared section beside Q714's fields (ctx.byn:459 `Map<string, Type> associatedBindings = []`, ctx.byn:461 `Map<string, TextSpan> baseSpans = []`), keyed as T12 keys them: `"{s} {name}"` and `"{s} {i}"`; value types from C#'s `Dictionary<(StructSymbol, string), TypeSymbol>` and `Dictionary<(StructSymbol, InterfaceSymbol), TextSpan>`. T12 writes them (Compilation.cs:946, :1006) and its redo adds the same two declarations; the dispatcher reconciles the duplicates at merge. The tests' `World` copies both from the C# compilation. *Kept (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* the dead `Map<i64, i64> conformancesChecked` (ctx.byn:356, Q585); nothing reads or writes it since SelfhostSemanticsT13Tests.cs:607 emits `c.checkedConformances = true`. It is deleted at T28 (work/todo.md), since guard check C lets ctx.byn sections only grow. *Empty map for null (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* `t14CloneDefault` stores a copy of the map (conformance.byn:310) where C# stores `null` when it is empty (Conformance.cs:170); an empty `typeMap` stands for C#'s null, so the binder port must treat empty as absent in `typeArgs ?? fn?.TypeMap ?? container?.TypeMap` (Binding/Binder.cs:55). C# never mutates a `TypeMap` after construction, so the sharing is not observable. *Instance order (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* conformed instances follow `c.instanceKeys` insertion order (conformance.byn:73-75); C#'s `_instances.Values` can reuse a freed slot after `_instances.Remove` (Compilation.cs:1737), so diagnostic order may differ only after a first-pass rollback. Dictionary slot order is not part of the language's behaviour; insertion order is kept. *Not compared* (each goes only through an unported stub): (1) interface-method members: `t14Expected`'s `.functionDecl` arm (conformance.byn:264) and `t14CloneDefault`'s (conformance.byn:319) call T38's `declareSignature` (declare2.byn:15, empty), so the expected method signature, the field-for-a-method case (conformance.byn:172), a missing method and BYN2814 through `conform` (conformance.byn:206) wait for T38; add a `checkConformances` struct with a method witness of the wrong `ref this`, one missing a method, and one with a field for a method. The `ref this` fix itself is compared in `refThisFix`. (2) The instance part of BYN2780 (conformance.byn:151-154) and instance bases: an instance's fields and bases come from T12's `declareMembers` (declare.byn:13, ported by the T12 redo; the T14 cases (2) and (5) are owed in SelfhostSemanticsT14Tests.cs, work/todo.md); add a `Box<T> : IList` with a `T items` field instantiated with `List<i64>` when T12 lands. (3) `t14CloneDefault`'s interface-template branch (conformance.byn:288-296): an interface instance's members come from T38's `declareInterfaceMembers` (declare2.byn:12, empty); add a generic interface with a default conformed through an instance when T38 lands. (4) `t14RefThisFix`'s `file != c.structs[s].file` (conformance.byn:484): `conform` passes only witnesses of `s` itself, so it is unreachable there, as in C# (Conformance.cs:233). (5) `t14Drop`'s left-in-arena path (conformance.byn:508 false): needs an interface getter typed with an instance (`Box<Item>`) whose `declareMembers` (T12) appends methods; add that `expected` case when T12 lands. (6) The `checkConformances` `work … at` lines are rebuilt from C#'s `_baseSpans` (SelfhostSemanticsT14Tests.cs:483-485) because `Compile` drains the C# queue before it returns; this matches `CloneDefault` enqueueing at `at` (Conformance.cs:184). *Resolved (dispatcher, 2026-10-31):* gaps (1)-(6) are accepted until T12/T38 land, per the Q584 policy; each owner adds the named case. New.
724. **010 dispatcher: mutation exemptions cover spans, each cited (2026-10-31).** The guard allowed one `// mutation-exempt: Qnnn` per file, exempting the next line. T16's `binder2.byn` has two stub-only regions (the `assert … fails` set check after T20's `bindCall`, and the untyped-local arm after T22's `built`, errorcases.byn:15 `=> -1`), and sampling hits a different line of them each run, so no test could make the guard pass. *Decided (dispatcher):* a marker may exempt a span (`// mutation-exempt: Qnnn through N`, lines after the marker to N), a file may carry several, and each marker's Question must cite a line of its span as `file.byn:L` or `file.byn:A-B`; `scripts/selfhost/mutation-exempt.py` checks this and `mutation-exempt.test.sh` tests it. This replaces the once-per-file limit Q594(g) mentions. The independent review still judges whether each span is stub-only. Spec 013's compiled mutant schemata replace the sampler.

729. **010 T20: `bindCall`, `bindFunctionCall` and `bindParse` also take the whole `parser.Expr` (dispatcher, 2026-11-01).** C# `ReportUnhandled(Expr c, string name)` (BinderCalls.cs:944) is called with the `CallExpr` itself (:177, :242); Bayan `reportUnhandled` takes a `parser.Expr`, which the inner `parser.CallExpr` cannot supply. Q633 updated. The same T38 double-fill broke three more harnesses, each failing alone, not only together: (1) T21: `Checks` made its own `requires` function, appended a second `StructChecks` and repointed `checksOf[s]` (SelfhostSemanticsT21Tests.cs, old :370, :381-382) over the entry T38's `declareCheck` now makes (declare2.byn:178-179, C# Compilation.cs:1072 in DeclareCheck), so `bindAll` found no owner for T38's entry and panicked indexing `c.structs[-1]` (generics.byn:118) in all 98 cases. Both `Signatures` fills are removed with their `tcParam`/`tcSet`/`tcNth`/`BayanType`/`Instance` helpers and the overload-list rewrite, which T12's `checkOverloads` no longer needs on real signatures. 739. **010 T40: `for try` synthetic names report at the iterable.** C# `BindForTry` gives `<sequence N>` and `next` the iterable's span (`new Name(span, …)`, `span = f.Iterable.Span`, Binding/Binder.cs:1110-1115). The port keeps their text out of the source: `t28SyntheticName` (binder3.byn:211) still returns a span with `start` -1 - index into `c.syntheticNames`, which `t15Text` (binder.byn:11) and `t18Text` (express2.byn:29) read. It now also takes the iterable span (`at: span`, the `span` of binder3.byn:165) and appends it to `c.syntheticSpans` (ctx.byn:560, `// ── T40 state`), parallel to `c.syntheticNames`. Diagnostics leave the binder at one place, `addDiag` (diag.byn:36): it maps the diagnostic's span, its fix span and each related span through `t40RealSpan` (diag.byn:67), so a synthetic span becomes the iterable's span and any other span is unchanged. `t13Add` (generics.byn:74) skips `addDiag`, but it only re-adds diagnostics from bags that `addDiag` filled, and the related spans it builds come from their already-mapped `d.span` (generics.byn:316). The typed dump prints only function and local spans (typed.byn:34, :45), and the `<sequence N>` local's `nameSpan`/`span` were already set to the iterable (binder3.byn:173-174), so the dump needed no change. Before this, a `next` that was found but not visible (BYN2005 through `checkAccess(…, at: member)`, express2.byn:358) recorded a negative span and the renderer panicked (`offset out of range`, exit 134). Covered by `diag/for-try-next-not-visible` (no `package.byn`: `bayan check` parses one as a module and reports BYN1012) and SelfhostSemanticsT40Tests. Break-test: diag.byn:39 changed to `m.span = m.span` fails all 5 SelfhostSemanticsT40Tests (`spans.inplace` BYN2005 -1..-1 where C# gives 88..89, `spans.copy` -3..-3, the check and golden facts panic `offset out of range`, exit 134), L022 on `diag/for-try-next-not-visible` and L023 (the renderer panic on the golden). Resolved.
740. **010 T40: `AddDiagMapsFixAndRelated` has no C# oracle.** No C# path records a fix span or a related span on a `for try` synthetic name: the C# names carry the iterable span from the start, so it never maps one. The `for try` programs compared here (diag/for-try-next-not-visible and the T40 `inplace`/`copy` programs) report only BYN2005, with no fix and no related span. The fact (SelfhostSemanticsT40Tests.cs:81, `// no-oracle: Q740`) calls `t28SyntheticName` with the span 7..10, then `addDiag` with that name as span, fix span and first related span, plus a real related span 2..3, and checks that all three map to 7..10 and that 2..3 is unchanged. That covers diag.byn:40 and :42, which no oracle case reaches. Break-tests: diag.byn:40 changed to `m.fixSpan = m.fixSpan` fails `AddDiagMapsFixAndRelated` (`fix -1..-1`); diag.byn:42 changed to `= m.related[i].span` fails it (`related -1..-1`). Resolved.

Dispatcher commit 1e70eb9 added `// ── T40 state` to both `Ctx` (ctx.byn:558) and the binder's cursor struct, and the guard passed after it was merged. 742. **Windows stdout newlines.** A Bayan program's `print`, `Io.stdout` and stderr writes go through the C runtime's text mode on Windows, so each `\n` reaches the pipe as `\r\n`; stdin is already read in binary mode (`byn_io_read_stdin`). Two options: (a) keep text mode (CRLF, current); (b) put stdout and stderr in binary mode (LF everywhere, like stdin; Go and Rust write what the program wrote). The CI fix for the Windows run did not decide this: the tests that compare program output now read child-process text with `\r\n` as `\n` (`ProcessText.ReadToEndLf`, the rule `Golden.Compare` uses), so they pass either way. Text mode stays meanwhile. *Resolved 2026-11-02 (user): (b), binary-mode stdout/stderr in the runtime, C# CLI writes LF; see LfOutputTests.*
743. **Windows path model in the selfhost port.** The port treats only `/` as a separator and only a `/` prefix as rooted, where the C# uses `Path.*` (Windows: `\`, drive roots). Sites: compile.byn:1271 `t11DirectoryName`, :1287 `t11FullPath` (C# Compilation.cs:93), :1330 `t11Combine` (Compilation.cs:110, 187), :1337 `t11RelativePath` (Compilation.cs:116, 209); typed.byn:137 `t26PathOf` (TypedDump.cs:89-90); json.byn:35 `t26FileName`. 77 Windows CI failures (run 41318084615). User decision 2026-11-01: port the C# behaviour through scripts/selfhost/land.sh. Blocked (dispatcher, same day): the C# result depends on the host OS (`Path.DirectorySeparatorChar`, drive roots), and a Bayan program has no way to ask which OS it runs on and no working directory (Q571), so the port cannot choose; inferring it from a path's shape would be an invented fallback. Needs a language decision first, one of: (a) a target/OS query in the standard library (e.g. a compile-time constant the backend fills per target), then the port branches on it; (b) a standard-library path module (`Path.combine`, `fullPath`, `relative`, `directoryName`, `fileName`) implemented in the runtime per OS, which the port calls; (c) leave the port `/`-only and mark Windows unsupported for `bayan-check`. *Resolved 2026-11-02 (user): (b), a std Path module: `combine`, `fileName`, `directoryName` pure; `fullPath` carries the process/fs effect; Windows drive letters, UNC paths and both separators; `relative` compares case-insensitively on Windows; no `Target.os`. Spec: docs/specs/014-std-path-module/014-spec.md (draft). Until it lands, the Windows CI job marks the Q743 failures as known.* Closed by 014 (Q1006).
744. **L018/L023 proof tier (user 2026-11-02: enact at 011 start, before L025; two 30-min proofs per merge too slow).** Proposal, for the user (open):
   - **Quick tier, before every merge.** Each proof test reads `BAYAN_LAW_TIER`. Unset means quick: a fixed, seeded subset of its corpus, sized to finish in about 3 minutes on the Mac (L018: the 128 corrupted seeds plus the first N of the 4,000 random inputs; L023: every golden plus the first N mutations). The law file's `check:` stays as it is, so `laws-check.js --run` runs quick, and `timeout:` drops from 1800 to 300. The subset is the same on every run, so a failure reproduces.
   - **Full tier, nightly and before push.** `BAYAN_LAW_TIER=full` runs the whole corpus. A scheduled GitHub workflow runs it nightly, and `scripts/selfhost/pre-push-laws.sh` runs it locally before the user pushes (it never pushes).
   - N is measured when the laws are enacted, not guessed: time per input from one full run, then N = 180 s / that time.
   - Rejected: a `check-full:` field in `~/.claude/tools/laws-check.js`. It changes a tool every repo shares for one repo's need.
   - Rejected: a rotating random subset. It covers more over time, but a failure on Monday's subset may not reproduce on Tuesday.
   - Cost: a regression that only the full corpus hits is caught up to a day late (or at push), not at merge.

747. **A `ref this` store into a map field escapes the store summary (found 2026-11-03 by the review of 22e4e844..e1b970c4; fixed 2026-11-03 on `fix/q747`).** Resolution: C# `IsThisRooted` gains `BoundBuiltinCall { Member: MapIndexSet or MapSlot } b => IsThisRooted(b.Receiver)` (commit 936f5905); goldens `diag/ref-out-escape-ref-this-map-field` and `-map-slot` now give BYN3002; selfhost `isThisRooted` ported as spec 010 T43 (landed through `land.sh`, review PASS). `ThisFieldSymbol` left unchanged: two probes gave the same BYN3004 with and without a map case there, so no reachable behavior depends on it. Original report: `struct Bag { Map<i64, string> m; void put(ref this, string v) { m[1] = v } }` called as `b.put("ann".copy(to: arena))` inside a `using let arena` block, then `print(b.m[1])` after it: `bayan check` accepts (exit 0) and `bayan run` prints garbage; the same store written inline (`b.m[1] = name`) gets BYN3002, as does a plain field write through `ref this`. Cause: `IsThisRooted` (`src/Bayan.Semantics/Binding/RegionAnalysis.cs:846-853`, from `StoreInto` :703) has no `BoundBuiltinCall` `MapIndexSet`/`MapSlot` case, so no (v, this) pair is recorded, and `BuiltinStores` (:439) stores only the key; `ThisFieldSymbol` (:861-868) lacks the same case (changed-fields tracking, :502-504, untested). The selfhost port mirrors it (`selfhost/semantics/region2.byn:450`, `isThisRooted` :647-662). Not a regression: before Q745 every `ref this` store was accepted. Fix: C# first with a diag golden (map value and `MapSlot`), then the selfhost port through `land.sh`.
748. **L018/L023 quick-tier N (011 P1, 2026-11-03; answers the sizing in Q744).** `BAYAN_LAW_TIER` unset runs the quick tier: L018 the 128 corrupted seeds plus the first N = 400 of its 4,000 random inputs; L023 every golden, the 79 seeds and the CLI path plus the first N = 1,000 of its 10,000 random inputs (`KnownCSharpThrows` is asserted only for the random indices below N). `full` runs everything. The seeded generators write the same prefix whatever the corpus size, so a quick failure reproduces. **Measured on the Mac, and it does not match Q744's premise:** L018 alone full 10 s, L023 alone full 74 s (before the tier existed), quick and full together 32 s and 54 s. Both full tiers are already under 3 minutes here, so N cannot be "180 s / time per input" (that exceeds the corpus). I set N to one tenth of each random corpus (Q744's 30 minutes to 3 minutes) and wrote the measurement into both law pages; if the 30-minute figure was from a slower machine, N is a guess to revisit when it is measured there. The laws are `status: enacted` with `timeout: 300`, as Q744 proposes; the `check:` lines are unchanged.
749. **Landing scripts take the spec from `scripts/selfhost/specs.tsv` (011 P1, D7).** One tab-separated table (spec, dir, tasks, plan, api, shared-state files, bare-`.byn` directory, test-class prefix, base branch, review/land/tick subjects, tmp prefix), rows 010 and 011. Selection is an explicit argument: `land.sh [spec] T<n> <branch>` (two arguments mean 010), `--spec <nnn>` on `guard.sh`, `wave-brief.py`, `review-brief.py` (default 010), and a fourth argument on `guard-checks.py`; never the branch name. Row 010 stays byte-identical: its guard line carries no `--spec` (only other rows' lines end in `--spec 011`, which `land.sh` passes through), so the 010 prompt for T10, T28 and T43 is the same file as before and `land.test.sh`'s stub still sees `--base base --filter F`. `wave-brief.test.sh` compares T43's writer and review briefs with those of commit 8dae45cc and skips when that commit is not in the clone. The task-line parser cuts the `files:` field at ` — C#:` (011 names its C# range there; 010 has none), or the C# file would be allowed as a test file.
750. **What "area" means in the `land.sh` dry run (011 P1).** The guard's scope check (`--allow`, plus the handoff, `work/todo.md`, tasks files, reviews and the row's shared-state files) is the only per-row area there is, so `guard.sh --scope-only` stops after checks 1 and 2 and `land.sh --check-scope [spec] T<n> <branch>` runs it in the landing worktree, with no review, guard run, merge or tick. `land-rows.test.sh` runs it per row on a throwaway repo with the real `wave-brief.py`, `guard.sh` and `specs.tsv`: the row's `.byn` file and shared-state files are accepted (010 by the old two-argument form), the other row's shared-state file and a `.byn` outside the task's `--allow` are refused with `scope: <file> is outside --allow`, an unknown spec is refused, and it fails if the 011 row is gone.
751. **The 011 writer and review briefs are parameterised in their paths only (011 P1).** `wave-brief.py --spec 011` writes `tmp/011-<t>/prompt.md` with the 011 tasks file, base `feat/011-self-hosted-emitter` (`BAYAN_BASE` still overrides), `selfhost/emitter/` for bare names, `FullyQualifiedName~SelfhostEmitterT<n>Tests` (or the task's named test class), and the handoff plus `011-tasks.md` always allowed. The 010-only gates stay 010-only (T28's `SelfhostSemantics` filter, the docs-only `SelfhostSemanticsApiTests`). The prose of the brief (a type checker ported from `src/Bayan.Semantics/`, the `SelfhostSemanticsHarness` section, the C#-oracle test advice) is still spec 010's: rewriting it for the emitter is a dispatcher or T1 decision, not a path. `guard-checks.py` check C now covers every shared-state file of the row (011: `lctx.byn`, `cprint/cctx.byn`), naming the file in its message; for 010 the messages are as before.
752. **`pre-push-laws.sh` and `laws-nightly.yml` (011 P1, D11).** `pre-push-laws.sh` runs `BAYAN_LAW_TIER=full dotnet test -v q --filter "Law=<id>"` for the `id:` of every `docs/laws/0*.md` with `status: enacted` (23 today, including the non-selfhost laws), continues past a failure and exits 1 naming the failed laws; it never pushes. `.github/workflows/laws-nightly.yml` (`cron: '0 4 * * *'`, one hour after the mutation run, plus `workflow_dispatch`) clones the exact commit at depth 1, runs `install-dotnet.sh` and `install-zig.sh` as shell steps as `ci.yml:25-40` does (no `actions/checkout`, no `actions/setup-dotnet`), builds `Bayan.slnx` and runs the script; `timeout-minutes: 180` is a guess, nothing measured the whole 23-law full tier on `ubuntu-latest`. Not exercised here: the workflow has not run on GitHub.
753. **Path effects (011 P2, 2026-11-03; dispatcher decision).** `Path.isRooted` takes no effect; `Path.relative` and `Path.fileName` carry `alloc` and return fresh strings that borrow nothing (`EffectAnalysis.cs`, `RegionAnalysis.cs` allocated-from-context list and `BuiltinResults`, `PanicHandlerCheck.cs` allocation list). None takes io, fs or process, although `relative` reads the working directory to make a relative input full, as .NET's `GetRelativePath` does; a pure-string `relative` would differ from .NET on relative inputs.
754. **T44 widened (011 P2, 2026-11-03; dispatcher decision).** Spec 010 T44 ports the `Path` builtin kind, its three members, their `BuiltinFunction` cases and their effect and region entries to `selfhost/semantics/` (`builtins.byn`, `express.byn`, `express2.byn`, `types.byn`, `symbols.byn`, `region2.byn`, `ownership.byn`), mirroring the C#; `SelfhostSemanticsT9Tests` and `SelfhostSemanticsT3Tests` gain the Path rows. `effects.byn` (`t23Builtin`'s alloc line) carries the effect entry and is in T44's file list.
755. **Path's Windows branch follows .NET; the first wp1 run found three gaps, fixed in 011 P2 fix 2 (2026-11-04).** `src/runtime/bayan-rt.c`'s `_WIN32` branch mirrors .NET: `PathInternal.GetRootLength` (device `\\?\` and `\\.\`, `\??\`, UNC, `\`, `C:`, `C:\`), both separators, blank paths effectively empty, and full paths through `GetFullPathNameW` followed, when the result has a `~`, by `byn_path_expand_short`, a line-by-line port of `PathHelper.TryExpandShortFileName`. That port uses `GetLongPathNameW` through a `\\?\` or `\\?\UNC\` form, trims one segment at a time on not-found, puts back the part that does not exist, and restores `\\.\`. An extended `\\?\` path is returned as-is. The buffer sizes are .NET's: 260 units (`stackalloc char[MaxShortPath]`), then `ArrayPool` power-of-two growth. The first port used a buffer of the input's length, so a longer long name went through the grow-and-retry branch after the temporary NUL had been put back, and `C:\PROGRA~1\a` stayed unexpanded on wp1. UTF-8 to UTF-16 uses the runtime's maximal-subpart decoder (as `Encoding.UTF8`), and the way back makes a lone surrogate U+FFFD; `MultiByteToWideChar` gave `ED A0 80` two U+FFFD where .NET gives three. `StdPathTests.ShortNamesExpandAsDotNet` (Windows only) prints `GetFullPath` against the runtime for `PROGRA~1`, a non-existent `NOPE~1` tail, `\\.\` and a path longer than 260 units, through the native driver with a `from` on another root. On wp1 at 660ccd78 plus the regenerated table, `StdPathTests` passes 4 of 4.
756. **Path case folding follows .NET, per OS (011 P2, 2026-11-03; per-OS tables 2026-11-04).** `relative` decodes both full paths to UTF-16 units. On `_WIN32` and `__APPLE__` (.NET's `IsCaseSensitive` false) it compares roots with `OrdinalIgnoreCase` as `OrdinalCasing.CompareStringIgnoreCase` does (a unit by `OrdinalCasing.ToUpper`, a surrogate pair by `CharUnicodeInfo.ToUpper` of its scalar), and the common prefix with `char.ToUpperInvariant` per unit; elsewhere both are ordinal. .NET's casing differs by OS (Windows .NET 10 leaves U+019B, U+0264, U+1C8A, U+A7CD, U+A7CF, U+A7D3, U+A7D5 and their pairs unmapped), so the runtime has one generated block per OS, `#if defined(_WIN32)` and `#else` (macOS; Linux compiles it but compares ordinally), with no fallback. `StdPathTests.CaseTablesMatchDotNet` checks all 65,536 units and every supplementary scalar against the running .NET, and with `BAYAN_UPDATE=1` rewrites only the running OS's block. The Windows block was generated on wp1 (Windows 11, .NET 10) at 9d838eb2. The corpus pairs é/É, ß/ẞ, ı/I, ς/Σ, ſ/S and 𐐨/𐐀 against live .NET; `/é/a` to `/É/b` gives `../b`. Bytes that are not UTF-8 decode to U+FFFD per maximal subpart, as `Encoding.UTF8` does, on every OS; `StdPathTests.InvalidUtf8MatchesDotNet` checks this through a native driver, since no Bayan string holds such bytes.
757. **Path edge cases (011 P2, 2026-11-03).** `Path.relative` panics ("the path is empty", or a NUL byte) where .NET throws `ArgumentException`; `StdPathTests` skips the pairs .NET throws on. No Windows run golden: `// os: unix` marks `run/path-relative.byn` (its outputs depend on posix rules), there was no `// os: windows` marker (014 T6 added it, `RunTests.cs:47`, Q936), and Windows output cannot be generated here and must not be typed by hand. `path-is-rooted` and `path-file-name` use OS-neutral inputs only.
758. **011 T1: how much of semantics is `public`, and what the checker made of it (2026-11-03; conservative).** Public: every struct, enum, union, alias and field in `ctx.byn`, `bound.byn`, `types.byn` and `symbols.byn` (a struct literal in another module needs its fields public), and only the functions `Lowerer.cs` and `CEmitter.cs` call (all of `bound.byn`'s but `realText` and `constantText`; the curated `types.byn` list; the non-`new*` functions of `symbols.byn`; `create`, `fromPath`, `fromProject`; `t26Symbols`, `t26ParseBuildOptions`, `t26Compile`, `t26Failed`). Each public function declares the effects the checker inferred (BYN6002 asks for them: `alloc` on the bound constructors, `fs, clock, console, alloc` on the compile entry points), and each is indexed in `011-api.md`. The CLI half of `semantics/main.byn` moved to `semantics/cli.byn` (D2) so `bayan-emit` shares it. If a later task needs another function it adds `public` and its effect clause and one `011-api.md` line. Open: an effect clause on a public function is part of its signature, so a callee that later gains an effect forces the clause up the call chain; accepted.
759. **011 T1: the lowered tree is the `ltree` module, and the arenas are an `LTree` (2026-11-03; deviation from D1).** Import cycles are rejected (BYN2010), so the lowered-tree types (`LKind`, the `L*` structs, `LoweredFunction`, `LoweredProgram`, `WriteSink`) live in `selfhost/emitter/ltree/`, imported by `emitter` and `emitter.cprint`. The per-kind arenas, which the plan puts on `LCtx`, are the struct `LTree` held as `LCtx.tree`, so the printer takes `in LTree` without the lowerer's state: `lower(ref Ctx c, to ref LCtx l)` takes an `LCtx` the caller owns (not in the C# signature), `cprint.emit(ref Ctx c, from in LTree t, through in LoweredProgram program, by bool ownershipChecks)` does not take one. Node constructors are `addLX(ref LTree t, from move LX n)` (the `addX` form of `bound.byn`), not one parameter per field, because the particle rule allows one unlabeled parameter. `LoweredProgram` gains `testFunctions` (the C# `LoweredProgram` has the test bodies in a second list; kept apart from `functions` so the printer's order is the C# order). `CFunc` has no `sb` field: a struct cannot hold a `StrBuf` (BYN3001), so the emitting functions will take a `ref StrBuf`. Stub signatures took particles (`from`, `through`, `for`, `at`, `by`, `as`) to satisfy BYN5004/5006; T2 to T11 may rename them, each change updating `011-api.md`.
760. **011 T1: small state choices in `LCtx` and the lowered records (2026-11-03).** (a) `_targets` is `Map<i64, LTarget>` keyed by `JumpTarget.id` (D6), with `LTarget {breakLabel, continueLabel?, depth}` for the C# tuple. (b) `LKind.never` and `LUnionTag.union`/`LUnionField.union` are `neverValue` and `unionValue` because `never` and `union` are keywords; the arena for `LNever` is `neverValues`. (c) `_shown`/`_ran` are `Map<BExpr, BExpr>` and `Map<BExpr, LocalId>` with a `showing: bool` standing for `_shown != null`. (d) C# `HashSet<T>` is `Map<T, bool>` (Q449). (e) `lKindBase` (100) is a file-private `const`, since `public const` does not parse; `lNode`, `isLowered`, `lKindOf` and `lIndexOf` are the public face. (f) `SymbolMark` is `const symbolMark: u32 = 1` (a code point). (g) `LFunctionValue.env` is a `LocalId` (-1 for none) and carries the `// Q1: round 4 redoes this` marker at the port of `LoweredNodes.cs:118`. Each is the conservative reading; T2 to T11 may change one with a line here.
761. **011 T1: `bayan-emit`'s argument scan (2026-11-03).** `main.byn` scans `--ascii`, `--mode`, `--tests` and `--color <when>` itself and hands the rest to `t26ParseBuildOptions`; `--color` is consumed and ignored (the emitter prints no diagnostics in colour), and `--tests` is parsed but unused until T12. An unknown mode is a usage error (exit 2, `bayan: unknown mode ...`), checked before the compile. T12 owns the full CLI and may move this into `cli.byn`.
762. **011 T1: the wp1 Windows count was not measured (2026-11-03; for the dispatcher).** The plan has T1 run every `run/` input through `bayan-emit` and `CliApp.EmitC` on wp1 and record the failing inputs in `011-api.md`. T1 has no Windows host and `bayan-emit` prints no C yet (`lower` and `emit` are stubs), so there is nothing to compare. The `bayan-emit` against `CliApp.EmitC` count stays with T12.
763. **011 T2: names and helpers that differ from the C# in `lower.byn` and `cprint/common.byn` (2026-11-04).** `Become` (Lowerer.cs:215) is `lowerBecome` (selfhost/emitter/lower.byn:342), since `become` is a keyword. C# expression-building calls are file-private functions named after what they build: `boolLiteral`, `i64Literal`, `notExpr`, `andExpr`, `orExpr`, `localExpr`, `isNeverExpr` and `isVoidExpr`. `Any` (Lowerer.cs:275) is `anyNode`, with its `Func` test as the `T2AnyTest` union and `t2Passes`. None of these is in `011-api.md`, so the brief's rule makes them private `t2` helpers: `t2Type` (a bound or lowered expression's type), `t2Span`, `t2Children`, `t2IsExpr` (selfhost/emitter/lower.byn:218-284), and `t2Copy` (selfhost/emitter/cprint/common.byn:160; a list copy, so `c` can be passed by `ref` beside a list read from it, BYN3005). `semantics.addLocal` (selfhost/semantics/bound.byn:1211) resolves inside lower.byn to selfhost/semantics/binder.byn:260's private `addLocal` (BYN2005), so `localExpr` inlines its body and calls the public `makeBound` (selfhost/emitter/lower.byn:204-208). `cType` and `helper` declare `uses alloc`, which their `011-api.md` lines do not have; the API test compares signature prefixes, so it passes. The C# `Helper` (CEmitter.cs:591-597) takes a `Func<string>` body; the port splits it into `helperReserve` (selfhost/emitter/cprint/common.byn:229, CEmitter.cs:593-595: false when `name` is registered, else reserves `(proto, "")` and appends `name` to `helperOrder`) and `helperFill` (selfhost/emitter/cprint/common.byn:237, CEmitter.cs:596-597: stores `proto + " " + body` and returns `name`), and `helper` (selfhost/emitter/cprint/common.byn:170) is `if helperReserve(...) { helperFill(...) }` then `name` (Q840). `helper` takes a body that is already built, so it fits only bodies that register no helper; a T6 to T11 caller whose body registers helpers writes `if helperReserve(...) { <build body>; helperFill(...) }`, which reserves the outer name first as the C# does (D5). `mapLine` compares `StrBuf.length` in bytes with itself, where the C# compares UTF-16 units; this changes no output. 765. **011 T2: `captureGuard` and `BIf.guarded` (2026-11-04; Q842).** Lowerer.cs:296-297 `CaptureGuard` matches `BoundIf { Syntax: GuardedStmt, Else: null }`. A selfhost `BIf` keeps no syntax, so T2 added `public bool guarded = false` to `BIf` (selfhost/semantics/bound.byn:955) and `guarded: true` to the `BIf` that `bindStatement`'s `.guardedStmt` case builds (selfhost/semantics/binder2.byn:287); no other 010 code changed. `captureGuard` (lower.byn:489-504) returns `body` unless it is a bound `ifStmt` (the `isLowered` test stands for C#'s type test: a lowered handle is never a `BoundIf`) with `guarded` set and no `else`; otherwise it adds a copy of the `BIf` whose condition is `spill(lowerExpr(condition))`, the other fields copied as C#'s `with` does. `Synth_MatchesCSharp` compares it on the `gd` fixture's five `defer`s (`print(..) if f`, `print(..) unless f`, `if` without and with `else`, a plain call) and on an empty block: whether the result is `body`, is an `if`, keeps `then`, has no `else`, has a temp condition, and how many statements it emitted. 766. **011 T2: what the T2 tests compare, and what they do not yet (2026-11-04).** `SelfhostEmitterT2Tests` builds the emitter with a generated `main.byn` whose modes print what the ported functions return, and compares each line with the C# run in-process (`Lowerer.Lower`, `CEmitter` through its private constructor, `FunctionLowerer` and `FunctionEmitter` through reflection). `t2Type`'s `default` (now `ltree.typeOf`'s, ltree.byn:460, marked `coverage-exempt`; Q856) takes only the statement kinds `label` to `claim`; their C# records are `BoundStmt`s (LoweredNodes.cs:27-78), and `BoundStmt` (BoundNodes.cs:254) has no `Type`, so the C# has no such path. It compares these:
    - Program shape (`lower`).
    - `cType` of every parameter and return type of every lowered function, then `errorCType` and `typeOrder`.
    - For each top-level local initializer: `isTrivial`, `isRepeatable`, `isLvalue`, `hasEffects`, `moves` against the earlier locals, and how many statements and temps `spill` and `emitEffect` add.
    - `line`, `lineOf`, `loc` and `mapLine`, with and without a `#line` path. The C# is given `"a.byn"` when it has none.
    - `helper` registering twice, and a nested registration through `helperReserve`/`helperFill` against a C# `Helper` whose body registers two helpers (one the outer name).
    - `key` and `cType` of every parameter, return and top-level local type (`keys`).
    - Program shape with tests included (`lowertests`), and of a program with warnings.
    - `Synth_MatchesCSharp` (`synth` mode, the `SynthFixture` program): every lowered expression kind through `t2Type`, `t2Span`, the predicates, `t2IsExpr`, `moves`, `anyNode`, `emitEffect` and `spill`; a tuple element (`t.q`), a move of a lowered node and of a field, and assignments whose target, or neither side, reads the moved local; every lowered statement kind; `key` and `cType` of the `Io`, `Hex`, `Utf8`, `IoStream`, `IoInput` and `Path` builtins and a text view; `note`, `newLabel`, `i64Literal`, `boolLiteral`, `andExpr`, `orExpr`, `notExpr`, `emitAssign`, `operands`, `captureGuard` (an empty block and the `gd` defers, Q765), `emitCleanups`/`emitCleanup`/`lowerOutside` over every cleanup kind, `lowerBecome` and `lineOf` for a function with no file. The C# side calls `FunctionLowerer`'s private methods by reflection.

    These run over every `tests/cases/run/` file that compiles in C#, each alone in a temporary directory. There are three failure paths: lowering a compilation with errors (four programs, Q765), `key` of a type parameter, and a program that exits non-zero. `positional-requires.byn` skips the `pred` and `keys` sections only: the selfhost binder's synthesized `requires` body has one more local declaration than the C# body (whose 4th is `violations`, a `BoundCollection`). That is a 010 binder divergence, not traced further here. Some functions cannot be compared until their callees exist: `operands`, `lowerBecome`, `emitAssign`, `captureExpr`, `emitCleanups`, `emitCleanup` and `lowerOutside` reach T3/T4 stubs (`lowerExpr` and the statement lowering). T3 and T4 add these to the corpus mode. `operands` returns `bool` and fills `values`, so a `false` is the C# `null`. `t2TypeArgs` (common.byn:153) ports CEmitter.cs:372 `TypeArgs`, which is in T6's range and is needed by `cType` and `key`; T6 replaces it with its own. The guard's coverage run first failed in `SelfhostSemanticsHarness.SnapshotSkip`, which resolved module paths against the working directory; the dispatcher fixed it in ca5894f9. The guard then reported 17 items, all blocked by the T3/T4 stubs; they carry `coverage-blocked` markers (Q768). C# `LowerExpr` throws on an `LNever` or `LVoid` input (Lowerer.cs:1084-1085), so a hand-built one has no oracle.

823. **011 T14: the law tiers and their N (2026-11-04).** `BAYAN_LAW_TIER` unset is quick, `full` is the whole corpus (`SelfhostEmitterEquivalenceLawTests.TierSeeds`, `SelfhostEmitterEquivalenceLawTests.cs:32`). The seeds are the generator's 8 fixed ones, then a xorshift64 chain from the first (`state ^= state << 13; >> 7; << 17`), so quick (N = 256) is a prefix of full (N = 1,024); the 8 alone were 1.3 s. L024 measured on the Mac: quick 2,632 comparisons (3 modes x (15 + 3 x 256) generated programs, plus 283 flat `run/` inputs) in about 15 s, full 9,544 in 65 s. L025 adds the faulty programs (`GenerateFaulty`) and 1,000 (full: 10,000) corrupted copies: quick 21 s, full 80 s. L024 fits `timeout: 300`; L025 has `timeout: 1200` (3 corpora x 3 modes x its 120 s bound per `--many` run); N was set from these times, not from the 3-minute target, since the full tier is already under 3 minutes. Directory cases of `run/` are not in the corpus (the `--many` runner compiles flat files alone); `SelfhostEmitterParityTests` covers them.
824. **011 T14: the corpora run through `--many`, one process per mode (2026-11-04).** Each corpus is written to `tmp/l024/<corpus>/` (`tmp/l025/`), run as `bayan-emit --mode m --many <dir>`, and the `== name` sections are split by `SelfhostEmitterEquivalenceLawTests.Sections`. The C# side per file is `Compilation.Create([source], dir)` then `CliApp.EmitC(c, mode)` (the `--package` compile of RunTests.cs:80-82), and for a `*.test.byn` `SelfhostEmitterHarness.TestRunC` (the C `bayan test -v` builds, mode `safe`); a file the C# rejects is removed from the directory first (L025 covers rejected inputs). A `run/` input is compared in the mode its `// mode:` line names (debug 3, safe 278 including the tests, fast 2). The first difference is reported as `corpus/name (mode): line n` with both lines. The generated programs' warnings reach stderr on both sides, so stderr is asserted free of `panic:` only. 850. **011 T21: the syntax side table and its read API.** `parser.Expr` owns its children, so `Ctx` stores a non-owning copy of each recorded node: `ctx.byn` `public List<ExprSyntax> exprSyntaxNodes = List<ExprSyntax>()` holds the nodes and `public Map<i64, i64> exprSyntaxOf = []` maps a bound node handle to its node's index. `ExprSyntax` (bound.byn) carries `kind` (an `ExprSyntaxKind`, one member per `parser.Expr` case), `span`, and the children `Lowerer.Anchor` and `IsLiteral` walk, as indices into the same list (-1 when the case has none): `inner` (`ParenExpr`), `member` (`MemberExpr`, a span), `callee` (`CallExpr`), `left` (`BinaryExpr`), `value` (`IsExpr`), `target` (`IndexExpr`), `condition` (`ConditionalExpr`), `operand` and `op` (`UnaryExpr`). The child nodes are recorded with their parent, so they are not separate entries in `exprSyntaxOf`. The recorders are `syntaxNode` (selfhost/semantics/bound.byn:477 `i64 syntaxNode(ref Ctx c, from in parser.Expr e) uses alloc {`), `recordSyntax` (Syntax is `e`), `recordSyntaxNode` (an index already recorded; -1 records nothing) and `shareSyntax` (Syntax is another bound node's `Syntax`, for the conversions and narrowings C# builds with `operand.Syntax`). The binder computes nothing new: the table is only written. Read API; T21 added these two lines to `011-api.md` itself (round 2), so `SelfhostEmitterApiTests.EveryIndexedEntryPointExists` checks them:
   - `- T21 semantics/bound.byn: ExprSyntax? exprSyntax(in Ctx c, for BNode n)  ← BoundNodes.cs:20 BoundNode.Syntax`
   - `- T21 semantics/bound.byn: ExprSyntax exprSyntaxNode(in Ctx c, at i64 node)  ← BoundNodes.cs:20 BoundNode.Syntax (a walked child)`

   `exprSyntax` is selfhost/semantics/bound.byn:467 `public ExprSyntax? exprSyntax(in Ctx c, for BNode n) {` and returns null when the C# `Syntax` is not an `Expr`; `exprSyntaxNode` is selfhost/semantics/bound.byn:474 `public ExprSyntax exprSyntaxNode(in Ctx c, at i64 node) => c.exprSyntaxNodes[node]`. A synthetic `for try` member name (`t28SyntheticName`, a negative span start) records its C# span, `f.Iterable.Span`, through diag.byn's `t40RealSpan` (selfhost/semantics/bound.byn:570 `i64 syntaxOfMember(ref Ctx c, from in parser.MemberExpr x) uses alloc => syntaxAppend(ref c, from: ExprSyntax { kind: .memberExpr, span: x.span, member: t40RealSpan(in c, for: x.member) })`). 910. **Nightly mutation runs exceed the 6h job limit (2026-11-04; user decision: one recording per shard, cron off meanwhile).** `mutation.yml` runs 83 groups (`mutate-batch.sh --list`) over 4 shards. Each group records its filtered tests once under `BAYAN_SNAPSHOT`, and every filter includes the same heavy classes (`SelfhostSemanticsEquivalenceLawTests`, `GeneratorTests`, `NoPanicLawTests`, `T25`, `T41`, `SelfhostSemanticsTests`). Run 41813419997, shard 4: group `semantics-binder` recorded for 1h59m; its 701 mutants took 54 s (0.077 s each). That is ~2h a group, ~40h a shard. The 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-03 runs were cancelled at 6h02m; in 41813419997 shard 4 got a runner shutdown signal at 2h13m (exit 143, cause not in the log). Decision (user, 2026-11-04): groups share one recording per shard (a union filter, `BAYAN_SNAPSHOT_FILES` naming every file of the shard). As built (`mutate-batch.sh`, merged 2026-11-04) that is one recording per (shard, family): lexer, parser and semantics keep their own test builds, so a 4-shard run records 3 times a shard, each `BAYAN_SNAPSHOT_FILES` naming that family's files in the shard. Consequence the user accepted: a file's mutants can be killed by another task's tests, so per-file scores are no longer isolated to the file's own task tests. A further consequence (review d3348d1b..73f8d661, open): the union depends on `--shard` n and `--files` (semantics: 36 classes unsharded, 14-18 per shard at n=4, 6 for `--files bigint.byn`), so a baseline raised by a wider run can make a narrower run's `check` fail on an unchanged file; today no baseline entry has a mutation score. Building each group's filter from the whole family instead fixes it at ~2x the semantics recording time; decide after the mb1 timing (work/todo.md). Meanwhile the `schedule:` trigger is commented out (`workflow_dispatch` stays); `mutate-batch.test.sh` fails while it is on, and comes off after a `workflow_dispatch` run with the shared recording finishes every shard under 6h.

922. **012 T8: what the libc list holds and how the test finds it (2026-11-04).** `src/runtime/libc-uses.txt` is 84 names, one per line, ordinal order. `SelfhostDriverT8Tests.RuntimeLibc` strips comments, strings and character literals from `bayan-rt.c` and `bayan-rt.h` in one pass, takes every `name(` not preceded by `.`, `>` or a word character, and drops the runtime's own names (`byn_`, `BYN_`, `bynt_`, `bayan_`, `__builtin_` prefixes) and a fixed `NotFunctions` set: statements, types and macros of the language or the platform headers (`if`, `sizeof`, `UINT64_C`, `_Alignas`, `WEXITSTATUS`, `WIFSIGNALED`, `WTERMSIG`, ...) and the function-pointer and macro parameters `hook`, `eq`, `less`, `flush`, `N`, `X`, `_i`, `_u`. The rest must equal the file; a new libc call, or a new callback name, fails the test until it is listed or added to `NotFunctions`. The list includes the Win32 calls of the `_WIN32` branches (`CreateProcessW`, `GetLastError`, ...), which are not libc but are what the runtime takes from the platform, so a Windows-only addition also fails the test. Macros of `<sys/wait.h>` are not listed.

979. **012 T16: `Env.get` as it stands (2026-11-05).** `string? Env.get(string name)` is `BuiltinKind.Env`/`BuiltinFunction.EnvGet` (Builtins.cs `EnvGet`/`FindEnv`, BinderExpressions.cs name and member binding, unknown member `Env.set` gives BYN2003 with `did you mean get`), effects `["env", "alloc"]` (Q971 decided `env`; `alloc` is kept because the result is a copy from `context.allocator`, as the `Path` rows), the region and panic-handler fresh-allocation lists carry it like `PathDirectoryName`, and `CEmitter` writes `bynh_env_get` over `bool byn_env_get(byn_str, byn_str*, byn_alloc*)`. POSIX: a NUL ends the name (.NET passes a C string), a name with `=` is never found (decided by `StdEnvTests` against live .NET: `getenv` on macOS would match `NAME=value`), then `getenv`, the value copied with `byn_env_decode` (`bayan-rt.c:2811-2838`, private: each lone invalid byte and each well-formed sequence cut short is one U+FFFD, as .NET decodes; `byn_utf8_decode_replace` skips the continuation bytes a lead expects and did not match); an empty value is a present empty string. `_WIN32`: `GetEnvironmentVariableW` in a grow loop as .NET (128 wchars, then the size it reports, until the value fits; `bayan-rt.c:2843-2860`), UTF-16 to UTF-8, copied with `byn_utf8_decode_replace` (a UTF-16 value converts to valid UTF-8); `ERROR_ENVVAR_NOT_FOUND` is none. The Windows branch ran on wp1 at 606099bc (`StdEnvTests` filter 20/20, Release). The invalid-UTF-8 value is run on POSIX by `InvalidUtf8ValueMatchesDotNet`: 31 raw byte values set through `/bin/sh`, the Bayan bytes compared with a .NET child's (`OracleChild`); it returns early on Windows, where a UTF-16 value cannot hold invalid UTF-8. `libc-uses.txt` gains `getenv`; `selfhost/driver/runtime.byn` regenerated. `StdEnvTests` (6 facts): `GetMatchesDotNet` (set, empty, non-ASCII, 40000-byte, absent, NUL and `=` names against `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable`; variables removed in a `finally`), `InvalidUtf8ValueMatchesDotNet` with `OracleChild`, `GetNeedsEnvEffect` (BYN6002; its fix help is not compared), `UnknownMemberIsReported` (`Env.set`, full `code line:col message | help` with `did you mean `get`?`), `FarMemberHasNoSuggestion`. The `byn_env_get` prototype sits at the end of `bayan-rt.h`, after `BYN_INT_TYPES(BYN_DEF_ARITH)`, not beside the `Path` declarations: there it shifted the overflow-builtin lines that `011-c-inventory.md:10-16` pins (`CInventoryTests`). A declaration added above those lines later shifts the same rows; that task updates the inventory. Break-test: `bayan-rt.c:2875` `if (name.len > 0 && memchr(name.ptr, '=', (size_t)name.len)) return false;` changed to `if (0) return false;` fails `GetMatchesDotNet`; restored and it passes.
980. **012 T17: `Fs.fileExists` as it stands (2026-11-05).** `bool Fs.fileExists(string path)` is `BuiltinKind.Fs`/`BuiltinFunction.FsFileExists` (Builtins.cs `FsFileExists`/`FindFs`, BinderExpressions.cs name binding and member binding; an unknown member such as `Fs.exists` gives BYN2003 with no suggestion, as `Suggest` finds `fileExists` too far), effect `["fs"]` only (`EffectAnalysis.cs:262`; a `bool` allocates nothing, so Region and PanicHandler rows are unchanged), and `CEmitter.cs:1900` writes `byn_fs_file_exists(path)` directly. Runtime `bayan-rt.c:2887-2929`: as .NET `File.Exists`, an empty path (on `_WIN32` blanks only, `byn_path_effectively_empty`) or a NUL gives false; the path is made full with `byn_path_full` (`Path.GetFullPath`, so `file/.` and `a/../file` are normalised lexically as .NET does); a result ending in a separator is false. POSIX then asks `stat`, and when that fails `lstat` (`bayan-rt.c:2923`): live .NET on macOS says true for a dangling symlink and for a looping one, so a link is an entry, and only a directory is false. `_WIN32`: as .NET `FileSystem.FileExists`/`FillAttributeInfo`: a full path of 260 or more chars gets `\\?\` (`\\?\UNC\` for `\\server\share`; an already extended or device path is left), `GetFileAttributesW`, and on `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` the attributes from `FindFirstFileW`; true when the attributes are read and the directory bit is clear (links are not followed, so a dangling link is true there as well). The Windows branch is pending a wp1 run (the dispatcher records the result). The decided check (Q974) is `File.Exists`, hence not an X_OK test. `byn_fs_file_exists` is declared at the end of `bayan-rt.h`, after `byn_env_get` (so `011-c-inventory.md:10-16` stays pinned). `libc-uses.txt` gains `stat` and `lstat` (the directory test is `st_mode & S_IFMT`, not the `S_ISDIR` macro, which `SelfhostDriverT8Tests` would read as a call) and `SetLastError`, which T16's `byn_env_get` calls and the list lacked (`LibcListIsTheRuntimesLibcCalls` failed); `runtime.byn` is regenerated. `StdFsTests` (3 facts): `FileExistsMatchesDotNet` (about 80 paths against `File.Exists` in one Bayan program: files, an empty file, a non-ASCII name, directories, missing entries, symlinks to a file, a directory, nowhere, itself and an absolute target, `file/`, `file/.`, `file/..`, `file/x`, `sub/../file`, NUL in several places, blanks, `\\` forms, relative paths from the working directory; everything under `tmp/std-fs-corpus`, removed in a `finally`; creating a symlink must succeed, else the test fails naming the row, with no skip; plus a directory chain making a full path over 260 chars, with an existing file, a missing file and the directory), `FileExistsNeedsFsEffect` (BYN6002 compared whole), `UnknownMemberIsReported` (`Fs.exists` and a far name, whole `code line:col message`). Break-test: `bayan-rt.c:2923` `found = (stat(c, &st) == 0 || lstat(c, &st) == 0) && (st.st_mode & S_IFMT) != S_IFDIR;` with `|| lstat(c, &st) == 0` removed fails `FileExistsMatchesDotNet` (dangling link); restored and it passes.

1040. **010-012 tooling: symbol anchors replace line-number pins (user decision 2026-11-05).** A check that names code names it by an anchor, not `file:N`, so an edit above the code no longer fails it (T16's HIGH: `byn_env_get` moved the `bayan-rt.h` rows of `011-c-inventory.md`). An anchor is a fragment in backticks, matched exactly against single lines; an end of the fragment that is a letter, digit or `_` must not touch another one, so `` `byn_env_get` `` is a symbol and does not match `byn_env_get_all`. It must match exactly one line; no line or several is an error naming the anchor. (1) `011-c-inventory.md` rows: `| <file> `<fragment>` | `<token>` | <why> |`, the fragment unique in the whole file and on the hit's line; `CInventoryTests.EveryHitIsARowAndEveryRowHasAHit` resolves each row to `file:line` and compares as before. (2) Coverage markers (`scripts/selfhost/coverage-gate.py`): `// coverage-exempt: Qnnn through `<fragment>`` and `// coverage-blocked: Qnnn T<k> <fn> through `<fragment>``; the marker line is the start anchor, the fragment the end, unique in the rest of the marker's function (the lines after the marker up to the next line starting with `}`), since a last line such as `return -1` repeats across a file. A `through N` line number is a FAIL item. The marker's Question must cite a line of the marker's file, but the cited number is prose (checked by preflight, not by the gate), so it no longer has to fall inside the span. Converted: bound.byn (Q853), binder2.byn (2, Q765), lowerexpr.byn (3, Q774), lowerstmt.byn (Q769, Q780, Q777); each exempts the same lines as before. Not converted: Question prose citations, and `mutation-exempt.py` (spec 015's parity-tested tool; no marker uses it).

1026. **012 T20: `Io.remove`, `Io.createDirectory` and `Io.removeDirectory` in C# and the runtime, as it stands (2026-11-05).** Q1042 (a), decided 2026-11-05: T20 adds both directory builtins; the `build.byn` calls belong to T5, and T20 touches neither `selfhost/driver/build.byn` nor `SelfhostDriverT5Tests.cs`. `Builtins.IoRemove`, `IoCreateDirectory` and `IoRemoveDirectory` (`void Io.x(string path) fails IoError`, `uses fs` in `EffectAnalysis`), the `BuiltinFunction` members, the `Binder` suggestion list and `CEmitter` (`byn_io_remove(path)`, `byn_io_create_directory(path)`, `byn_io_remove_directory(path)`, no helper). `byn_io_remove` (`bayan-rt.c`): an effectively empty path or a NUL gives `notFound`; POSIX `unlink` of the full path (`byn_path_full`, as .NET resolves `.` and `..`), `ENOENT` is a no-op unless the parent of the full path is not an existing directory (then `notFound`, as .NET throws `DirectoryNotFoundException`), `EISDIR` is `permissionDenied`, other errno through `byn_io_error`; Windows `DeleteFileW`, `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` is a no-op. `byn_io_create_directory` (`Directory.CreateDirectory`): empty or NUL is `notFound`, trailing separators are stripped from the full path, `byn_mkdir_all` creates missing parents, an existing directory is success, an existing file is an error; Windows creates each prefix with `CreateDirectoryW`. `byn_io_remove_directory` (`Directory.Delete(path)`, non-recursive): `rmdir` of the full path; a missing, non-empty or file path fails; a symlink to a directory is unlinked, as .NET does (`ENOTDIR` then `unlink`); Windows `RemoveDirectoryW`. Windows branches are unchecked on this host; wp1 to confirm. `libc-uses.txt` gains `unlink`, `DeleteFileW`, `mkdir`, `rmdir`, `CreateDirectoryW`, `RemoveDirectoryW`; the header declarations go at the end of `bayan-rt.h` so the pinned inventory line numbers do not move. `StdFsTests.IoRemoveMatchesDotNet`, `IoCreateDirectoryMatchesDotNet` and `IoRemoveDirectoryMatchesDotNet` run each row through .NET and a compiled Bayan program and compare the outcome and the tree left behind (fixture: empty and non-empty directories, a read-only directory on POSIX, a file, symlinks to a file, a directory and nothing); `Io*NeedsFsEffect` and `IoUnknownMemberSuggestsRemove` compare the diagnostics. 1065. **012 final review: `bayan run` of a program with non-UTF-8 output (needs a user decision).** `selfhost/driver/build.byn` `t5Start` runs the built program through `Io.run`. `byn_process_finish` (`src/runtime/bayan-rt.c`) fails with `invalidUtf8` when the captured stdout or stderr is not valid UTF-8 and drops the exit code, and `t5Start`'s `catch return exitFailure` turns that into exit 1 with nothing printed. The C# `Start` (`CliApp.cs` `Start`) inherits stdio, so it passes the bytes through and returns the program's exit code. Repro: a program that writes FF 41 0A to `/dev/stdout` and returns 7 gives stage 2 exit 1 with empty output, and the C# `ff410a` with exit 7. `Io.runBatch` loses the exit code the same way. This corrects Q1018 (h): the `t5Start` catch is reachable by a test, not only when the executable cannot start, so its `coverage-exempt` marker is wrong. Meanwhile (most conservative, inside spec Q1, which allows no new builtin in 012): the divergence is kept, and such programs stay out of the L028/R10 corpus. Options: (a) keep it until a streaming or inherited-stdio `Io.run` (spec Q5 defers that to 015 S6 or later); (b) decode the captured output lossily with U+FFFD in the runtime, which brings back the exit code but changes `Io.run` for every program, an A1 exception like Q1042; (c) a bytes or inherited-stdio process builtin across C#, runtime and selfhost, about the size of T20. **Decided (user 2026-11-06, Q1065 (a)):** the divergence stays as a known gap tied to the streaming `Io.run` of 015 S6. Fallback if a current test is ever blocked by it: (b) inside `t5Start` only, decoding with `Utf8.decode(bytes, invalid: .replace)` (J82's lossy form, no new API), logged as an A1 exception beside Q1042 and removed when S6 lands. (c) rejected. No test is blocked now: such programs stay out of the L028 corpus. Note for the fallback: `byn_process_finish` fails before `t5Start` sees any bytes, so it needs `Io.run` to hand back the raw bytes first.

1086. **017 T4: `new` and `init` in `selfhost/driver/scaffold.byn`; where it differs from `Scaffold.cs` 18-322.** `scaffoldNew`, `scaffoldInit`, `scaffoldParseOptions`, `scaffoldNames`, `scaffoldWrite`, `scaffoldInitGit`, `scaffoldGit` and `scaffoldFiles` are `New`, `Init`, `ParseOptions`, `Names`, `Write`, `InitGit`, `Git` and `Files` in C# order; main.byn's `new` and `init` cases call `scaffoldNew` and `scaffoldInit`. (a) Bayan raw strings do not interpolate, so each template is a constant with `{kebab}`, `{module}`, `{kind}` or `{command}` that `scaffoldFiles` replaces; `Files` is a `Map<string, string>` and `scaffoldWrite` sorts its keys with `List.sort` (ordinal bytes, as the C# `SortedDictionary` with `StringComparer.Ordinal`). (b) `scaffoldNames` calls `semantics.kebabOf`, `semantics.camelOf`, `semantics.t10IsKebabName` and `lexer.Keywords.build().lookup`; the dispatcher made them `public` (the keyword only; `kebabOf` and `camelOf` also gained `uses alloc`, which a `public` function must declare), so there are no copies; the one branch of `lookup` that `new` cannot reach (a first byte above `z`) carries `coverage-exempt: Q1086` (tokens.byn:334). (c) `Io.writeFile` sets no executable bit and there is no chmod builtin, so a `#!` file (the script layout) gets `chmod a+x` through `Io.run` (scaffold.byn:297), which adds u+x,g+x,o+x as `File.SetUnixFileMode` does; with no `chmod` on `PATH` it panics where the C# succeeds (Q1089). (d) `Io.run` has no working directory (Q1009), so `Git` runs `git -C <dir> <args>`, the substitution Q1009 resolved for every driver command; `git` sees the same directory, so the output matches. (e) The C# lets `Process.Start`, `Directory.CreateDirectory` and `File.WriteAllText` throw uncaught; the driver `panic`s at each `catch`, and the unreachable ones carry `coverage-exempt: Q1086`. (f) `Environment.CurrentDirectory` is `Path.fullPath(".")` in the script branch's relative `shown`. Rooted targets are shown as given.

Options: (a) an `Io.setExecutable(path)` builtin across the C# compiler, `bayan-rt.c` (`stat` + `chmod`, a no-op on Windows) and the selfhost emitter, an A1 exception and the user's call; (b) keep `Io.run("chmod")`, record it, and pin the panic. *Current choice: (b).* Rows that need an empty `PATH` stay out of the L028 corpus. `ScriptWithAnEmptyPathPanicsAtChmod` pins it: non-zero exit, stderr has `cannot make`, the file is written with no execute bit set.
