1100. **017 T10: the C# compiler binds a struct field default `= S {}` to `BoundErrorExpr` when `S` is declared later in the file.** `struct A { B b = B {} }` then `struct B { i64 x = 0 }` and `let a = A {}`: `bayan check` passes, and `bayan build --emit-c` aborts with `cannot lower BoundErrorExpr` (Lowerer.cs:1085). Reproduced 2026-11-07 with the probe `tmp/probe/fwddef/main.byn`; T10 avoids it by declaring `CoverageProbes` before `LoweredProgram` in ltree.byn. Not fixed (outside T10's files). Status: open; for the C# front end (field defaults should bind after all types are declared, or report).

      A second C# bug: `only() catch (G.a) 4` in a function that does not fail, `only` failing `G` (whose only variant is `a`), lowers the propagation of the uncaught variants as `return t1;` of type `byn_err` in an `int64_t` function, and clang rejects it (`returning 'byn_err' ... incompatible result type`). Reproduced 2026-11-07 by `bayan build` and `bayan build --emit-c` on the probe `tmp/probe/catchv/main.byn` (output `tmp/probe/catchv/build.txt`, C in `tmp/probe/catchv/out.c`). Reproduced again (continuation 6) by the C# CLI alone, `src/Bayan.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/bayan build main.byn` in `tmp/probe/catchv`: exit 4, BYN4001 over clang's `main.byn:10:20: error: returning 'byn_err' (aka 'struct byn_err') from a function with incompatible result type 'int64_t'` (output `tmp/probe/catchv/build2.txt`); no selfhost stage runs in the repro, so the bug is the C# compiler's. The edge fixture of `SelfhostDefaultT10Tests` has the same catch in `total` and passes, since it compares C text and does not compile it. Not fixed (outside T10's files). Status: open; for the C# lowerer (a variant catch over a set it covers should drop the propagation, or the binder should report).
1101. **017 P2: where `BoundNode.Syntax` is kept (Q1076 option 1, Q1096).** `selfhost/semantics/bound.byn` keeps two tables. (1) `ExprSyntax` (T21's, `c.exprSyntaxNodes`/`c.exprSyntaxOf`) is the `Syntax` that is an `Expr`; P2 adds the facts its consumers read: `binaryOp` and `right` (the right operand's span) for a `BinaryExpr`, `literalKind` and `suffix` for a `LiteralExpr` (`syntaxOfLiteral`), and `becauseKeyword` for a `CallExpr` with `because` (`because` is a keyword, so the field cannot take that name). (2) `NodeSyntax` (`c.nodeSyntaxNodes`/`c.nodeSyntaxOf`, ctx.byn's `// ── P2 state`) is the `Syntax` that is not an `Expr`: a `NodeSyntaxKind` (the 24 `Stmt` records, the 12 `Pattern` records, then `RequiresRule`, `GlobalStatement`, `FunctionDecl`, `StructDecl`, `Name`, `Param`, `Argument`, the types the corpus shows), its span, and for an `AssignStmt` the operator, target span and value span, for a `ReturnStmt` the value span. "Came from the parser or the binder" is the kind: a statement whose `Syntax` is not a `Stmt` record was made by the binder (`bindChecks` records `structDecl`, `bindMain` `globalStatement`, a missing body `functionDecl`). Each node records its `Syntax` where it is built (`recordNodeSyntax`, `recordAssignSyntax`, `recordReturnSyntax`, `recordStmtSyntax`, `recordPatternSyntax`), in binder*.byn, calls*.byn, states.byn and errorcases.byn; `shareSyntax` copies both tables. `bindUnionPattern`, `bindWholeVariant` and `bindErrorSetPattern` take the `NodeSyntax` in place of its span, as their C# take `p`; a `move` argument's `BMove` records `argument` through `recordMoveSyntax` (calls2.byn), which `bindMove` reaches with syntax -1 (BinderCalls.cs:540 passes `arg`). The emitter and `features` do not read the tables yet (T2, T10).
1102. **017 P2: the literal suffix is a span.** C# `LiteralExpr.Suffix` is a token; `ExprSyntax.suffix` keeps its span (`TextSpan?`), and its text is the file's bytes at that span, as every other selfhost name is read (`t15Text`). The test compares the span. No consumer reads the suffix's text without its file, so no string is stored.
1103. **017 P2: `withFile` (Compilation.cs:129-140, 212).** `compile.byn` `withFile(in c, from: in text)` compiles again through `t2Create`, C#'s private `Create` overload; public `create` calls it with no replacements. ctx.byn's P2 state keeps C#'s `Options` and `_entryFiles` (copies, `t2CopyOptions`, `t2CopySource`) and `_replaced` as `Map<string, lexer.SourceText>` (review 1 ruling 1): `withFile` copies it and sets `replaced[text.path]` (Compilation.cs:131-132), and `loadModule`'s import branch looks the path up by key (Compilation.cs:212, `GetValueOrDefault`). Bayan neither copies a map whose values are unique (`map.copy` is BYN `CopyUniqueElement`, BinderCalls.cs:845-852) nor iterates one (`for (k, _) in m` copies each value, BYN2780), so ctx.byn also keeps `replacedPaths`, the map's keys in insertion order, which `withFile` walks to copy each entry by key; it is never read for a lookup. The parameter is `through` because every labelled parameter needs a particle (BYN5008).

the imported `sub/sub.byn` gains a field, looked up past the replaced `main.byn`; `main.byn` reads the new field, which needs the second step's text; a path the program does not read), each step's diagnostics and bound-node lines equal `Compilation.WithFile`'s. 1106. **017 T6: the walk without link metadata (plan D7).** `walk.byn` ports `Format.cs:119` (`BynFiles`) whole except two things no builtin can do. (a) `realPath` (walk.byn:42) is `Path.fullPath`: the C# `RealPath` (`Format.cs:193-224`) resolves every symlink component by component and throws "Too many levels of symbolic links"; no builtin reports a link target or resolves a path, so no link is resolved and a link cycle is stopped only by `seenDirs` on the unresolved path. A cycle `up -> ..` is a new path each time until the path gets too long to list, so the walk ends (the probe gave 33 repeated `d/up/d/up/.../a.byn` lines and `◆ 33 bypasses` where the C# gives 1). `AuditWalksSymlinkCyclesOnce` (CliTests.cs:146) and `AuditWalksASymlinkToAParentOfTheRootOnce` (CliTests.cs:158) therefore differ from the C# and are listed skips in `SelfhostDriverT1Tests.AuditReportsALoopingFileLinkAsCliApp`'s summary, with the M3 symlink-outward row (CliMemoryBoundsTests.cs:162-200). Closing them needs a builtin (a real path, or a link target); the dispatcher decides. A dangling link `broken.byn -> /nonexistent` is reported by both, with exit 1, by different routes: the C# lists it as a file and fails to read it (`bayan: .../broken.byn: Could not find file ...`); the driver takes it for a directory, `Fs.fileExists` being false, and fails to list it (`The file does not exist.`, the message text differing as above); `AuditReportsADanglingLinkAsCliApp` compares exit, stdout and stderr up to the path. `AuditReportsALoopingFileLinkAsCliApp` ports CliTests.cs:172 `AuditReportsALoopingFileLinkAndGoesOn` (`loop.byn -> loop.byn` is a file by `Fs.fileExists`, reported when read, the walk goes on). (b) The `within` bound's `DirectoryInfo.LinkTarget is not null` refusal (`Format.cs:168`) is the marked comment walk.byn:84. Also: `GetFiles`/`GetDirectories` become one `Io.listDir` (sorted by byte order, where .NET's order is unspecified; `audit` sorts, `format` does not need it); an entry is a file when it ends in `.byn` and `Fs.fileExists` is true, and a directory otherwise (so an unreadable directory is entered and reported, as the C#); `.byn` matches case-insensitively (ASCII letters) on macOS and Windows and case-sensitively elsewhere (`t6IsByn`, walk.byn:31, as .NET's `GetFiles` pattern; the row `uppercase`; its Linux branch runs only on Linux, so it carries `coverage-exempt: Q1106` as Q1083's per-OS branches do); the IO message is the `IoError` where the C# prints `e.Message` (`Format.cs:129`), so the IO rows compare stderr up to `bayan: <path>: `; the "directory ends in a separator" test of `within` accepts `/` or `\` on Windows and `/` elsewhere, as `Path.EndsInDirectorySeparator` does (`Format.cs:121`) (its Windows operands, walk.byn:23, run only on Windows and carry `coverage-exempt: Q1106`); `bynFiles` takes `silent` for the `TextWriter.Null` of `PackageNames`, and `exit` as `through ref i32`. `SelfhostDriverT1Tests.WalkAsFormatBynFiles` runs `bynFiles` through `RunProbe` against `Format.BynFiles` with no bound, the root, a subdirectory, a subdirectory with a trailing separator, a bound that holds nothing, `silent`, and an unreadable directory. The lines no input reaches carry `coverage-exempt: Q1106`: a repeated canonical directory or a repeated real file, both needing a resolved link.
1107. **017 T6: `manifestFor` and `packageNames`.** Both bodies are ported in full. `ManifestFor` is `Format.cs:230` (walk.byn:113). `PackageNames` is `Format.cs:255` (walk.byn:136). `manifestFor` walks up from the directory of the full path, fills and reads `cache`, and tests `Fs.fileExists` of each `package.byn`; `packageNames` takes the `realPath` of `dir`, lists `bynFiles(dir, ..., by: root, for: true)`, skips `package.byn`, reads each file and goes on when it cannot (the `RealPath` catch has no Bayan counterpart, `realPath` not failing). The C# `Dictionary<string, (Manifest, string)?>` is the parameter `through ref Map<string, T6Found?> cache`, owned by the caller as `Format.Run` owns it (so `dctx.byn` keeps no T6 state), the tuple is `T6Found { manifest, dir }`, and the `HashSet<string>` is a `Map<string, bool>` (Bayan has no set). Only the two sibling calls are stubs: `Manifest.Read` is `t6ManifestRead` (walk.byn:104), which returns `T6Manifest { path }` because `Manifest` and `manifestRead` are not `public` in `selfhost/semantics/manifest.byn` (:36, :102), a file T6 does not own, and `OtherUses` (`Format.cs:406`) is `t6OtherUses` (walk.byn), T8's, which returns no names; it takes the parsed tree as the C# does, `packageNames` doing the `SyntaxTree.Parse` of `Format.cs:274` itself (the selfhost lexer and `parseCompilationUnit`), so only `OtherUses` is stubbed. T8 replaces both stubs, which needs `public` on `Manifest` and `manifestRead`. The one line that runs only with a real `OtherUses` (the loop body in `packageNames`) carries `coverage-blocked: Q1107 T8 otherUses`. `ManifestForAsFormat` compares the directory found for each of five files and the cache size against the private `Format.ManifestFor` by reflection (the manifest itself is not compared); `PackageNamesAsFormat` compares `packageNames` against `Format.PackageNames` where the C# set is empty (files holding only a comment, an unreadable file, a missing directory). Neither is called by `audit`.
1108. **017 T6: `audit` and what it borrows.** `selfhost/driver/audit.byn` ports `Audit.cs:1-110` in order (`auditCommand`, `t6Bypasses`, `t6Construct`, the records as `T6Bypass`/`T6Construct`); the tokens come from `lexer.lex` (public already, so `selfhost/lexer/main.byn` is untouched) and the text and positions from `SourceText.getText` and `getLinePosition`. `Role.Warning` has no case in doctor.byn `T5Role`, so `t6PaintWarning` (audit.byn:24, `\e[33m` under `--color always`, the Ansi16 palette of Q919) is a private copy for T28 to merge with `t5Paint`; Note and Success go through `t5Paint`. The path test is `Directory.Exists` then `File.Exists` (`Audit.cs:26-27`): `Fs.fileExists` (stat-based, true for an existing non-directory whether or not it can be read) for the file, and `t6DirectoryExists` (audit.byn:31) for the directory. No builtin tests that a directory exists, so `t6DirectoryExists` is `Io.listDir` succeeding or failing with `permissionDenied`, the closest match to `Directory.Exists` on a mode-000 directory (the C# then reports the IO error and exits 1 with `0 bypasses`, as the rows `locked-root-dir` and `locked-root-file` check); it also answers true for a path whose parent cannot be searched, where `Directory.Exists` is false. The earlier `t3DirectoryExists` and `t1FileExists` test that a path lists or reads, and gave `not found` and exit 2 on a mode-000 path. The rows of `SelfhostDriverT2Tests.RefusesTheOtherCommands` (:164) and `SelfhostDefaultT4Tests.StillRefusesTheCommandsOfTheOtherTasks` (:263) listed `audit` as refused; the `audit` rows were removed from both and from `RefusesWhatItDoesNotPort` in SelfhostDriverTests.cs. The `tests/cases/style/audit.*` shape is compared by StyleTests against the C#; its input is the `bypasses` row's shape (`AuditAsCliApp` `color` and `ascii` rows compare the same command with `--color always` and `--ascii` against `CliApp.Run`).

1111. **017 T9: the cache needs a rename and an executable copy (decision needed; blocks T9's done criterion).** No builtin moves a file or a directory or sets a file mode: `src/Bayan.Semantics/Builtins.cs` has `Io.readFile/readText/writeFile/remove/createDirectory/removeDirectory/listDir/run`, and `src/runtime/bayan-rt.c` calls no `rename` or `chmod`. Toolchain.cs needs both: `TagCacheDirectory` (:80 `File.Move(temp, tag, overwrite: false)`), `ReplaceFile` (:273 `File.Move(temp, path, overwrite: true)`), `Compile` (:341 `Directory.Move(work, programs/<key>)`, the step that makes a staged build an entry), `Discard` (:449 `Directory.Move(dir, trash)`) and `RememberScript` (:485). The cache hit copies the cached executable to the output (:254 `File.Copy`, which keeps the mode); `Io.writeFile` creates a file without the executable bit (Q1018 (j)), so a copied hit would not run. So these are stubs in cache.byn (`tagCacheDirectory`, `replaceFile`, `t9MoveAndDelete`, `t9Compile`, `rememberScript`, each `// stub: T9 … (blocked: Q1111)`), and build.byn is unchanged: no lookup before `cc.byn` compiles, and the staging stays `.bayan-staging-*` beside the output (docs/memory-leaks.md:77 stays open). `t9Compile` has `Compile`'s signature and fails `.unsupported` (cache.byn:273 `fail .unsupported`, under `coverage-exempt: Q1111`; it has no caller) rather than return the null that means success. `discard` is ported up to the move: `Directory.CreateDirectory(Staging)` (:448) is `Io.createDirectory`, a permission error fails `lookup` as the C#'s uncaught `UnauthorizedAccessException` (tested with `v1/` and `programs/` at 0555) and any other error returns as its `catch (IOException)` (tested with `v1/tmp` a file); then it calls the `t9MoveAndDelete` stub for `Directory.Move(dir, trash)` and `Directory.Delete(trash, recursive: true)` (:449-450), whose `trash-<Guid>` name also has no builtin (no `Guid.NewGuid`). What the stub changes, against the C#: (1) the damaged entry stays in `programs/<key>` where the C# removes it, so a second lookup of the key finds it again and discards again (`lookup` still returns null both times; `LookupAsToolchain` compares only the result, `badsum`/`noexe`/`nosum`/`badutf8`/`stagingfile`); (2) when `Staging` can be created but `Directory.Move` would fail with a permission error (`programs/` or the entry not writable while `v1/` is), the C# throws `UnauthorizedAccessException` out of `Lookup` and the driver returns null (no test; that row waits for the move); (3) nothing is ever left in `Staging`. `lookupScript` calls the `tagCacheDirectory` stub, so no `CACHEDIR.TAG` is written on a hit. Options: (a) an A1 exception as Q1042 (a): land `Io.move(string from, to string to, overwrite: bool)` over `rename(2)`/`MoveFileExW` and `Io.copyFile` keeping the mode (or a mode setter), then T9 ports the stubs and build.byn; (b) keep the builtins and `run`/`build` without a cache (R2 not met for the cache); (c) a non-atomic `Io.writeFile` in place of each move (readers can see partial entries, which Toolchain.cs:26-28 rules out; still no executable bit on a hit). Recommended: (a). Open.
1112. **017 T9: write times (plan D7; decision needed).** No builtin reads or sets a write time. `Touch` (Toolchain.cs:363 `SetLastWriteTimeUtc`), `Evict` (:384 orders by `LastWriteTimeUtc`, :392 keeps entries used within 10 minutes), `SweepStale` (:434 `GetLastWriteTimeUtc` against the cutoff) and `ComputeCompilerBuild` (:514 size and `LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks` of `Environment.ProcessPath`, which also has no builtin) cannot be ported, so `touch`, `evict`, `evictWith` (the `Evict(keep, maxBytes, maxEntries, minAge)` overload, :379), `sweepOnce` (:407), `sweepStale` and `compilerBuild` in cache.byn are stubs (`// stub: T9 … (blocked: Q1112)`; `compilerBuild` returns `CompilerVersion` without the file parts at cache.byn:353 `return version`, under `coverage-exempt: Q1112`); `s_swept` (:404) waits with `sweepOnce`, so the `// ── T9 state` section of dctx.byn holds no field yet. `scriptKey` takes `build` as the C#'s optional parameter (:498) and calls `compilerBuild()` only for null; the tests pass a build string to both sides. `evict` has the `Evict(keep)` signature (:372); the `BAYAN_CACHE_MAX_MB`/2 GiB/4000 arms wait with it. Rows blocked here and by Q1111: the `CacheTests.cs` argv rows (hit, miss, `--verbose` cache line, unwritable `BAYAN_CACHE`, `BAYAN_CACHE_MAX_MB`), `CliMemoryBoundsTests.cs` M5/M6 and F13; none is in `SelfhostDefaultT9Tests` yet (each needs the driver's `build`/`run` to go through the cache, which needs Q1111 (a)). Options: (a) land `Io.lastWriteTime(path) -> i64` and `Io.setLastWriteTime(path, i64)` (and `Io.processPath`) with Q1111 (a); (b) evict in name order with no in-use window (not the C#'s LRU, and it can remove an entry a concurrent build is running); (c) leave eviction out (the cache grows without bound, M5 fails). Recommended: (a). Open.

Targets.Host`; the `BuildMode` names come from `t9ModeName`), `lookup` (:289), `t9Intact` (the `File.ReadAllText(sum).Trim() == HashFile(exe)` of :297 split out so that a permission error fails as the C#'s uncaught `UnauthorizedAccessException` and any other `IoError` counts as damage, as its `catch (IOException)`), `t9ReadTrimmed` (`File.ReadAllText(path).Trim()` for `program.sha256` and the scripts pointer: a leading U+FEFF is dropped as `ReadAllText`'s BOM detection does, then `trimmed(by:)` with the 25 `char.IsWhiteSpace` code points of `t9Whitespace`, since `trimmed()` is ASCII only, bayan-rt.c:585), `t9DirectoryExists` (`Directory.Exists` of :294), `discard` up to the move (:443, Q1111), `lookupScript` (:462), `scriptKey` (:498), `t9Hash` (:556) and `t9HashFile` (:558, which reads the whole file). `lookup` and `lookupScript` test existence with `Fs.fileExists`, not main.byn `t1FileExists`, which is false for a file it cannot read. 1116. **017 T7: the progress timer without a thread.** Progress.cs draws from a `Timer` after 300 ms and every 250 ms. The language has no thread, so progress.byn reads `Io.monotonicNanos()` in `start` (progress.byn:90 `Progress start(in DStyle style, by bool isTty, through bool json, for string phase, i64 after = progressThreshold) uses alloc, clock, console, env`) and `done` (progress.byn:112 `void done(ref Progress p) uses alloc, clock, console {`) draws the frames the timer would have drawn by then (one at `after`, one per interval; an ASCII line once) before it clears the line; `after <= 0` draws at once (progress.byn:96 `if after <= 0 { tick(ref p) }`). A line is therefore written when the operation ends, not while it runs; for a stderr that only the line itself touches the bytes are the same, and `TheTimerDrawsAsProgressDoes` compares them with a `Progress.Start` timer over a `StringWriter` (1 and 2 frames, ASCII, below the threshold). The `Compile` site is ported: build.byn:162 `semantics.Ctx t5Compile(in T5Options o, by in semantics.T26Symbols symbols, to ref List<semantics.T26Reported> reported, through ref bool ok, bool includeTests = false, bool ascii = false, i64 width = 100, bool isTty = false) uses alloc, clock, console, env, fs {` starts it (CliApp.cs:264) and clears it before the report of the `--package` and path branches (CliApp.cs:300). `buildCommand` and `runProgram` pass the stderr style and tty; `checkCommand` and `diagCommand` (commands.byn) and `featuresCommand` (features.byn) call `t5Compile` without them, so those draw no line, and commands.byn and features.byn are not in T7's files list. Blocked (blocked: Q1116): CliApp.cs:272 and :279 clear the line before the manifest diagnostics and the no-entry message, which `semantics/cli.byn` `t26Compile` prints, so on the project branch the driver clears it after them (build.byn:194 `done(ref progress)`). Nothing shows a line in a driver run anyway: `stderrTty` is always false (Q919, Q1117), so the `Compile` start and clear are covered by running `check` and `build` but no test can see them draw; the break-test removing build.byn:200 `done(ref progress)` fails no test for that reason. The `ProgressTests.cs` rows with stderr a terminal are a listed skip (SelfhostDriverTests.cs, beside `TheTimerDrawsAsProgressDoes`): the law runs without a tty, and `start` is called with `by: true` directly in the progress probe. Break-test: progress.byn:118 `let owed = 1 + (elapsed - p.after) / progressInterval - p.frame` without the `1 +` failed `TheTimerDrawsAsProgressDoes` (two rows); restored by `cp`.

1122. **017 T8: `WriteReplacing` and what the rows skip.** selfhost/driver/format.byn:143 `stub: T8` marks `writeReplacing` as blocked by Q1111: its body selfhost/driver/format.byn:145 `try Io.writeFile(file, bytes.span)` writes in place, where Format.cs:284-298 writes a temp file beside the target, copies the Unix mode and renames it over (no builtin renames a file or reads or sets a mode). - **2026-10-23 — Spec 006 re-review fixes (C–G) and merge.** Region analysis now tracks borrows of `this` fields, `dyn ref` for-variables, element writes and by-value element arguments (C1–C4). It also tracks borrows of `ref`/`out`/`in` arguments by calls returning a span or `dyn ref`, a `ref this` call that structurally changes a borrowed field (a bodiless callee changes every field), `ref items` while borrowed, loops over a `this` List field, and span `dyn ref` loops (E1–E5). `for dyn ref` mutates element slots. A `unique` field cannot witness a getter (BYN2780), and a `unique` `Item` under a constraint is reported at instantiation (D1–D3). A `for dyn ref` loop that mutates elements is a write to the array: it is BYN2104 on `let`, and BYN2311 no longer fires on `var` (F). Before this fix, the `let` form compiled and mutated the array. `move` and `.take()` while a span or `dyn ref` still borrows the value is the new error BYN3006 "moved while borrowed" (G1, the review's B5 hole). A borrow's loan now starts where the expression first lends the owner, not at the end of the initializer, so `first(w.items.asSpan(), w.grow())` is BYN3004 (G2). I: place-ness by shape; a `dyn ref` result keeps its ref arguments' regions (BYN3002); writable `dyn ref` arguments count as writes. J: span-index, `with`, `try` and `catch` places; `this` outlives the method body; passing or calling through a writable `dyn ref` value mutates its owners. - **2026-11-06 — fix/runtime-security: runtime audit fixes.** From `docs/security/2026-11-06-runtime-audit.md`. `byn_arena_take` panics "arena allocation is too large" before rounding when `n < 0` or `n > INT64_MAX - 15 - sizeof(byn_chunk)`, and its room and doubling checks cannot overflow (`run/memory-arena-repeated-too-large`, `run/memory-arena-padded-too-large`, both compilers). Map and `Symbol` hashing is SipHash-1-3 keyed by 128 bits (`byn_hash_seed`, `byn_hash_seed_hi`) from `arc4random_buf` (macOS/BSD), `getrandom` (Linux) or `BCryptGenRandom` (Windows, looked up from System32 `bcrypt.dll` with `LoadLibraryExW`/`GetProcAddress` so no link flag changes); the key is zero under `--test`; `byn_hash_mix` is SipHash over the 16 bytes of both parts; no golden output changed; `SipHashTests` checks Rust's `test_siphash_1_3` vectors. `byn_slice_range` rejects `^n` and `^end` outside `0..len` and an inclusive end of `i64.max` before computing (`run/slice-from-end-min`, `run/slice-inclusive-max`; the goldens passed before the fix too, since `-fwrapv` wrapped into the slice check, so the break-test was UBSan on the old header: two signed-overflow reports, none after). `replaced`, `joined` and `byn_list_reserve` use `__builtin_*_overflow` and panic "... is too long" (`RuntimeSizeOverflowTests`, a C harness). `libc-uses.txt` drops `getpid`/`GetCurrentProcessId`, adds `GetProcAddress`, `LoadLibraryExW`, `arc4random_buf`, `getrandom`; `011-c-inventory.md` gains rows for the five new `__builtin_*_overflow` calls. Stdin is done (user, 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07): `Io.stdin.readAll()` fails with `invalidUtf8` on bytes that are not UTF-8 (`byn_io_read_stdin` checks `byn_utf8_valid`; `run/io-stdin-invalid-utf8`), and the new `Io.stdin.readAllBytes()` returns `Result<List<u8>, IoError>` unchecked (`byn_io_read_stdin_bytes`; `run/io-stdin-bytes`), which the selfhost lexer, parser and `bayan lex -` now read; `BYN_RUNTIME_VERSION` is 2. Out of scope items are `work/todo.md` lines.
